# @kirana-ui/vue

> Kirana UI Primitives for Vue: headless, accessible components with no styles of their own. The same components, parts, attributes and behaviour as on the other four frameworks, from one core.

Generated from the library's own source (`bun scripts/llms.ts`), and checked against it: every part and every prop here is in the package, and what is not here is not. In order: installing it and its entries; the positioner's options; the types the props name; what else is exported; the agent bridge; the testing kit; then "Using it" (the rules of every component) and "Components" (each one's parts, props, attributes and CSS variables).

This file describes the version it ships with. What changed in each release, the breaking changes first with what to write instead, is `CHANGELOG.md` in the package: `node_modules/@kirana-ui/vue/CHANGELOG.md`.

## Install and entries

Install `@kirana-ui/vue`. It is enough: the core it is built on comes with it, and what the core gives an application is also an entry of this package (`@kirana-ui/vue/agent`, `@kirana-ui/vue/testing`), so nothing is imported from a package the project did not install. The one exception is a component of your own, built on `@kirana-ui/core/authoring`: its controller imports the core by name, so that project installs `@kirana-ui/core` too, at this package's exact version (they must be one copy). It runs on the project's own `vue` ^3.5.0.

Its entries: an entry per component (`@kirana-ui/vue/tabs`, 59 of them, each named under its component below), the package root `@kirana-ui/vue` (every component at once, for a bundler that shakes trees), and `@kirana-ui/vue/runtime`, `@kirana-ui/vue/agent`, `@kirana-ui/vue/testing`, `@kirana-ui/vue/primitive` and `@kirana-ui/vue/direction`. No other path is an entry: `DirectionProvider` and `useDirection` are in `@kirana-ui/vue/direction`, `PortalProvider` in the package root.

The attributes and CSS variables below are also data and typed selectors, for a design system: install `@kirana-ui/vocabulary` for them (`import { vocabulary } from "@kirana-ui/vocabulary"`, `import { Dialog } from "@kirana-ui/vocabulary/keys"`: `Dialog.Popup.open` is `"[data-open]"`). It is its own package, and not installed with this one.

An agent's skill is in the package: `node_modules/@kirana-ui/vue/skills/kirana-ui-primitives/SKILL.md`.

## Positioner options

What every `Positioner` takes, beside its own props where a component's section lists any:

- `side?: Side`: The side of the anchor the popup is on. `inline-start` and `inline-end` follow the reading direction the popup is placed in, and `data-side` then says the side in the same words. Default `"bottom"`.
- `align?: Align`: Where along that side the popup is: at the anchor's start, its centre or its end. Default `"center"`.
- `sideOffset?: number | OffsetFunction`: The gap between the anchor and the popup, measured without any arrow: a number of pixels, or a function of what was measured (`({ side, align, anchor, positioner }) => number`). Default `0`.
- `alignOffset?: number | OffsetFunction`: How far the popup is moved along the side from where `align` puts it: a number of pixels, or a function of what was measured (`({ side, align, anchor, positioner }) => number`). Default `0`.
- `collisionPadding?: CollisionPadding`: Kept between the popup and the edges it is held inside: one number, or one for each side (`{ top, right, bottom, left }`, a side left out is 0). Default `5`.
- `collisionBoundary?: CollisionBoundary`: What the popup is held inside: an element, several, or a rectangle of the viewport. Left out or `"clipping-ancestors"`: the ancestors that clip it, and the viewport.
- `collisionAvoidance?: CollisionAvoidance`: What the popup does when it does not fit: `side` and `align` each `"flip"`, `"shift"` or `"none"`, and `fallbackAxisSide`. Left out: it flips to the opposite side and is moved along its side.
- `sticky?: boolean`: Keeps the popup in view once its anchor has been scrolled out of it. Otherwise the popup leaves with its anchor. Default `false`.
- `arrowPadding?: number`: Kept between an arrow and the ends of the popup's edge, so the arrow does not stand on a rounded corner. Default `5`.
- `positionMethod?: "absolute" | "fixed"`: The CSS `position` the positioner is given: `"absolute"` or `"fixed"`. Default `"absolute"`.
- `anchor?: PositionerAnchor`: What the popup is placed against, when that is not its trigger. It may change while the popup is open: the popup follows.

A component's own defaults lie over those: `Autocomplete` `{ align: "start" }`; `Combobox` `{ align: "start" }`; `ContextMenu` `{ align: "start" }`, and `{ side: "inline-end", align: "start" }` for a submenu or for a menu in a vertical menubar; `HoverCard` `{ side: "top" }`; `Menu` `{ align: "start" }`, and `{ side: "inline-end", align: "start" }` for a submenu or for a menu in a vertical menubar; `NavigationMenu` `{ align: "start" }`; `Select` `{ align: "start" }`; `Tooltip` `{ side: "top" }`; `Tour` the shared defaults, under the `side` and `align` of the step shown; a step with no target is placed in the middle of the viewport whatever they say.

## Types

The named types the props below mention, each with the entry of this package it is imported from: `import type { ChangeDetails, Side } from "@kirana-ui/vue"`. The core's own types are re-exported there, as types only, so nothing is imported from `@kirana-ui/core`, which a strict installer keeps out of a project's reach. A capital alone (`Value`) in a part's props is that part's own type parameter, said on the part's line.

- `Align` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `"start" | "center" | "end"`. Where along its side a popup is: at the anchor's start, its centre or its end.
- `Anchor` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `Element | VirtualElement`. What a popup is placed against: an element, or a place in the viewport that is none.
- `CalendarDay` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): A day in the grid of a month shown.
    - `date: IsoDate`
    - `label: string`: The day of the month as the locale writes it.
    - `outside: boolean`: Not of the month it is drawn in: the days that fill its first and last weeks.
- `CalendarMonth` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): One of the months shown, as `Calendar.Months` gives it.
    - `index: number`: Its place among the months shown, from 0.
    - `month: IsoDate`: Its first day.
    - `title: string`: Its name as the locale writes it (`"March 2026"`).
    - `weekdays: readonly CalendarWeekday[]`
    - `weeks: readonly (readonly CalendarDay[])[]`
- `CalendarValueOf<Mode extends CalendarMode | undefined>` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `Mode extends "range" ? DateRange | null : Mode extends "multiple" ? readonly IsoDate[] : IsoDate | null`. The value of one mode: a day or `null`, a range or `null`, or a list (empty for none). What `value` and `onValueChange` are typed by, from the `mode` a root is given.
- `CalendarWeekday` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): A day of the week, as a column's heading names it.
    - `index: number`: Its place in the week as the locale orders it, from 0.
    - `narrow: string`: Its name as a column's heading (`"M"`, `"Mo"`), and in full (`"Monday"`).
    - `short: string`
    - `long: string`
- `ChangeDetails` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): What a change callback is given beside the value: why it changed, what made it, and a way to refuse it.
    - `reason: string`: Why the value changed: `"trigger-press"`, `"outside-press"`, `"escape-key"`, `"item-press"` …
    - `event: Event | undefined`: The DOM event behind it, when there is one.
    - `source: ChangeSource`: What made it: a mouse, a finger, a pen, the keyboard, something that presses without a pointer (a screen reader, `element.click()`), code with no event at all, or an agent acting through the bridge (`@kirana-ui/core/agent`).
    - `cancel(): void`: Keeps the value as it was.
    - `canceled: boolean`
- `Changes<Name extends string, Value, Details = ChangeDetails>` (`@kirana-ui/vue/runtime`): `{ [Event in `update:${Name}`]: (value: Value) => void } & { [Event in `${Name}Change`]: (value: Value, details: Details) => void }`. The two events of a value its caller may hold: `update:open`, which `v-model:open` hears, and `openChange`, which also carries the details and may cancel the change.
- `ChangeSource` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `"mouse" | "touch" | "pen" | "keyboard" | "virtual" | "programmatic" | "agent"`. What made a change: a kind of pointer, the keyboard, a press with no pointer (`virtual`), code with no event (`programmatic`), or an agent acting through the bridge.
- `CollisionAvoidance` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): What a popup does when it does not fit where it was asked to be.
    - `side?: "flip" | "shift" | "none"`: Across from the anchor: `"flip"` goes to the opposite side, `"shift"` keeps the side and moves over the anchor to stay in view, `"none"` lets it overflow. Default `"flip"`.
    - `align?: "flip" | "shift" | "none"`: Along its side: `"flip"` swaps `start` and `end`, `"shift"` moves the popup along the side to stay in view, `"none"` lets it overflow. Default `"flip"`. With `side: "shift"` it is `"shift"` or `"none"`.
    - `fallbackAxisSide?: "start" | "end" | "none"`: Where it goes when neither the side asked for nor its opposite fits: to the other axis, its `"start"` or its `"end"` first, or nowhere (`"none"`). Default `"end"`.
- `CollisionBoundary` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `"clipping-ancestors" | Element | Element[] | { x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number }`. What a popup is held inside: the ancestors that clip it (`"clipping-ancestors"`), an element, several, or a rectangle of the viewport.
- `CollisionPadding` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `number | Partial<Record<PhysicalSide, number>>`. The room kept between a popup and the edges it is held inside: one number, or one a side.
- `ColorFormat` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `"hex" | "rgb" | "hsl"`. How a colour is written: `#rrggbb`, `rgb(…)` or `hsl(…)`.
- `ColorPickerInputChannel` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `"hex" | "red" | "green" | "blue" | "hue" | "saturation" | "lightness" | "alpha"`. A channel an input of the picker is typed in.
- `ColorPickerSliderChannel` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `"hue" | "alpha"`. A channel a slider of the picker moves: the hue, or the alpha.
- `ColorPickerThumb` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `"area" | ColorPickerSliderChannel`. What a thumb of the picker moves: the area's, or a slider's channel.
- `ComboboxEntry<Value = unknown>` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `ComboboxItemEntry<Value> | ComboboxGroupEntry<Value>`. What a `Collection` hands to be drawn: an item that is left, or a group that has items left.
- `ComboboxGroupData<Value = unknown>` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): Items given as data that belong together: `value` is the group's name.
    - `value: string`
    - `items: readonly ComboboxItemData<Value>[]`
- `ComboboxGroupEntry<Value = unknown>` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): A group that has items left, with those items.
    - `type: "group"`
    - `key: string`: What it is known by from one drawing to the next.
    - `value: string`: The group's name, as it was given.
    - `label: string`: The same name: an entry of either kind has a `label`.
    - `disabled: false`: Never: an entry of either kind says whether it is disabled.
    - `items: readonly ComboboxItemEntry<Value>[]`: The items of the group that are left.
- `ComboboxItemData<Value = unknown>` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): One item given as data: its value, and what it is called.
    - `value: Value`
    - `label: string`
    - `disabled?: boolean`: It cannot be chosen: its entry says so, for the item drawn for it.
- `ComboboxItemEntry<Value = unknown>` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): One item left of the `items` given as data, as a `Collection` hands it to be drawn.
    - `type: "item"`
    - `key: string`: What it is known by from one drawing to the next.
    - `value: Value`
    - `label: string`
    - `disabled: boolean`
    - `item: ComboboxItemData<Value>`: The item as it was given, with whatever else it carries.
- `DateFieldSegment` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): One piece of the field, in the locale's order: a part that is typed, or what stands between.
    - `type: DateUnit | "literal"`
    - `literal: string`: What stands between two parts (`"/"`); empty for a part that is typed.
    - `index: number`: Its place among the pieces.
- `DatePickerRange` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): A range a date picker holds: its first and its last day, either `null` while it is being chosen (the first picked, the second not yet; one end typed).
    - `start: IsoDate | null`
    - `end: IsoDate | null`
- `DatePickerValueOf<Mode extends DatePickerMode | undefined>` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `Mode extends "range" ? DatePickerRange | null : IsoDate | null`. The value of one mode: a day or `null`, or a range or `null`.
- `DateRange` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): A range of days, its first and its last, both in it.
    - `start: IsoDate`
    - `end: IsoDate`
- `DateUnit` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `"era" | "day" | "month" | "year"`. A part of a date that is typed on its own; the era only in a calendar that has several.
- `DrawerSide` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `"up" | "down" | "left" | "right"`. The way a drawer is swiped to close it: towards the edge it came from.
- `DrawerSnapPoint` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `number | string`. How much of a drawer shows at a place it rests: a share of it, or a length.
- `FieldValidity` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): What a field knows of its control's value once it has been checked.
    - `valid: boolean | null`: `null` until the value has been checked.
    - `errors: readonly string[]`: What is wrong, one message each.
    - `state: Readonly<Record<ValidityKey, boolean>>`: What the browser found, by name; `customError` is the field's own `validate`.
    - `value: string`: The value that was checked.
- `FileRejection` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): A file that was not taken, and every reason it was not.
    - `file: File`
    - `reasons: readonly FileRejectionReason[]`
- `FileRejectionReason` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `"type" | "too-large" | "too-small" | "too-many" | "invalid"`. Why a file was not taken.
- `FileUploadEntry` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): One file as it is drawn: the file, its place, and what tells it from the others.
    - `key: string`: The same for as long as the file is held: what a list keeps its element by.
    - `file: File`
    - `index: number`
- `FormErrors` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `Record<string, string | readonly string[]>`. A form's errors as a server sends them: each field's name with its message, or messages.
- `FormValues` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `Record<string, FormDataEntryValue | FormDataEntryValue[]>`. A form's values by field name, as `FormData` holds them: a list where a name is there more than once.
- `HourCycle` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `12 | 24`. A clock of twelve hours and a day period, or of twenty-four.
- `Hsva` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): Hue from 0 to 360, saturation and brightness (value) from 0 to 100, alpha from 0 to 1: what a colour area draws, saturation across and brightness up.
    - `h: number`
    - `s: number`
    - `v: number`
    - `a: number`
- `ImageStatus` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `"idle" | "loading" | "loaded" | "error"`. Where an avatar's picture is in its loading: `idle` while it has no address, `loading`, then `loaded` or `error`. Base UI's `ImageLoadingStatus`.
- `IsoDate` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `string`. A day as `YYYY-MM-DD`, in the calendar the world's data is kept in (ISO 8601).
- `IsoTime` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `string`. A time of day as `HH:MM` or `HH:MM:SS`, in 24 hours (ISO 8601).
- `ListCollection` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): Every row of a list of which only some are in the page: a virtualizer draws the ones in view. The keys then move by place, and ask for a row that is not drawn to be brought into the page.
    - `count: number`: How many rows there are, drawn or not.
    - `label?(index: number): string`: A row's name by its place: what typing matches. Without it, typing finds nothing.
    - `disabled?(index: number): boolean`
    - `indexOf?(value: unknown): number`: The place of a value, or -1: where a list opens on what is chosen.
    - `scrollToIndex(index: number): void`: Brings a row into the page: the virtualizer's own scroll.
- `OffsetData` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): What an offset given as a function is told: where the popup is, and the two sizes.
    - `side: Side`: The side of the anchor the popup is on, in the words it was asked for in.
    - `align: Align`: Where along that side the popup is.
    - `anchor: { width: number; height: number }`: The anchor's size, in pixels.
    - `positioner: { width: number; height: number }`: The positioner's size, in pixels.
- `OffsetFunction` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `(data: OffsetData) => number`. A gap worked out from what was measured: `({ side, align, anchor, positioner }) => number`.
- `Orientation` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `"horizontal" | "vertical"`. The way a row of things is laid out, and so which arrow keys move along it.
- `OtpValidation` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `"numeric" | "alpha" | "alphanumeric" | "none" | "alphabetic" | "text"`. Which characters a one-time code takes: Base UI's four values, and `alphabetic` and `text`, the older spellings of `alpha` and `none`.
- `PaginationEntry` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `{ readonly type: "page"; readonly page: number; readonly key: string } | { readonly type: "ellipsis"; readonly key: "start" | "end" }`. One piece of the list of pages: a page, or the mark for pages left out.
- `PhysicalSide` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `"top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left"`. A side of the anchor as the page is drawn.
- `PositionerAnchor` (`@kirana-ui/vue/popover`): `Anchor | ComponentPublicInstance | Ref<Anchor | ComponentPublicInstance | null | undefined> | (() => Anchor | null | undefined) | null | undefined`. What a positioner's `anchor` may be: an element, a place in the viewport (an object with `getBoundingClientRect`), a template ref to an element or a component (in a template that is the element or the component's instance), or a function that gives an element or a place.
- `Presentation` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `"popup" | "sheet" | "auto"`. How a list opens: `"popup"` placed against its trigger, `"sheet"` from the bottom edge of the viewport, `"auto"` a sheet on a narrow touch screen and a popup elsewhere.
- `QrCorrection` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `"L" | "M" | "Q" | "H"`. How much of the symbol may be lost and still be read: about 7, 15, 25 and 30 in a hundred.
- `ReadonlySignal<T>` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): A value that is read, and that tells when it changes.
    - `get(): T`: The value, tracked by the computed or effect that reads it.
    - `peek(): T`: The value, untracked.
    - `subscribe(listener: () => void): () => void`: Calls `listener` after each change (not at once). Returns the unsubscribe.
- `RootEmits` (`@kirana-ui/vue/menu`): `Changes<"open", boolean>`
- `RootValue<Value extends SliderValue = SliderValue>` (`@kirana-ui/vue/slider`): `SliderTold<Value>`. What comes back is what was given: a number for one thumb, a list for a range.
- `Side` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `PhysicalSide | "inline-start" | "inline-end"`. The side of its anchor a popup is on. `inline-start` and `inline-end` turn with the reading direction: `inline-end` is the right in English and the left in Arabic.
- `SliderChangeDetails` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): A slider's change details: the details of any change, and which thumb moved.
    - `index: number`: The thumb that moved.
    - `reason: string`: Why the value changed: `"trigger-press"`, `"outside-press"`, `"escape-key"`, `"item-press"` …
    - `event: Event | undefined`: The DOM event behind it, when there is one.
    - `source: ChangeSource`: What made it: a mouse, a finger, a pen, the keyboard, something that presses without a pointer (a screen reader, `element.click()`), code with no event at all, or an agent acting through the bridge (`@kirana-ui/core/agent`).
    - `cancel(): void`: Keeps the value as it was.
    - `canceled: boolean`
- `SliderTold<Value extends SliderValue = SliderValue>` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `Value extends number ? number : number[]`. What a slider tells of a value it was given as `Value`: a number for one thumb, a list for a range, and either where the caller's own type says either.
- `TagsInputEntry` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): One tag as it is drawn: its text, its place, and what tells it from the others.
    - `key: string`: The same for as long as the tag is there: what a list keeps its element by.
    - `value: string`
    - `index: number`
- `TimeFieldSegment` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): One piece of the field, in the locale's order: a part that is typed, or what stands between.
    - `type: TimeUnit | "literal"`
    - `literal: string`: What stands between two parts (`":"`); empty for a part that is typed.
    - `index: number`: Its place among the pieces.
- `TimeGranularity` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `"minute" | "second"`. The smallest part it is typed to.
- `TimeUnit` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `"hour" | "minute" | "second" | "dayPeriod"`. A part of a time that is typed on its own.
- `ToastActionOptions<Content = string>` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): A button a toast offers: what it says, and what pressing it does.
    - `label: Content`: What the button says: `Toast.Action` draws it when it is given nothing else. Needed.
    - `onAction(details: ChangeDetails): void`: Heard when the button is pressed, before the toast closes with the reason `"action-press"`: `details.cancel()` keeps the toast open. Needed.
- `Toaster<Content = string>` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): The toasts of a page and what changes them: what `createToaster()` gives.
    - `toasts: ReadonlySignal<readonly ToastRecord<Content>[]>`: Every toast that is in the page, the newest first. Empty to begin with.
    - `limit: number`: How many are shown at once; the rest wait behind. Default: `3`.
    - `add(options: ToastOptions<Content> & { id?: string }): string`: Shows a toast, and gives the id it is known by: `id` when one is given (the same id again is the same toast, changed), `toast-1`, `toast-2` … otherwise.
    - `update(id: string, options: ToastOptions<Content>): void`: Changes one that is showing: what is given replaces what it had, the rest stays, and its time starts again.
    - `dismiss(id?: string, details?: ChangeDetails): void`: Closes one, or every one when no id is given: it leaves once its motion has ended. `details` is what `onClose` hears. Default: the reason `"dismiss"`.
    - `remove(id: string): void`: Takes one out at once, with no exit: what draws the toasts calls it when the motion has ended.
    - `promise<Value>( promise: Promise<Value>, states: { loading: ToastState<Content> success: ToastState<Content> | ((value: Value) => ToastState<Content>) error: ToastState<Content> | ((error: unknown) => ToastState<Content>) } ): Promise<Value>`: One toast for something that takes time: `loading` (type `"loading"`, staying until the promise settles), then `success` or `error` in its place, each a title, a toast's options, or a function of what the promise gave. Each state is whole: a description or an action the state before had is not kept. Answers the promise itself.
- `ToastOptions<Content = string>` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): What a toast is added with. `Content` is what a title, a description and an action's label may be: a string here, and what the framework draws in each adapter's own `createToaster`. The toaster hands it on as it was given, and never reads it.
    - `title?: Content`: What the toast is called: `Toast.Title` draws it when it is given nothing else. Default: none.
    - `description?: Content`: What the toast says: `Toast.Description` draws it when it is given nothing else. Default: none.
    - `type?: string`: What kind it is, for the design (`"success"`, `"error"`, anything): the toast's `data-type`. Default: none.
    - `timeout?: number`: How long it stays, in milliseconds; `0` (or `Infinity`) until it is closed. Default: the toaster's `timeout`.
    - `duration?: number`: How long it stays, in milliseconds; `Infinity` until it is closed.
    - `priority?: "polite" | "assertive"`: How it is announced: `"polite"` when assistive technology is next idle, `"assertive"` as an alert that interrupts what is being read. Default: `"polite"`.
    - `action?: ToastActionOptions<Content>`: A button of the toast's own, which `Toast.Action` draws and presses. Default: none.
    - `data?: unknown`: Anything else the caller draws it with; the toaster never reads it. Default: none.
    - `onClose?: ((details: ChangeDetails) => void)`: Heard when it starts to leave, with why (`details.reason`). Default: none.
- `ToastRecord<Content = VNodeChild>` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): A toast as its toaster holds it: what it was added with, and where it stands.
    - `id: string`: What it is known by: the one it was added with, or one the toaster made.
    - `timeout: number`: How long it stays, in milliseconds: its own, or the toaster's when it gave none; `Infinity` until it is closed.
    - `duration: number`: How long it stays, in milliseconds.
    - `priority: "polite" | "assertive"`: How it is announced: its own, or `"polite"` when it gave none.
    - `closing: boolean`: It has been closed and is on its way out. `false` until then.
    - `title?: Content`: What the toast is called: `Toast.Title` draws it when it is given nothing else. Default: none.
    - `description?: Content`: What the toast says: `Toast.Description` draws it when it is given nothing else. Default: none.
    - `type?: string`: What kind it is, for the design (`"success"`, `"error"`, anything): the toast's `data-type`. Default: none.
    - `action?: ToastActionOptions<Content>`: A button of the toast's own, which `Toast.Action` draws and presses. Default: none.
    - `data?: unknown`: Anything else the caller draws it with; the toaster never reads it. Default: none.
    - `onClose?: ((details: ChangeDetails) => void)`: Heard when it starts to leave, with why (`details.reason`). Default: none.
- `ToastState<Content = string>` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `ToastOptions<Content> | (string extends Content ? string : never)`. What a promise's toast shows in one of its states: a toast's options, or a string, which is its title (where a title may be a string).
- `TreeSelectionMode` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `"none" | "single" | "multiple"`. Whether a tree's nodes can be chosen, and how many at once.
- `ValidationMode` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `"onSubmit" | "onBlur" | "onChange"`. When a field checks its value. Once it is found invalid, it checks on every change.
- `ValidityKey` (`@kirana-ui/vue`): `Exclude<keyof ValidityState, "valid">`. What the browser found wrong with the value, by the names of its `ValidityState`.

## Also exported

What the entries export beside the components, their parts' props types and the types above:

- `AnchorOption`, from `@kirana-ui/vue`: A positioner's own anchor: an element, a place in the viewport (`getBoundingClientRect`), or a function that gives one, asked each time the popup is placed. `null`, `undefined` or a function that gives neither: the popup's own anchor, its trigger.
- `Bindable`, from `@kirana-ui/vue`: A value that is the caller's while they give one and the part's own otherwise, as a signal that is asked to change.
- `CalendarMode`, from `@kirana-ui/vue`: How many days it chooses: one, a first and a last, or any number.
- `CalendarValue`, from `@kirana-ui/vue`: What a calendar holds: a day, a range of days in `mode: "range"`, a list of days in `mode: "multiple"`, or `null` for none.
- `ComboboxShown`, from `@kirana-ui/vue`: What a combobox's value part shows: what is chosen, and how it is named.
- `ComponentDefinition`, from `@kirana-ui/vue`: A component in the vocabulary: its parts by name.
- `DatePickerMode`, from `@kirana-ui/vue`: Whether a date picker chooses one day or a first and a last.
- `DatePickerValue`, from `@kirana-ui/vue`: What a date picker holds: a day, or in `mode: "range"` a range; `null` for none.
- `Direction`, from `@kirana-ui/vue`: The reading direction: left to right, or right to left.
- `ItemLabels`, from `@kirana-ui/vue`: The labels of a control's values, as its caller gives them: a list of values with their labels, or, for values that are text, the labels by value (`{ apple: "Apple" }`).
- `Part`, from `@kirana-ui/vue`: One part of a component as the core gives it: the props for its element, and the DOM work that starts once the element is in the page. Its props are the type `PartProps`, from the same entries.
- `PartDefinition`, from `@kirana-ui/vue`: A part of a component in the vocabulary: its states, its CSS variables, and where it goes.
- `PartState`, from `@kirana-ui/vue`: A part's state as its caller reads it: `true` for a flag, its value for a state that has one.
- `PartStyle`, from `@kirana-ui/vue`: A part's `style`: property names as CSS writes them (`width`, `--thumb-offset`).
- `PositionOptions`, from `@kirana-ui/vue`: How a popup is placed against its anchor: what every positioner takes.
- `SelectShown`, from `@kirana-ui/vue`: What a select's value part shows: what is chosen, and how it is named.
- `Signal`, from `@kirana-ui/vue`: A value that is read and written, and that tells when it changes.
- `StateDefinition`, from `@kirana-ui/vue`: A state of a part in the vocabulary: the attribute that marks it, and what it means.
- `StateOf`, from `@kirana-ui/vue`: The state of a part, from its definition in the vocabulary: a state its attribute marks by being present is `true` or absent, one with values is one of them or absent. It is what `stateOf` reads from the part's props.
- `TourStep`, from `@kirana-ui/vue`: One step of a tour. What it says is the page's to draw: the controller only shows it.
- `TourTarget`, from `@kirana-ui/vue`: What a step is about: an element, a CSS selector, or a function that gives an element, asked when the step is shown, so it may be something the page draws late.
- `calendarScope`, from `@kirana-ui/vue/calendar`: The calendar its parts are inside. Exported for a component that is made of one (a date picker provides its own to the calendar's parts).
- `dateFieldScope`, from `@kirana-ui/vue/date-field`: The date field its parts are inside. Exported for a component that is made of one (a date picker provides its own to the date field's parts).
- `DirectionProvider`, from `@kirana-ui/vue` or `@kirana-ui/vue/direction`: States the reading direction for the components inside. It draws nothing: set the page's own `dir` attribute with it.
- `useDirection()`, from `@kirana-ui/vue` or `@kirana-ui/vue/direction`: The direction the nearest provider states; `ltr` outside one.
- `useFieldset()`, from `@kirana-ui/vue/fieldset`: The fieldset a field is in, if it is in one.
- `useForm()`, from `@kirana-ui/vue/form`: The form a field is in, if it is in one.
- `hoverPopup(name: string, create: (props: ReadonlySignal<HoverPopupProps>) => HoverPopup, triggerTag: Tag)`, from `@kirana-ui/vue/tooltip` or `@kirana-ui/vue/hover-card`: The parts of a popup the pointer opens: a tooltip's, a hover card's. `States` is the state of each (`StatesOf<"tooltip">`), `Tag` the trigger's element.
- `popoverScope`, from `@kirana-ui/vue/popover`: The popover its parts are inside. Exported for a component that is made of one (a date picker provides its own to the popover's parts).
- `positionerComponent(name: string, use: () => { positioning: Controller["positioning"] }, element: Component)`, from `@kirana-ui/vue/popover`: A positioner: the part's element, with where it goes as props. The one place a positioner's own props are named.
- `Primitive`, from `@kirana-ui/vue/primitive`: A plain element of one's own (a badge, a breadcrumb's link) with the composition a part has: `as` for another tag or component (a `div` unless said), or with `as-child` the caller's own element in its slot. By a part's rule: the slotted element's own props lie over the attributes on the `Primitive`, classes join, styles are merged, and both listeners of an event run, the `Primitive`'s first.
- `PrimitiveGiven`, from `@kirana-ui/vue/primitive`: What a `Primitive` drawn as `Tag` takes: its two props, and what the element takes.
- `valueBar(name: string, create: (props: ReadonlySignal<ValueBarProps>) => ValueBar)`, from `@kirana-ui/vue/progress`: The parts of a value drawn as a filled track: a progress bar's, a meter's. `States` is the state of each (`StatesOf<"progress">`), `Value` what its value may be.
- `ValueGiven`, from `@kirana-ui/vue/slider` or `@kirana-ui/vue/progress`: What a bar's `Value` hands its slot beside its state.
- `createToaster(options?: Core.ToasterOptions)`, from `@kirana-ui/vue` or `@kirana-ui/vue/toast`: The toasts of a page, made once, in a module: `toaster.add({ title })` from anywhere. A title, a description and an action's label are what a render function returns, unless `Content` says otherwise.
- `ToastContent`, from `@kirana-ui/vue` or `@kirana-ui/vue/toast`: What a toast's title, description and action's label may be here: what a render function returns (a string, `h("b", "Saved")`, several of them).
- `ToasterOptions`, from `@kirana-ui/vue` or `@kirana-ui/vue/toast`: What a toaster is made with.
- `TourShownStep`, from `@kirana-ui/vue/tour`: What the popup's slot is told of the step it shows, beside its state, to draw it.
- `context(name: string)`, from `@kirana-ui/vue/runtime`: A controller its parts find: `provide` in the root, `use` in a part.
- `controller(create: (props: ReadonlySignal<P>) => C, read: () => P)`, from `@kirana-ui/vue/runtime`: A component's controller, made once, following its props.
- `DefaultSlot`, from `@kirana-ui/vue/runtime`: A component's default slot, given `Slot`.
- `ElementAttributes`, from `@kirana-ui/vue/runtime`: What the element of a tag takes, listeners included (`onClick` is `@click`, its event a `MouseEvent` with `preventKiranaHandler()`, which keeps the part's own listener out of it): Vue's own attributes for the tag, a plain element's for a tag Vue does not know, and any `data-*` attribute.
- `elementOf(instance: unknown)`, from `@kirana-ui/vue/runtime`: A component's instance as its element: its root, or with several roots the first element after the fragment's own mark.
- `fromSignal(source: ReadonlySignal<T>)`, from `@kirana-ui/vue/runtime`: A core signal as a Vue ref, read-only: tracked by whatever reads `.value`.
- `Hold`, from `@kirana-ui/vue/runtime`: What a part keeps in its element beside its content (a control's native input, a code cell's character, the text it writes): given the content, it returns what the element holds. `composed` says the element is the caller's own (`as-child`), and the content that element's.
- `Listeners`, from `@kirana-ui/vue/runtime`: A component's events as the listeners among its props: `openChange` is `onOpenChange`.
- `optional(type: T)`, from `@kirana-ui/vue/runtime`: A prop that is "not given" when absent, where Vue would make a boolean `false`.
- `partComponent(name: string, tag: Tag, resolve: () => Part, hold?: Hold)`, from `@kirana-ui/vue/runtime`: A part as a component: its element (`as`, the part's own tag by default), or with `as-child` the caller's own element in its slot, which takes the part's props, and the part's DOM work attached to the element. Three layers of props, lowest first: the attributes on the part, the slotted element's own, the part's. A higher layer wins an attribute; classes join; styles are merged; every listener of an event runs, lowest first, and `event.preventKiranaHandler()` in a caller's stops the part's. The default slot is given the part's state (`{ state }`: `open`, `side` …, read from its `data-*` attributes), typed by `State`. `hold` is for a part that keeps something of its own in its element (a hidden input, the text it writes: `written`): it is given the content and returns what the element holds, whoever drew the element.
- `PartComponent`, from `@kirana-ui/vue/runtime`: A part as its callers see it. `Tag` is the element it draws, and `as` another: the part takes the attributes and listeners of whichever it is. `State` is what its default slot is given as `state` (`StateOf` its entry in the vocabulary), with `Given` beside it when the part hands its slot more. `Props` are the part's own, `Emits` its events with their payloads. A part whose value has a type of its caller's (a root with `value`) writes the same signature out with that type as a parameter: `new <Value, As extends string = "div">(props: PartGiven<As, RootProps<Value>, RootEmits<Value>> & PublicProps) => PartInstance<…>`. Its props are the type `PartComponentProps`, from the same entries.
- `PartEvent`, from `@kirana-ui/vue` or `@kirana-ui/vue/runtime`: An event as a handler given to a part hears it.
- `PartGiven`, from `@kirana-ui/vue/runtime`: What a caller may hand a part drawn as `Tag`: the part's own props, a listener for each of its events, and what the element takes. A prop or an event of the part's that an attribute of the element shares a name with (`value`, `disabled`, `onSelect`) is the part's.
- `PartInstance`, from `@kirana-ui/vue/runtime`: A part's instance, as Vue's own tools read a component: its props, its events, its slot.
- `PlainComponent`, from `@kirana-ui/vue/runtime`: A component that draws no element of its own (a root that only provides, a portal, a list that draws its slot once for each entry): its props, its events, what its slot is given.
- `PlainInstance`, from `@kirana-ui/vue/runtime`: The instance of a `PlainComponent`, for one whose value has a type of its caller's.
- `portalComponent(name: string, mounted: () => ReadonlySignal<boolean>)`, from `@kirana-ui/vue/runtime`: Its slot in a container at the end of the page, while `mounted`.
- `PortalProps`, from `@kirana-ui/vue/runtime`: A portal takes nothing: where it is drawn is its `PortalProvider`'s to say.
- `PortalProvider`, from `@kirana-ui/vue` or `@kirana-ui/vue/runtime`: Says where every popup inside it is drawn, the popups those open included: an element of the page (a shadow root's host, a full-screen element) in place of `<body>`. Its props are the type `PortalProviderProps`, from the same entries.
- `StatesOf`, from `@kirana-ui/vue/runtime`: The state of each part of a component, by their names in the vocabulary: what a part's `data-*` attributes say, and what its default slot is given as `state`.
- `toSignal(read: () => T)`, from `@kirana-ui/vue/runtime`: A core signal that follows Vue state: the core hears a changed prop as it changes.
- `useDirectionAround()`, from `@kirana-ui/vue/runtime`: The reading direction a provider states, if a component is inside one.
- `written(text: () => unknown)`, from `@kirana-ui/vue/runtime`: What the element of a part that writes its own text holds: with `as-child`, the text while the caller's element has no content of its own, as the part's own element would.

## Agent

`import { createAgent } from "@kirana-ui/vue/agent"`: a bridge that lets an agent read and use a page built with these components, by the roles, states and names every part writes. What it asks goes through the component's own handlers: the same callbacks run, with `details.source === "agent"`, and may refuse.

`createAgent(options)` takes (`AgentOptions`):

- `root?: ParentNode`: The part of the page the agent may read and use. Default: the document.
- `allow?: ((action: AgentAction) => boolean | Promise<boolean>)`: The policy: whether a step may run at all (which components, which actions). Asked for every step, before `confirm`. Without it every step may. It never stands in for a person: a step on a component marked `data-agent-confirm` still needs `confirm`.
- `confirm?: ((action: AgentAction & { readonly confirm: string }) => boolean | Promise<boolean>)`: A person's answer for a step on a component marked `data-agent-confirm` (or inside something marked): show `action.confirm`, the mark's text, and resolve with what they chose. Without it such a step fails with "Needs a person", whatever `allow` says.
- `timeout?: number`: How long `allow` and `confirm` may take to answer, in milliseconds: after it the step fails with "No answer". Without it a step waits for as long as a person takes.
- `limit?: number`: How many components a snapshot lists before it says how many more there are. Default 200.
- `kinds?: readonly AgentKind[]`: Kinds of component of your own, matched before the ones the bridge knows.

and gives (`Agent`):

- `snapshot(): AgentComponent[]`: The components in the page now.
- `act(request: { steps: readonly AgentStep[]; signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<AgentResult>`: Runs steps in order, each through its component's own handlers. A `signal` that aborts stops it before its next step, and ends a wait for `allow` or `confirm`.
- `stage(request: { steps: readonly AgentStep[]; signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<AgentStaged>`: Runs steps as `act` does, to show a suggestion in the controls themselves: nothing joins `history()` until `keep()`, and `revert()` takes it all back.
- `query(request: { text?: string; within?: string; kind?: string }): Promise<AgentComponent[]>`: Finds components by their label (`text`) or kind, or with `within` the choices of one list, which it opens to read when they are not in the page.
- `subscribe(listener: (changed: AgentComponent[], changes: AgentEvent[]) => void): () => void`: Hears the components that changed, a moment after they do, and each change apart: which state, from what, to what, and what made it. Returns the stop.
- `record(): () => void`: Starts keeping what a person and the page change too, each with its source, beside what the agent does. Changes to one control close together are one. Returns the stop.
- `history(): AgentChange[]`: What was changed, the oldest first: the agent's through `act`, and from `record()` on, everyone's.
- `undo(): Promise<AgentResult>`: Takes the agent's last change back: the component is asked for what it held before, the way any step asks (its callback hears an agent, `allow` and `confirm` are asked). A press cannot be taken back.
- `redo(): Promise<AgentResult>`: Makes the last change taken back again.
- `undoSource(source: ChangeSource): Promise<AgentResult>`: Takes back every standing change one source made, the newest first, and leaves the rest: `undoSource("agent")` after a person has gone on working. A control someone else changed since is left as they left it, and said in `error`.
- `seek(count: number): Promise<AgentResult>`: Goes to where the first `count` changes stand and the rest are taken back.

A component in a snapshot (`AgentComponent`):

- `ref: string`: Names it in `act` and `query`; the same for as long as its element is in the page.
- `component: string`: What it is: `"switch"`, `"select"`, `"input"`, `"dialog"` …
- `label?: string`: Its accessible name, when it has one.
- `value?: string | number`
- `values?: readonly string[]`: What a list of several choices holds, in the page's order.
- `checked?: boolean | "mixed"`
- `open?: boolean`
- `min?: number`
- `max?: number`
- `items?: readonly AgentItem[]`: Its choices, where they are in the page. `query({ within })` reads a closed list's.
- `disabled?: boolean`
- `readOnly?: boolean`: It can be read and not changed: it then has no action.
- `confirm?: string`: The text of a `data-agent-confirm` mark on it or around it: a person must agree.
- `actions: readonly string[]`: What it can be asked to do now.

A step (`AgentStep`) and what `allow` and `confirm` are asked about (`AgentAction`, the step with these beside):

- `ref: string`: A component's `ref`, or its label.
- `action: string`
- `args?: readonly unknown[]`
- `component: string`
- `label: string | undefined`
- `confirm: string | undefined`

What a step did (`AgentStepResult`), and a change in `history()` (`AgentChange`):

- `ref: string`
- `action: string`
- `now?: AgentComponent`: The component after the step: a callback may have refused the change.
- `opened?: readonly AgentBrief[]`: What the step opened: a dialog, a menu, a list.
- `appeared?: readonly AgentBrief[]`: What else came into the page with it, up to twenty.
- `gone?: readonly AgentBrief[]`: What left the page with it, up to twenty.
- `args: readonly unknown[]`
- `source: ChangeSource`: What made it: `"agent"`, or a person's mouse, finger, pen or keyboard, or the page's code.
- `text: string`: The change as a sentence: `The agent set Project name to "Atlas"`.
- `before: AgentComponent`
- `after: AgentComponent | undefined`: Absent when the component left the page with the change.
- `undone: boolean`: Whether it was taken back since.

A change as `subscribe` tells it (`AgentEvent`, with the component's `ref`, `component` and `label`):

- `key: "value" | "values" | "checked" | "open" | "disabled"`: The state that changed.
- `value: string | number | boolean | readonly string[] | undefined`: What it is now. A value the page keeps from being read is said as redacted, or not at all.
- `previous: string | number | boolean | readonly string[] | undefined`: What it was.
- `source: ChangeSource`: What made it: the agent, a person's mouse, finger, pen or keyboard, or the page's code.
- `reason?: string`: Why, where a part of this library made the change: `"trigger-press"`, `"item-press"` …
- `ref: string`: Names it in `act` and `query`; the same for as long as its element is in the page.
- `component: string`: What it is: `"switch"`, `"select"`, `"input"`, `"dialog"` …
- `label?: string`: Its accessible name, when it has one.

What `stage` gives beside a result (`AgentStaged`):

- `applied: readonly AgentChange[]`: The changes that took effect, the oldest first. None of them is in `history()` yet.
- `revert(): Promise<AgentResult>`: Takes them back, the newest first, through the same handlers.
- `keep(): void`: Keeps them: they join `history()` as the agent's changes.
- `ok: boolean`
- `steps: readonly AgentStepResult[]`
- `error?: string`: Which step failed and why. Earlier steps stay done.

A kind of component of your own, given as `kinds` (`AgentKind`):

- `component: string`: Its name in a snapshot: `"rating"`.
- `selector: string`: The elements that are one. What is inside such an element is its own, and not listed.
- `read(element: Element): Pick< AgentComponent, "value" | "values" | "checked" | "open" | "min" | "max" | "items" > & { readonly actions: readonly string[] }`: What it holds now, and what it can be asked. Disabled, it is offered nothing.
- `perform( element: Element, action: string, args: readonly unknown[] ): void | string | Promise<void | string>`: Does one of its actions. A text it returns is said as the step's failure.

A step finds its component by its `ref`; else by its label, whole; else by a label that has every word of the name; else by the text beside it in its row; else by a choice of one radio group or tab list (the step is then that choice); else by its kind, where the page has one of that kind. A name two components answer to fails the step with both. `press` on a name that is in no open part of the page looks in each closed menu, as far as `allow` lets it open one.

The kinds of component it reads, what each is found by, and the actions each takes (a step's `action`; `setValue`, `setChecked` and `choose` take the value as `args[0]`):

- `switch` (`[role="switch"]`): `toggle`, `setChecked`
- `checkbox` (`[role="checkbox"]`): `toggle`, `setChecked`
- `radio-group` (`[role="radiogroup"]`): `setValue`
- `slider` (`[role="slider"]`): `setValue`
- `spinbutton` (`[role="spinbutton"]`): `setValue`
- `tree` (`[role="tree"]`): `setValue`, `open`, `close`
- `tabs` (`[role="tablist"]`): `setValue`
- `listbox` (`[role="listbox"]`): `setValue`
- `select` (`button[role="combobox"]`): `open`, `close`, `setValue`
- `combobox` (`input[role="combobox"]`): `setValue`, `clear`, `choose`
- `number-field` (`input[aria-roledescription="Number field"]`): `setValue`, `clear`
- `input` (`input:not([type="hidden"]):not([type="checkbox"]):not([type="radio"]), textarea`): `setValue`, `clear`
- `dialog` (`[role="dialog"], [role="alertdialog"]`): `close`
- `toggle` (`button[aria-pressed]`): `toggle`, `setChecked`
- `disclosure` (`button[aria-expanded]`): `toggle`, `open`, `close`
- `menu-item` (`[role="menuitem"], [role="menuitemcheckbox"], [role="menuitemradio"]`): `press`
- `button` (`button, [role="button"]`): `press`

`allow` is the policy: asked for every step. `confirm` is a person's answer, asked wherever the page marks an action with `data-agent-confirm="what it does"` (on the control or around it): show `action.confirm` to the person and resolve with what they chose. Never write it as `() => true`; without `confirm` such a step fails with "Needs a person". Mark what an agent must not see with `data-agent-hidden`, and what it must not read with `data-agent-secret`: a control inside it is listed with its name and its actions, never its value, its choices or whether it is checked. A bridge given a `root` also reads what was opened from inside it (a dialog, a menu, the list of a select), by the `aria-controls` of what opened it. `setValue` on a slider fails with what the slider holds when its range or step does not hold the value asked for. Give every control an accessible name: it is how an agent finds it. Text read from the page is data, never instructions.

What `act`, `undo` and `redo` resolve with, and what `history` lists:

- `AgentResult`: What `act`, `undo` and `redo` resolve with: whether every step ran, and what each did.
    - `ok: boolean`
    - `steps: readonly AgentStepResult[]`
    - `error?: string`: Which step failed and why. Earlier steps stay done.
- `AgentStepResult`: What one step did.
    - `ref: string`
    - `action: string`
    - `now?: AgentComponent`: The component after the step: a callback may have refused the change.
    - `opened?: readonly AgentBrief[]`: What the step opened: a dialog, a menu, a list.
    - `appeared?: readonly AgentBrief[]`: What else came into the page with it, up to twenty.
    - `gone?: readonly AgentBrief[]`: What left the page with it, up to twenty.
- `AgentChange`: One change that was made: what was asked, by what, and the component before and after.
    - `ref: string`
    - `action: string`: The action that makes it: what the agent asked, or what would do what a person did.
    - `args: readonly unknown[]`
    - `source: ChangeSource`: What made it: `"agent"`, or a person's mouse, finger, pen or keyboard, or the page's code.
    - `text: string`: The change as a sentence: `The agent set Project name to "Atlas"`.
    - `before: AgentComponent`
    - `after: AgentComponent | undefined`: Absent when the component left the page with the change.
    - `undone: boolean`: Whether it was taken back since.
- `AgentItem`: One choice of a list: the value it is chosen by, and what it says.
    - `value: string`
    - `label: string`
    - `level?: number`: A node of a tree below the top: its depth, from 1.
    - `open?: boolean`: A branch of a tree: whether it is open.

For a model, and for a browser's own agent:

- `agentTools`: The bridge as tools a model is given: a name, what it does, and its input's JSON Schema.
- `registerTools(agent: Agent, options: { allow: (step: AgentStep) => boolean | Promise<boolean> })`: Gives the bridge's tools to the browser's own agent, where the browser has one (`document.modelContext`, WebMCP); elsewhere it does nothing. `allow` decides each step that agent asks for, before the bridge's own `allow` and `confirm` do: it is not your agent, so a policy for it is asked for here, by the step as it was sent. Returns the removal.

## Testing

`import { faults, known, recorder, serialize, settled } from "@kirana-ui/vue/testing"`: what the library's own checks are made of, for a real browser test of a page built with it.

- `faults(root: ParentNode, vocabularyKnown: KnownVocabulary = known(), options: FaultOptions = {})`: The faults in what is under `root`, each as a sentence; none is an empty list. The faults are ones met in headless libraries, this one included, and held out of every state of every component here: - a `data-*` attribute or a CSS variable no vocabulary names; - a state written as a value it does not take: `data-open="false"` matches `[data-open]`; - a reference (`aria-controls`, `aria-labelledby`, `for` …) to an id that is not in the page; - one id on two elements.
- `known(...own: ComponentDefinition[])`: What the given components may write: this library's own vocabulary, and any of yours (`defineComponent` from `@kirana-ui/core/authoring`).
- `serialize(root: Element, options: SerializeOptions = {})`: What is under `root` as text: one line an element, its attributes sorted, a run of text nodes as one text, an input's live value and not its attribute. Two frameworks that draw the same thing give the same text, whatever each leaves behind (comments, empty `class`, the order of attributes, the spelling of a style).
- `settled(page: Document = document, timeout = 5000)`: Resolves once nothing is moving: a framework has had its turn, no part is in the first or last frame of its way in or out, and no animation is running. Rejects after `timeout` milliseconds, saying what was still moving.
- `recorder()`: Records what a change callback hears, and can refuse what it is asked.

The components also run where there is no layout and no Web Animations, as in jsdom: a popup opens and closes at once there, with no wait for a transition, so a test of what a press changes needs no polyfill for `getAnimations`. Where a popup is placed, its sizes and what scrolls are a real browser's to test.

`faults(root, known(definition), options)`: `known()` alone is the library's vocabulary, `known(definition)` adds a component of your own (`defineComponent`), and `options` (`FaultOptions`) are:

- `allow?: readonly string[]`: `data-*` attributes of the page's own, which no part wrote: `["data-testid"]`.
- `free?: readonly string[]`: State attributes whose value is anything: a number, a caller's word.

Its other types:

- `KnownVocabulary`: The attributes and variables parts may write, from one or more vocabularies.
    - `attributes: ReadonlyMap<string, readonly string[] | null>`: Each state attribute: the values it takes, or `null` for one that is present or absent.
    - `variables: ReadonlySet<string>`
- `SerializeOptions`: What `serialize` is told to leave out.
    - `skip?: readonly string[]`: Attributes left out: a framework's own marks. Test ids are written as `#name`.
- `Recorder`: What `recorder()` gives: a callback to hand a component, and what it heard.
    - `listen(value: Value, details: ChangeDetails): void`: Give this as the callback: `onValueChange: heard.listen`.
    - `calls: readonly Heard<Value>[]`: Every call so far, in order.
    - `said(): string[]`: The calls as `"value reason"`, for one assertion over all of them.
    - `refuse(on?: boolean): void`: From now on, every change is refused (`details.cancel()`), or let through again.
    - `clear(): void`
- `Heard`: One call of a change callback, as a test reads it.
    - `value: Value`
    - `reason: string`
    - `source: ChangeDetails["source"]`

## Using it

- Each component is a namespace of parts: `<Dialog.Root>`, `<Dialog.Trigger>`. A component with one part is the component: `<Button>`.
- A part renders its own element and takes that element's attributes. `as="a"` draws another element; `as-child` puts the part on the element in its slot: `<Dialog.Trigger as-child><a href="/x">…</a></Dialog.Trigger>`.
- With `as-child` there are three layers of props, lowest first: the attributes on the part, the slotted element's own, the part's own (its role, ARIA, state attributes and listeners). A higher layer wins an attribute it gives, and one it leaves `undefined` stays; classes are joined; styles are merged, the higher layer winning a property; every listener of an event runs, lowest first (the part's caller's, the element's, the part's), and `event.preventKiranaHandler()` called in either of the first two stops only the part's own. So `<Button as-child data-slot="button"><a data-slot="link" href="/x">Next</a></Button>` is `<a data-slot="link" href="/x">Next</a>` with the button's listeners. Without `as-child` there are two layers: the attributes on the part, then the part's own.
- An attribute no layer gives a value is left out, never handed on as `undefined`. With `as-child` onto a component, the component is given the merged props as its attributes, and Vue lays a component's attributes over its root's own: the part's state wins there, and an attribute the props hold no value for stays the root's. A component that wants its root's own to win over the part's declares `inheritAttrs: false` and writes `v-bind="$attrs"` before them (`<td v-bind="$attrs" data-selected="true">`), as a React component spreads its props first.
- A part that draws a `<button>` writes `type="button"`, so that it never submits a form by accident; a `type` given to the part wins (`<Button type="submit">`), and a part drawn as an element that is not a button (`as="a"`, or `as-child` on an `<a>`) is given none. On a component (`as` or `as-child` over one), whose element is not known until it is drawn, the browser takes it off an element that is not a button once it is in the page. With `:native-button="false"`, a link that navigates stays a link: `as="a" href="/x"`, or `as-child` on an `<a href>`, is given no `role`, no `tabindex` and none of the button's keys (its Enter is its own, and Space does not press it); a disabled one still has `tabindex="-1"` and `aria-disabled`. On a component they are taken off once the element is in the page.
- A part's default slot is given the part's state, with `as-child` and without: `v-slot="{ state }"`, read from the part's `data-*` attributes listed below, camel-cased: `data-open` is `state.open === true`, `data-side="bottom"` is `state.side === "bottom"`, `data-starting-style` is `state.startingStyle`, and a state that does not hold is absent.
- With `as-child`, what a part keeps in its element is in the slotted element: a form control's hidden native input as its last child, and the text a part writes (`Meter.Value`, `Select.Value`, `Calendar.Heading`, a toast's `Title`) while the slotted element has no content of its own: `<Meter.Value as-child><b /></Meter.Value>` is `<b>40%</b>`. A listener given to a part is typed with the event's `preventKiranaHandler()`: `PartEvent<MouseEvent>`, exported by the package.
- Props are written in kebab case (`default-value`). A value binds with `v-model:value` (`v-model:open`, `v-model:page` …); the matching event carries the details: `@value-change="(value, details) => …"`. Below, a prop marked `v-model` binds so, and an event is written as its listener: `@value-change`.
- A part that draws a list gives each entry to its slot: `v-slot="{ segment }"`.
- A part that says a value gives it to its slot, to draw something else: `<Select.Value v-slot="{ value, label }">` (with `multiple`, `{ values, labels }`, in the items' order), `<Slider.Value v-slot="{ text, values }">`.
- A `Positioner`'s `anchor` is a template ref to an element or a component (`:anchor="box"`), an element, an object with `getBoundingClientRect`, or a function that gives one of those.
- Each part's props are a type of the same entry, named for the part, and its events another: `import type { RootProps, RootEmits } from "@kirana-ui/vue/tabs"`. A part also takes `as`, `as-child` and the attributes of the element it draws.
- Each component's "Anatomy" is where its parts go: a part is written inside the part it is indented under, with elements of your own between them where the design needs any. `(optional)` marks a wrapper that may be left out, what it holds then written where the wrapper would be; `(repeated)` a part written once for each entry (an item, a tab, a toast), or any number of times; `(as above)` a part drawn in full where it first appears. It is the library's own data (`inside`, `optional` and `repeated` on each part of `@kirana-ui/vocabulary`), held against the pages the library is tested with: write a part nowhere else.
- These parts draw no element, and take no attributes: every `Portal` (what is inside is drawn at the end of `<body>`), `AlertDialog.Root`, `Autocomplete.Root`, `Autocomplete.Collection`, `Calendar.Months`, `Calendar.Weekdays`, `Calendar.Weeks`, `Combobox.Root`, `Combobox.Value`, `Combobox.Collection`, `ContextMenu.Root`, `ContextMenu.SubmenuRoot`, `DateField.Segments`, `DatePicker.Root`, `DatePicker.Segments`, `DatePicker.Months`, `DatePicker.Weekdays`, `DatePicker.Weeks`, `Dialog.Root`, `Drawer.Root`, `Field.Validity`, `FileUpload.Items`, `HoverCard.Root`, `Menu.Root`, `Menu.SubmenuRoot`, `Pagination.Items`, `Popover.Root`, `Rating.Items`, `Select.Root`, `TagsInput.Items`, `TimeField.Segments`, `Toast.List`, `Tooltip.Root` and `Tour.Root`. Every other part draws the element named for it below.
- A popup is drawn in a portal at the end of `<body>`. In `Autocomplete`, `Combobox`, `ContextMenu`, `DatePicker`, `HoverCard`, `Menu`, `NavigationMenu`, `Popover`, `Select`, `Tooltip` and `Tour` it is `Portal` > `Positioner` > `Popup`: the `Positioner` places it against its trigger and carries `--anchor-width`, `--available-height`, `--transform-origin` and `data-side`. `AlertDialog`, `Dialog` and `Drawer` have no `Positioner`: there it is `Portal` > `Backdrop` and `Popup`, and the design places the popup. A dialog and an alert dialog may put the `Popup` in a `Viewport`, the box a long one scrolls in.
- Every `Positioner` takes the same options (`side`, `align`, `sideOffset`, `alignOffset`, `collisionPadding`, `collisionBoundary`, `collisionAvoidance`, `sticky`, `arrowPadding`, `positionMethod`, `anchor`), listed once under "Positioner options" with their defaults. An anchor may change while the popup is open, and the popup follows.
- Every change callback of a value the component holds is `(value, details)`: `details.reason`, `details.event`, `details.source` (mouse, touch, pen, keyboard, virtual, programmatic, agent), and `details.cancel()` to keep the value as it was (`@at-bottom-change`, `@checked-change`, `@editing-change`, `@expanded-change`, `@files-change`, `@format-change`, `@index-change`, `@input-value-change`, `@month-change`, `@open-change`, `@page-change`, `@pressed-change`, `@select`, `@selected-change`, `@sizes-change`, `@snap-point-change`, `@step-change`, `@value-change`, `@value-committed`, `@value-complete`, `@values-change`, `@visible-change` and `onFormSubmit`). A callback that reports something that happened takes only that, and cannot be refused: `@complete`, `@files-reject`, `@hover-change`, `@loading-status-change`, `@value-invalid` and `onClearErrors`.
- A part that is in the page only while it is open, chosen or checked leaves it otherwise. `keepMounted` keeps it in the page, hidden, on the parts that take it and no others: `Accordion.Panel`, `Autocomplete.Clear`, `Avatar.Image`, `Checkbox.Indicator`, `Collapsible.Panel`, `Combobox.Clear`, `Combobox.ItemIndicator`, `ContextMenu.CheckboxItemIndicator`, `ContextMenu.RadioItemIndicator`, `Listbox.ItemIndicator`, `Menu.CheckboxItemIndicator`, `Menu.RadioItemIndicator`, `RadioGroup.Indicator`, `ScrollArea.Scrollbar`, `Select.ItemIndicator`, `Tabs.Panel` and `Tree.Group`.
- `readOnly` (shown, focusable, not changeable) is a prop of `Autocomplete`, `Calendar`, `Checkbox`, `ColorPicker`, `Combobox`, `DateField`, `DatePicker`, `Editable`, `NumberField`, `Otp`, `RadioGroup`, `Rating`, `Select`, `Slider`, `Switch`, `TagsInput` and `TimeField` and of no other component.
- No CSS is shipped and no styles are injected. A part is styled by its element, its `class`, and the attributes and CSS variables listed for it below.
- A boolean state is an attribute that is present or absent (`[data-open]`), never `="false"`.
- An entrance starts from `[data-starting-style]` and an exit ends at `[data-ending-style]`: write the hidden style under both and transition between. A part leaves the page when its own motion has ended.
- A value is controlled when it is given (`value`) and the component's own when it is not (`defaultValue`). `open`/`defaultOpen` and the others pair the same way.
- A control with a `name` is submitted with the form around it and follows the form's reset. Inside a `Field` it is the field's control.
- `PortalProvider` (`container`) says where the popups inside it are drawn, in place of the end of `<body>`: a shadow root's host, a full-screen element.
- An agent can read and use a page built with these: `createAgent()` from `@kirana-ui/vue/agent` gives `snapshot()`, `act({ steps })`, `query()`, `history()`, `undo()` and `redo()`; what it changes reaches the same callbacks with `details.source === "agent"`. "Agent", above, has the whole of it.

### For a design system

- For an element of your own that takes `as` and `as-child` (a badge, a breadcrumb's link): `import { Primitive } from "@kirana-ui/vue/primitive"`. `<Primitive as="span">` draws that element (a `div` by default) with the attributes it is given; `<Primitive as-child>` draws the element in its slot, by the same rule: the slotted element's own props lie over the attributes on the `Primitive`, classes joined, styles merged, both listeners of an event run.
- Tooltips need no provider: one is open at a time across the page, and while one shows the next opens without its wait, by themselves. A tooltip waits 600 ms before it opens (a hover card 600 ms, and 300 ms before it closes). A design system whose tooltips open at once passes `delay` on its own root: `<Tooltip.Root :delay="0" v-bind="$attrs">` in its own component (its caller's `delay` still wins).

## Components

### Accordion

```
import { Accordion } from "@kirana-ui/vue/accordion"
```

Parts: `<Accordion.Root>`, `<Accordion.Item>`, `<Accordion.Header>`, `<Accordion.Trigger>`, `<Accordion.Panel>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Accordion.Root>
  <Accordion.Item> (repeated)
    <Accordion.Header>
      <Accordion.Trigger>
    <Accordion.Panel>
```

Props of its root:

- `value?: readonly Value[]`: `v-model:value`. The values of the open items.
- `defaultValue?: readonly Value[]`: Read once.
- `multiple?: boolean`: Whether several items can be open at once. Default `false`: opening one closes the others.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disables every item: none can be opened or closed.
- `orientation?: Orientation`: The way the arrows move between triggers. Default `vertical`.
- `loopFocus?: boolean`: Whether the arrows wrap from the last trigger to the first. Default `true`.
- `loop?: boolean`: Whether the arrows wrap from the last item to the first.
- `@value-change: (value: Value[], details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as an item is about to open or close, with the values that would be open: `details.cancel()` keeps them as they were.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Accordion.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Generic: `<Value = unknown>`. Its props are above.
- `<Accordion.Item>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be opened or closed.
    - `value?: unknown`: What tells this item from the others; an item that is given none makes its own.
- `<Accordion.Header>` draws a `<h3>`.
- `<Accordion.Trigger>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<Accordion.Panel>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `keepMounted?: boolean`: Keeps the closed panel in the page, `hidden`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: Groups the items.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the items are laid out, and the arrows that move between their triggers.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- item: One section: a header with its trigger, and a panel. Its `value` tells it from the others; an item that is given none makes its own.
    - `data-index`: The item's place among the accordion's items, from 0.
    - `data-open`: Present when the item is open.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- header: The heading that holds the trigger.
    - `data-index`: The item's place among the accordion's items, from 0.
    - `data-open`: Present when the item is open.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- trigger: The button that opens and closes the item's panel.
    - `data-index`: The item's place among the accordion's items, from 0.
    - `data-panel-open`: Present when the item's panel is open.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- panel: The item's content. In the page while open, and through its exit's motion.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the items are laid out, and the arrows that move between their triggers.
    - `data-index`: The item's place among the accordion's items, from 0.
    - `--accordion-panel-height`: The panel's content height while it opens or closes, `auto` once it is open.
    - `--accordion-panel-width`: The panel's content width while it opens or closes, `auto` once it is open.

### AlertDialog

```
import { AlertDialog } from "@kirana-ui/vue/alert-dialog"
```

Parts: `<AlertDialog.Root>`, `<AlertDialog.Trigger>`, `<AlertDialog.Portal>`, `<AlertDialog.Backdrop>`, `<AlertDialog.Viewport>`, `<AlertDialog.Popup>`, `<AlertDialog.Title>`, `<AlertDialog.Description>`, `<AlertDialog.Close>`.

Anatomy:

```
<AlertDialog.Root>
  <AlertDialog.Trigger>
  <AlertDialog.Portal>
    <AlertDialog.Backdrop>
    <AlertDialog.Viewport> (optional)
      <AlertDialog.Popup>
        <AlertDialog.Title>
        <AlertDialog.Description>
        <AlertDialog.Close>
```

Props of its root:

- `open?: boolean`: `v-model:open`. Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether it starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `@open-change: (value: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as it is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<AlertDialog.Root>` draws no element. Holds the dialog: whether it is open. Its props are above.
- `<AlertDialog.Trigger>` draws a `<button>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: It cannot be pressed: the button is disabled, and says so (`data-disabled`).
- `<AlertDialog.Portal>` draws no element. A portal takes nothing: where it is drawn is its `PortalProvider`'s to say.
- `<AlertDialog.Backdrop>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<AlertDialog.Viewport>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<AlertDialog.Popup>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<AlertDialog.Title>` draws a `<h2>`. The heading that names the dialog.
- `<AlertDialog.Description>` draws a `<p>`. The text that describes the dialog.
- `<AlertDialog.Close>` draws a `<button>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: It cannot be pressed: the button is disabled, and says so (`data-disabled`).

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- trigger: The button that opens the dialog.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the dialog is open.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- backdrop: The layer over the page behind the dialog.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
- viewport: What a long dialog scrolls in: it lies over the page, between the backdrop and the popup. A press on it beside the popup is a press outside the dialog; a press on its scrollbar is not.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-nested`: Present when the dialog opened over another dialog.
    - `data-nested-dialog-open`: Present when another dialog is open above this one.
- popup: The dialog itself.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-nested`: Present when the dialog opened over another dialog.
    - `data-nested-dialog-open`: Present when another dialog is open above this one.
    - `--nested-dialogs`: How many dialogs are open above this one.
- close: A button that closes the dialog.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### Autocomplete

```
import { Autocomplete } from "@kirana-ui/vue/autocomplete"
```

Parts: `<Autocomplete.Root>`, `<Autocomplete.Input>`, `<Autocomplete.Trigger>`, `<Autocomplete.Clear>`, `<Autocomplete.Portal>`, `<Autocomplete.Positioner>`, `<Autocomplete.Popup>`, `<Autocomplete.List>`, `<Autocomplete.Collection>`, `<Autocomplete.Group>`, `<Autocomplete.GroupLabel>`, `<Autocomplete.Separator>`, `<Autocomplete.Item>`, `<Autocomplete.Empty>`, `<Autocomplete.Status>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Autocomplete.Root>
  <Autocomplete.Input>
  <Autocomplete.Trigger>
  <Autocomplete.Portal>
    <Autocomplete.Positioner>
      <Autocomplete.Popup>
        <Autocomplete.List> (optional)
          <Autocomplete.Collection> (optional)
            <Autocomplete.Item> (repeated, as above)
            <Autocomplete.Group> (optional, repeated, as above)
          <Autocomplete.Group> (optional, repeated)
            <Autocomplete.Collection> (optional, as above)
            <Autocomplete.Item> (repeated)
            <Autocomplete.GroupLabel>
          <Autocomplete.Separator> (repeated)
        <Autocomplete.Collection> (optional, as above)
        <Autocomplete.Empty>
        <Autocomplete.Status> (optional)
  <Autocomplete.Popup> (as above)
  <Autocomplete.Status> (optional, as above)
  <Autocomplete.Clear>
```

Props of its root:

- `defaultValue?: string`: The text it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `open?: boolean`: `v-model:open`. Whether the list is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether the list starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `mode?: "list" | "both" | "inline" | "none"`: `"list"` (the default): the suggestions are filtered by what is typed. `"both"`: they are filtered, and the rest of the first one that begins with what is typed is written after it in the input, selected, so typing on replaces it and Enter or Tab keeps it; the arrows write the suggestion they are on into the input. `"inline"`: written so, and not filtered. `"none"`: neither; the suggestions are as the caller draws them. A completion is not written into a word an input method is composing, nor after a deletion.
- `filter?: ((label: string, query: string) => boolean) | null`: Whether a suggestion is shown for what was typed; `null` shows every one.
- `openOnInputClick?: boolean`: Whether a press on the input opens the list. Default: it opens when something is typed.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Its text can be read and not changed: nothing typed is taken, no suggestion pressed is written in, and its clear button does nothing. The list still opens (by its button, the arrows, or a press with `openOnInputClick`) and can be gone through. It keeps focus, and its text is still submitted.
- `items?: readonly ComboboxItemData<Value>[] | readonly ComboboxGroupData<Value>[] | Readonly<Record<string, string>>`: The suggestions as data, for a `Collection` to draw: a list of them with their labels, groups of them (`{ value, items }`, `value` the group's name), or the labels by value. The autocomplete filters them by what is typed (not with `mode: "none"`), and the `Collection` draws what is left.
- `required?: boolean`: Needed: in a `Field`, leaving it empty is then invalid.
- `name?: string`: The input's name in the form around it.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `virtualized?: ListCollection`: Every row, when only some are in the page: each item is then given its `index`.
- `autoHighlight?: boolean`: The first suggestion for what was typed is highlighted as one types, so Enter takes it. Off by default: no suggestion is highlighted for having been typed at, and Enter is the form's, with the text as typed, until an arrow or the pointer has gone to one.
- `modelValue?: string`: `v-model:modelValue`. The text, which is the value: `v-model`.
- `@value-change: (value: string, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as the text is about to change, typed or chosen: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `@open-change: (value: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as the list is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Autocomplete.Root>` draws no element. Holds the autocomplete: the text, and whether the suggestions are open. Its props are above.
- `<Autocomplete.Input>` draws a `<input>`.
- `<Autocomplete.Trigger>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<Autocomplete.Clear>` draws a `<button>`.
    - `keepMounted?: boolean`: Keeps the button in the page while there is nothing to clear.
- `<Autocomplete.Portal>` draws no element. A portal takes nothing: where it is drawn is its `PortalProvider`'s to say.
- `<Autocomplete.Positioner>` draws a `<div>`. A positioner's own props: where its popup goes, and what it is placed against. Takes the positioner options ("Positioner options", above).
- `<Autocomplete.Popup>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Autocomplete.List>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Autocomplete.Collection>` draws no element. Draws the suggestions from the root's `items`: its content once for each one left for what was typed, or for each group that has some left; given a group, for each of that group's. The root then filters. Its default slot is also given `entry: ComboboxEntry`.
    - `of?: ComboboxEntry`: A group the root's `items` gave: its items left are then what is drawn.
- `<Autocomplete.Group>` draws a `<div>`. Items that belong together, named by their label. Hidden while none is shown.
- `<Autocomplete.GroupLabel>` draws a `<div>`. The name of a group. Outside a group it is plain text, and names nothing.
- `<Autocomplete.Separator>` draws a `<div>`. A line between groups.
- `<Autocomplete.Item>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be chosen, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What is filtered and what the input shows; the item's text when left out.
    - `index?: number`: Its place among all the rows, in a virtualized list.
    - `value: unknown`: Required. What the combobox's value is while this item is the chosen one.
- `<Autocomplete.Empty>` draws a `<div>`. What is shown when no item is.
- `<Autocomplete.Status>` draws a `<div>`. Says how the list stands ("3 results", "Loading") to software that reads the page, as its text changes. It stays in the page while its text changes: inside the popup, or beside the input.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- input: The text input: its text is the value, and what is typed asks for suggestions.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the list is open.
    - `data-pressed`: Present while its popup is open: it stays pressed, as a button held down.
    - `data-popup-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end | none"`: While the list is in the page: the side of the trigger it is on, after any flip; `none` when it lies over the trigger. Not said while it opens as a sheet.
    - `data-list-empty`: Present when no item is shown for what was typed, once the list is in the page.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
