    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
- trigger: A button that opens and closes the list. With the input inside the popup it is the combobox: a stop for Tab, and what the popup is placed against.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the list is open.
    - `data-pressed`: Present while its popup is open: it stays pressed, as a button held down.
    - `data-popup-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end | none"`: While the list is in the page: the side of the trigger it is on, after any flip; `none` when it lies over the trigger. Not said while it opens as a sheet.
    - `data-list-empty`: Present when no item is shown for what was typed, once the list is in the page.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
- positioner: Places the list against the input: against the chips' box when the input is in one, the button when the input is inside the popup, or its own `anchor`. It carries the geometry. As a sheet it is not placed, and carries none.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-presentation="popup | sheet"`: How the list opened: placed against its trigger, or as a sheet from the bottom edge.
    - `data-anchor-hidden`: Present while the anchor is out of view: scrolled away, or clipped by a box around it.
    - `data-empty`: Present when no item is shown for what was typed.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
- popup: The list of items. With a `list` inside, what holds it: a dialog around an input and the list. As a sheet, a design moves it by what it says of the drag, and gives it `touch-action: none` where a finger drags it.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-presentation="popup | sheet"`: How the list opened: placed against its trigger, or as a sheet from the bottom edge.
    - `data-swiping`: Present while the sheet is dragged.
    - `data-swipe-dismiss`: Present once a drag has closed it.
    - `data-anchor-hidden`: Present while the anchor is out of view: scrolled away, or clipped by a box around it.
    - `data-empty`: Present when no item is shown for what was typed.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-x`: As a sheet: how far it has been dragged across, always 0px.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-y`: As a sheet: how far it has been dragged down.
    - `--drawer-swipe-progress`: As a sheet: how far it has been dragged, of its own height: 0 to 1.
    - `--drawer-swipe-strength`: As a sheet, once let go: 0.1 to 1, the share of the design's own time it should take to come to rest.
- list: The items' own box inside the popup, when the popup holds more than items (an input): it is then the listbox.
    - `data-empty`: Present when no item is shown for what was typed.
- item: One suggestion: chosen, its text is written into the input.
    - `data-selected`: Present on the chosen item.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- clear: A button that empties the input and the value. It is in the page while there is something to clear (the text, for an autocomplete; else what is chosen), and through its exit; `keepMounted` keeps it there.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the list is open.
    - `data-visible`: Present while there is something to clear.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.

### Autosize

```
import { Autosize } from "@kirana-ui/vue/autosize"
```

Parts: `<Autosize.Textarea>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Autosize.Textarea>
```

Props of its root:

- `modelValue?: string`: `v-model:modelValue`. The text: `v-model`.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Autosize.Textarea>` draws a `<textarea>`. A `<textarea>` as tall as its text. Its `height` is written; `min-height` and `max-height` are the design's. Its props are above.

### Avatar

```
import { Avatar } from "@kirana-ui/vue/avatar"
```

Parts: `<Avatar.Root>`, `<Avatar.Image>`, `<Avatar.Fallback>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Avatar.Root>
  <Avatar.Image>
  <Avatar.Fallback>
```

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Avatar.Root>` draws a `<span>`.
- `<Avatar.Image>` draws a `<img>`.
    - `src?: string`: The picture's address: the part is in the page once it has loaded.
    - `keepMounted?: boolean`: Keeps the element in the page while the picture loads, as Base UI's: it loads the picture itself (`loading="lazy"` works), and until it has loaded it is `aria-hidden`, with `data-loading` or `data-error` for the design to hide or fade it by. Default: `false`, the element is drawn once the picture has loaded.
    - `@loading-status-change: (status: ImageStatus) => void`: `@loading-status-change`: each time the picture's loading status changes, `loading` once it has an address, then `loaded` or `error`; `idle` again when its address is taken away. The root says the same in `data-image-loading-status`.
- `<Avatar.Fallback>` draws a `<span>`. What shows until the picture has loaded, or when it cannot; after its `delay`, when it has one.
    - `delay?: number`: How long to wait before showing, in milliseconds, so a picture that loads sooner never lets the fallback be seen. Read once. Default: `0`, at once.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The frame the image and its stand-in share.
    - `data-image-loading-status="idle | loading | loaded | error"`: Where the picture is in its loading: `idle` while it has no address.
- image: The picture. In the page once it has loaded; with `keepMounted` (on Angular, the attribute form) in the page all along, `aria-hidden` until it has loaded.
    - `data-loading`: Present while the picture loads, on an image kept in the page.
    - `data-error`: Present when the picture cannot load, on an image kept in the page.

### Button

```
import { Button } from "@kirana-ui/vue/button"
```

Props:

- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: a press does nothing.
- `focusableWhenDisabled?: boolean`: Keeps a disabled button in the tab order, so what it would do can still be read.
- `nativeButton?: boolean`: `false` when the element is not a `<button>`: it is given a button's role, a place in the tab order and its keys (Enter, Space). A link that navigates (an `<a>` or `<area>` with an `href`) stays a link: no role is written over its own, it keeps its own place in the tab order and its own Enter, and Space does not press it; disabled, it is still blocked.

`<Button>` draws a `<button>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The button.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### Calendar

```
import { Calendar } from "@kirana-ui/vue/calendar"
```

Parts: `<Calendar.Root>`, `<Calendar.Heading>`, `<Calendar.Previous>`, `<Calendar.Next>`, `<Calendar.Months>`, `<Calendar.Grid>`, `<Calendar.Weekdays>`, `<Calendar.HeadCell>`, `<Calendar.Weeks>`, `<Calendar.Cell>`, `<Calendar.Day>`, `<Calendar.Input>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Calendar.Root>
  <Calendar.Months> (optional)
    <Calendar.Heading>
    <Calendar.Grid>
      <Calendar.Weekdays>
        <Calendar.HeadCell> (repeated)
      <Calendar.Weeks>
        <Calendar.Cell> (repeated)
          <Calendar.Day>
  <Calendar.Previous>
  <Calendar.Next>
  <Calendar.Input>
```

Props of its root:

- `value?: CalendarValueOf<Mode>`: `v-model:value`. One day; with `mode: "range"` a first and a last day; with `mode: "multiple"` a list of days, in the order they were chosen. `null` (or an empty list) for none.
- `defaultValue?: CalendarValueOf<Mode>`: The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `mode?: Mode`: Whether one day is chosen (the default), a first and a last (`"range"`), or any number (`"multiple"`: a day pressed is added, and pressed again is taken away).
- `required?: boolean`: Whether a day, once chosen, stays chosen. Off by default, as in react-day-picker: the chosen day pressed again is taken away and the value is `null`, heard with the reason `"day-deselect"` (cancellable). Given, the chosen day pressed again stays, and with `mode: "multiple"` the last day cannot be taken away. With `mode: "range"` a press always begins a range again, so a press never clears a range. It does not make a form ask for a value.
- `minDays?: number`: With `mode: "multiple"`: the fewest days that can be left chosen. A press that would leave fewer does nothing.
- `maxDays?: number`: With `mode: "multiple"`: the most days that can be chosen. Once they are, the other days are disabled until one is taken away.
- `months?: number`: How many months are shown side by side (1 by default): one selection and one grid for the keys, which go from a month into the next. Each is drawn in `Calendar.Months`.
- `pagedNavigation?: boolean`: With several `months`: whether Previous and Next turn them all (a page) rather than one month. Off by default, as in react-day-picker.
- `month?: IsoDate`: `v-model:month`. The month shown (the first of them, with several `months`), when the caller holds it: any day of it. A caption's month and year menus, or a "today" button, set it.
- `defaultMonth?: IsoDate`: The month it starts on, when the caller does not hold `month`. Read once. Without it, the month of `defaultFocusedValue`, of the value, or of today.
- `defaultFocusedValue?: IsoDate`: The day it opens on, focusable when Tab reaches the grid. It is also the month it opens on, unless `month` or `defaultMonth` says another: then the stop for Tab is a chosen day of the months shown, today, or their first day.
- `locale?: string`: The language and region its names, numbers, first day of the week and calendar follow (`"en-US"`, `"fa-IR"`). Give it: a server does not know the reader's. The week begins on the day the region begins it on (Sunday in `"en-US"`, Monday in `"fr-FR"`), or on the day a `-u-fw-` extension names: `"en-US-u-fw-mon"` is American English with weeks from Monday (`sun`, `mon`, `tue`, `wed`, `thu`, `fri`, `sat`). Default `"en-US"`.
- `calendarSystem?: CalendarSystem`: The calendar its months are laid out in, when it is not the Gregorian one: an instance from `@internationalized/date` (`new PersianCalendar()`). Given, not found from the locale: a page then carries only the calendars it uses.
- `min?: IsoDate`: The first and the last day that can be chosen.
- `max?: IsoDate`: The last day that can be chosen.
- `isDateUnavailable?: (date: IsoDate) => boolean`: Days that cannot be chosen, though they can be reached: a day off, a day taken.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: no day can be chosen.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is: the days can be moved through, and none can be chosen.
- `fixedWeeks?: boolean`: Always six rows, so the calendar is one height in every month.
- `name?: string`: The name its hidden input submits the value under: a day; the first and the last of a range, as two entries; each day of a list.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form it belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `@value-change: (value: CalendarValueOf<Mode>, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as a day is about to be chosen: `details.cancel()` keeps the value as it was.
- `@month-change: (value: string, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as another month is about to be shown (the keys, the buttons, a day of another month pressed): its first day. `details.cancel()` keeps the month as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Calendar.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Generic: `<Mode extends CalendarMode = "single">`. `value` and its events are typed by `mode`: a day, a range, or a list of days. Its props are above.
- `<Calendar.Heading>` draws a `<div>`. Names the month shown. Read out when it changes.
- `<Calendar.Previous>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<Calendar.Next>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<Calendar.Months>` draws no element. The months shown, with several: each is given to draw its heading and its grid. It draws no element, and is left out for one month. Its default slot is also given `month: CalendarMonth`.
- `<Calendar.Grid>` draws a `<table>`. The table of a month's days: a grid the arrows move in, from one month shown into the next.
- `<Calendar.Weekdays>` draws no element. The days of the week: each is given to draw its head cell. Its default slot is also given `weekday: CalendarWeekday`.
- `<Calendar.HeadCell>` draws a `<th>`. A column's heading: a day of the week.
    - `weekday: CalendarWeekday`: Required. The day of the week it names, as `Calendar.Weekdays` gives it.
- `<Calendar.Weeks>` draws no element. The weeks of the month shown: each is given to draw its row of days. Its default slot is also given `week: readonly CalendarDay[]`.
- `<Calendar.Cell>` draws a `<td>`.
    - `date: string`: Required. The day it is for, as a week of `Calendar.Weeks` gives it.
- `<Calendar.Day>` draws a `<button>`.
    - `date?: string`: The day it is the button of. Left out, the `Calendar.Cell`'s it is inside.
- `<Calendar.Input>` draws a `<input>`. The hidden input it is submitted by, when it has a name: one more is drawn after it for each other day.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The calendar.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when its value cannot be changed.
- previous: Shows the month before.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- next: Shows the month after.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- cell: A day's cell.
    - `data-selected`: Present on a chosen day, on every day of a chosen range, and on each day of a list. Also on a copy of one (a day of the month before or after, shown in its own month too), which is drawn as the day is but has no aria-selected.
    - `data-today`: Present on today.
    - `data-outside-month`: Present on the days of the month before and after that fill the first and last weeks.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-unavailable`: Present on a day that cannot be chosen.
    - `data-range-start`: Present on the first day of a range, and on a copy of it.
    - `data-range-end`: Present on the last day of a range, and on a copy of it.
- day: The button for a day.
    - `data-selected`: Present on a chosen day, on every day of a chosen range, and on each day of a list. Also on a copy of one (a day of the month before or after, shown in its own month too), which is drawn as the day is but has no aria-selected.
    - `data-today`: Present on today.
    - `data-outside-month`: Present on the days of the month before and after that fill the first and last weeks.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-unavailable`: Present on a day that cannot be chosen.
    - `data-range-start`: Present on the first day of a range, and on a copy of it.
    - `data-range-end`: Present on the last day of a range, and on a copy of it.

### Carousel

```
import { Carousel } from "@kirana-ui/vue/carousel"
```

Parts: `<Carousel.Root>`, `<Carousel.Viewport>`, `<Carousel.Item>`, `<Carousel.Previous>`, `<Carousel.Next>`, `<Carousel.Indicator>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Carousel.Root>
  <Carousel.Viewport>
    <Carousel.Item> (repeated)
  <Carousel.Previous>
  <Carousel.Next>
  <Carousel.Indicator> (repeated)
```

Props of its root:

- `index?: number`: `v-model:index`. Which slide is at the start of the view, from 0.
- `defaultIndex?: number`: The slide it starts at, when the caller does not hold `index`. Read once. Default `0`.
- `orientation?: Orientation`: Whether the slides go across (the default) or down.
- `loop?: boolean`: Whether going on from the last slide comes round to the first.
- `@index-change: (value: number, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as another slide is about to be at the start of the view: `details.cancel()` keeps the index as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Carousel.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Its props are above.
- `<Carousel.Viewport>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Carousel.Item>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `index?: number`: Its place among the slides, from 0. Left out, its place in the page, once it is there: give it on a page a server draws, which cannot count them.
- `<Carousel.Previous>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<Carousel.Next>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<Carousel.Indicator>` draws a `<button>`.
    - `index: number`: Required. The slide it goes to, from 0.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The carousel: a region, named by the caller.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the slides go across or down.
- viewport: What scrolls. The slides are its children; the design snaps them (`scroll-snap-type`) and says whether a step glides (`scroll-behavior`).
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the slides go across or down.
- item: One slide.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the slides go across or down.
    - `data-current`: Present on the slide the view is at, and on its button.
- previous: Goes back a slide.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- next: Goes on a slide.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- indicator: A button for one slide.
    - `data-current`: Present on the slide the view is at, and on its button.

### Checkbox

```
import { Checkbox } from "@kirana-ui/vue/checkbox"
```

Parts: `<Checkbox.Root>`, `<Checkbox.Indicator>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Checkbox.Root>
  <Checkbox.Indicator>
```

Props of its root:

- `checked?: boolean`: `v-model:checked`. Whether it is checked, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultChecked?: boolean`: Read once.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable.
- `required?: boolean`: Needed: in a `Field`, leaving it unchecked is then invalid.
- `name?: string`: With a name, the control is submitted with the form around it when it is checked.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `value?: string`: What is submitted. Default `"on"`, as a native checkbox's.
- `indeterminate?: boolean`: Neither checked nor unchecked: a parent of boxes that disagree.
- `parent?: boolean`: In a checkbox group with `allValues`: the box that stands for them all, written anywhere inside the group. It is checked when every one is, mixed when some are, and it is not submitted; its `aria-controls` names the boxes. A press from mixed checks them all, the next unchecks them all, and the next brings back the set they were left in (left all checked or none, a press goes between all and none); a disabled box keeps its state. Read once.
- `id?: string`: The id of the box's hidden native checkbox, not of the box: a `<label for>` names it. Inside a `Field`, that input takes the field's id instead.
- `@checked-change: (value: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as it is about to be checked or unchecked: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Checkbox.Root>` draws a `<span>`. Its props are above.
- `<Checkbox.Indicator>` draws a `<span>`. A dash while mixed and a tick while checked, from the slot's state: `<Checkbox.Indicator v-slot="{ state }">{{ state.indeterminate ? "–" : "✓" }}</Checkbox.Indicator>`.
    - `keepMounted?: boolean`: Keeps the mark in the page while the box is unchecked.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The box. It holds a hidden native checkbox, which a form and a label reach.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-indeterminate`: Present when it is neither checked nor unchecked.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-parent`: Present on the checkbox that stands for every box of its group.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
- indicator: The mark. In the page while the box is checked or indeterminate. `data-indeterminate` and `data-checked` say which mark to draw, a dash or a tick: in CSS (`[data-indeterminate]`), or from the part's state. Through its exit the box is already unchecked, and both are absent.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-indeterminate`: Present when it is neither checked nor unchecked.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.

### CheckboxGroup

```
import { CheckboxGroup } from "@kirana-ui/vue/checkbox-group"
```

Props:

- `value?: readonly string[]`: `v-model:value`. The values of the checked checkboxes, when the caller holds them.
- `defaultValue?: readonly string[]`: The values checked at the start, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `allValues?: readonly string[]`: The value of every checkbox of the group, for a checkbox marked `parent`: it is checked when all of them are, mixed when some are, and a press on it goes from the set they were left in to all, then none, then back. Its order names the boxes' elements (`<id>-0` …).
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disables every checkbox of the group.
- `id?: string`: The group's own id, and what its boxes' elements are named from (`<id>-0`, `<id>-1` …, by their place in `allValues`), which a parent box's `aria-controls` names. Inside a `Field`, the group takes the field's id instead.
- `@value-change: (value: string[], details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as a checkbox of the group is about to be checked or unchecked, with the values that would then be checked: `details.cancel()` keeps them as they were.

`<CheckboxGroup>` draws a `<div>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The group: `role="group"`, with its `id`. Name it with `aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby` naming a heading of your own; inside a `Field`, the field's label names it and its description describes it. A checkbox anywhere inside it with a `value` is checked while the group's value holds it; one marked `parent`, anywhere inside it too, stands for every value of `allValues`, and its `aria-controls` names their boxes.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### Collapsible

```
import { Collapsible } from "@kirana-ui/vue/collapsible"
```

Parts: `<Collapsible.Root>`, `<Collapsible.Trigger>`, `<Collapsible.Panel>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Collapsible.Root>
  <Collapsible.Trigger> (repeated)
  <Collapsible.Panel>
```

Props of its root:

- `open?: boolean`: `v-model:open`. Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Read once.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: its trigger does not open or close it.
- `@open-change: (value: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as it is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Collapsible.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Its props are above.
- `<Collapsible.Trigger>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<Collapsible.Panel>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `keepMounted?: boolean`: Keeps the closed panel in the page, `hidden`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: Groups the trigger and the panel.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of the panel's entrance, as on the panel.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through the panel's exit, as on the panel.
- trigger: The button that opens and closes the panel.
    - `data-panel-open`: Present when the panel is open.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- panel: The content. In the page while open, and through its exit's motion.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `--collapsible-panel-height`: The panel's content height while it opens or closes, `auto` once it is open.
    - `--collapsible-panel-width`: The panel's content width while it opens or closes, `auto` once it is open.

### ColorPicker

```
import { ColorPicker } from "@kirana-ui/vue/color-picker"
```

Parts: `<ColorPicker.Root>`, `<ColorPicker.Area>`, `<ColorPicker.AreaThumb>`, `<ColorPicker.ChannelSlider>`, `<ColorPicker.ChannelSliderTrack>`, `<ColorPicker.ChannelSliderThumb>`, `<ColorPicker.ChannelInput>`, `<ColorPicker.Swatch>`, `<ColorPicker.SwatchTrigger>`, `<ColorPicker.EyeDropperTrigger>`, `<ColorPicker.ValueText>`, `<ColorPicker.FormatTrigger>`.

Anatomy:

```
<ColorPicker.Root>
  <ColorPicker.Area>
    <ColorPicker.AreaThumb>
  <ColorPicker.ChannelSlider> (repeated)
    <ColorPicker.ChannelSliderTrack>
      <ColorPicker.ChannelSliderThumb>
    <ColorPicker.ChannelSliderThumb> (as above)
  <ColorPicker.ChannelInput> (repeated)
  <ColorPicker.Swatch> (repeated)
  <ColorPicker.SwatchTrigger> (repeated)
  <ColorPicker.EyeDropperTrigger>
  <ColorPicker.ValueText>
  <ColorPicker.FormatTrigger>
```

Props of its root:

- `value?: string`: `v-model:value`. The colour as text in `format`, when the caller holds it. Any format is read.
- `defaultValue?: string`: Read once. Default `#000000`.
- `format?: ColorFormat`: `v-model:format`. How the value is written, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultFormat?: ColorFormat`: Read once. Default `"hex"`.
- `alpha?: boolean`: Whether the opacity can be chosen. With it, the value always carries its alpha (`#rrggbbaa`, `rgba()`, `hsla()`); without it, never. Default false.
- `thumbAlignment?: "center" | "edge"`: Where a thumb is at the ends of its range. `"center"` (the default): its centre on the edge, so half of it lies outside. `"edge"`: its edge on the edge, so it stays inside.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable; still submitted with the form.
- `required?: boolean`: Needed by the form. A colour always has a value, so this only says so.
- `name?: string`: With a name, the value is submitted with the form around the picker.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the picker belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `getAriaValueText?: (text: string, thumb: ColorPickerThumb, color: Hsva) => string`: What assistive technology reads for a thumb, when the written one is not enough.
- `@value-change: (value: string, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Each step of a drag, each key, each colour typed or chosen: refusable.
- `@format-change: (value: ColorFormat, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: When the format trigger goes to the next format: refusable.
- `@value-committed: (value: string, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: The pointer let go, a key moved a thumb, a typed channel was left: the value to save.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<ColorPicker.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Its props are above.
- `<ColorPicker.Area>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<ColorPicker.AreaThumb>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<ColorPicker.ChannelSlider>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `channel: ColorPickerSliderChannel`: Required. The channel it moves: the hue, or the alpha.
    - `orientation?: Orientation`: The way its track runs. Default `horizontal`.
- `<ColorPicker.ChannelSliderTrack>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<ColorPicker.ChannelSliderThumb>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<ColorPicker.ChannelInput>` draws a `<input>`.
    - `channel: ColorPickerInputChannel`: Required. The channel it is typed in, or `hex` for the whole colour.
- `<ColorPicker.Swatch>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<ColorPicker.SwatchTrigger>` draws a `<button>`.
    - `value: string`: Required. The preset's colour, in any format: pressed, the colour is this one.
- `<ColorPicker.EyeDropperTrigger>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<ColorPicker.ValueText>` draws a `<span>`.
- `<ColorPicker.FormatTrigger>` draws a `<button>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: Groups the picker's parts. It holds the hidden input a form reads, and the colour for anything inside to paint with.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs a colour.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb of the picker.
    - `data-format="hex | rgb | hsl"`: How the value is written.
    - `--color`: The colour, with its alpha.
- area: The two-dimensional field a pointer presses and drags on: saturation across, the way the text runs, and brightness up. A design paints it from its hue.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs a colour.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds this part's thumb.
    - `--hue-color`: The colour's hue at full saturation and brightness.
- areaThumb: What is dragged in the area, and what the arrows move: a slider in two dimensions to assistive technology, its text saying both. Its place is written on it.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs a colour.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds this part's thumb.
    - `--saturation`: Its place across, as a share of the area: the saturation.
    - `--brightness`: Its place up, as a share of the area: the brightness.
    - `--color`: The colour under it, without its alpha.
- channelSlider: What a pointer presses and drags on to move the hue or the alpha. It holds the track and the thumb. It takes `channel` and `orientation`.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs a colour.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds this part's thumb.
    - `data-channel="hue | alpha"`: The channel the slider moves.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the track runs.
- channelSliderTrack: The channel's whole range: what a design paints the hues or the alpha on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs a colour.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds this part's thumb.
    - `data-channel="hue | alpha"`: The channel the slider moves.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the track runs.
    - `--color`: The colour without its alpha: the end of an alpha track.
    - `--hue-color`: The colour's hue at full saturation and brightness.
- channelSliderThumb: What is dragged, and what the keyboard moves: a slider to assistive technology, its range 0 to 360 for the hue and 0 to 100 for the alpha. Its place on the track is written on it.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs a colour.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds this part's thumb.
    - `data-channel="hue | alpha"`: The channel the slider moves.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the track runs.
    - `--color`: The colour under it: the pure hue, or the colour at its alpha.
- channelInput: A text input for one channel (`hex`, `red`, `green`, `blue`, `hue`, `saturation`, `lightness`, `alpha`). What is typed is taken when it is a colour or a number in range, and put back when focus leaves while it is not.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs a colour.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb of the picker.
    - `data-channel="hex | red | green | blue | hue | saturation | lightness | alpha"`: The channel the input is typed in.
- swatch: Shows the current colour.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs a colour.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb of the picker.
    - `--color`: The colour, with its alpha.
- swatchTrigger: A preset colour, given as `value`: pressed, the colour is this one.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs a colour.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb of the picker.
    - `data-selected`: Present while the colour is this one.
    - `--color`: The preset's colour, with its alpha.
- eyeDropperTrigger: Picks a colour from the screen with the browser's eye dropper. Hidden where the browser has none, and on a server.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs a colour.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb of the picker.
- valueText: The colour, written in its format.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs a colour.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb of the picker.
    - `data-format="hex | rgb | hsl"`: How the value is written.
- formatTrigger: Goes to the next format: hex, then rgb, then hsl.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs a colour.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb of the picker.
    - `data-format="hex | rgb | hsl"`: How the value is written.

### Combobox

```
import { Combobox } from "@kirana-ui/vue/combobox"
```

Parts: `<Combobox.Root>`, `<Combobox.Input>`, `<Combobox.Trigger>`, `<Combobox.Value>`, `<Combobox.Clear>`, `<Combobox.Chips>`, `<Combobox.Chip>`, `<Combobox.ChipRemove>`, `<Combobox.Portal>`, `<Combobox.Backdrop>`, `<Combobox.Positioner>`, `<Combobox.Popup>`, `<Combobox.List>`, `<Combobox.Collection>`, `<Combobox.Group>`, `<Combobox.GroupLabel>`, `<Combobox.Separator>`, `<Combobox.Item>`, `<Combobox.ItemIndicator>`, `<Combobox.Empty>`, `<Combobox.Status>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Combobox.Root>
  <Combobox.Input>
  <Combobox.Trigger>
    <Combobox.Value> (optional)
  <Combobox.Portal>
    <Combobox.Backdrop> (optional)
    <Combobox.Positioner>
      <Combobox.Popup>
        <Combobox.Input> (as above)
        <Combobox.List> (optional)
          <Combobox.Collection> (optional)
            <Combobox.Item> (repeated, as above)
            <Combobox.Group> (optional, repeated, as above)
          <Combobox.Group> (optional, repeated)
            <Combobox.Collection> (optional, as above)
            <Combobox.Item> (repeated)
              <Combobox.ItemIndicator>
            <Combobox.GroupLabel>
          <Combobox.Separator> (repeated)
        <Combobox.Collection> (optional, as above)
        <Combobox.Empty>
        <Combobox.Status> (optional)
  <Combobox.Popup> (as above)
  <Combobox.Status> (optional, as above)
  <Combobox.Clear>
  <Combobox.Chips>
    <Combobox.Input> (as above)
    <Combobox.Chip> (repeated)
      <Combobox.ChipRemove>
```

Props of its root:

- `presentation?: Presentation`: How the list opens. `"sheet"`: from the bottom edge, not placed against the input, modal with a backdrop, swiped down or pressed outside to close; the input then goes in the popup, at its head. `"auto"`: decided each time it opens, a sheet when the pointer is coarse and the viewport narrower than `sheetBelow`. Default `"popup"`. Not with `inline`.
- `sheetBelow?: number`: With `presentation: "auto"`: the viewport's width, in CSS pixels, under which a coarse pointer opens a sheet. Default 640.
- `value?: (Multiple extends true ? readonly Value[] : Value | null)`: `v-model:value`. The chosen value; `null` is "none". With `multiple`, the chosen values, in the order they were chosen.
- `defaultValue?: (Multiple extends true ? readonly Value[] : Value | null)`: The value it starts with (with `multiple`, the values), when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `inputValue?: string`: `v-model:inputValue`. What the input says.
- `defaultInputValue?: string`: The text the input starts with, when the caller does not hold `inputValue`. Read once.
- `open?: boolean`: `v-model:open`. Whether the list is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether the list starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Its value can be read and not changed. The list still opens and can be gone through, by the pointer and the arrows, but no press and no Enter chooses; nothing typed is taken, and its clear and chip buttons do nothing. It keeps focus, and its value is still submitted.
- `name?: string`: With a name, the value is submitted with the form around it.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `items?: readonly ComboboxItemData<Value>[] | readonly ComboboxGroupData<Value>[] | Readonly<Record<string, string>>`: The values with their labels: a list of them, groups of them (`{ value, items }`, `value` the group's name), or, for values that are text, the labels by value (`{ apple: "Apple" }`). The input shows a value by its label from here before the list has ever been opened. With the items written in the markup that is all it is for. With a `Collection` it is the list itself: the combobox filters it by what is typed, and the `Collection` draws what is left.
- `itemToStringLabel?: (value: Value) => string`: For values that are objects: the text the input shows for one, and what an item drawn with no text of its own is filtered by. Without it, an object's own `label` names it, then the label `items` gives it, then the item's text in the markup.
- `itemToStringValue?: (value: Value) => string`: For values that are objects: the text the form is sent for one. Without it, the `value` of an object shaped `{ value, label }` is sent, and any other object as JSON.
- `filter?: ((label: string, query: string) => boolean) | null`: Whether an item is shown for what was typed. Default: its label holds the text, without regard to case. `null`: every item is shown, and the caller draws the ones it wants (or gives the `items` it wants, when they are loaded for what was typed).
- `values?: readonly Value[]`: `v-model:values`. With `multiple`: the chosen values.
- `defaultValues?: readonly Value[]`: With `multiple`: the values it starts with.
- `required?: boolean`: In a field, "none" is then wrong.
- `inline?: boolean`: The list is always in the page, under the input, with no popup: a command palette. An item chosen is told to the caller, and the input keeps what was typed.
- `virtualized?: ListCollection`: Every row, when only some are in the page (a virtualizer draws the ones in view). The caller then filters: the collection is what is left, and each item is given its `index`.
- `autoHighlight?: boolean`: The first item shown for what was typed is highlighted as one types, so Enter chooses it. Off by default: typing then highlights nothing, and Enter chooses once an arrow or the pointer has gone to an item. Either way a list opened with nothing typed is on its chosen item, if it has one.
- `multiple?: Multiple`: Several values: `value` and `@value-change` then hold a list. Read once.
- `@value-change: (value: Multiple extends true ? Value[] : Value | null, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as a value is about to be chosen or cleared (with `multiple`, added or taken away, with the values there would then be): `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `@values-change: (value: Value[], details: ChangeDetails) => void`: With `multiple`: heard as a value is about to be added or taken away.
- `@input-value-change: (value: string, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as the input's text is about to change: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `@open-change: (value: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as the list is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Combobox.Root>` draws no element. Generic: `<Value = unknown, Multiple extends boolean | undefined = false>`. `Multiple` is read from `multiple`: with it, `value` and `@value-change` hold a list. Its props are above.
- `<Combobox.Input>` draws a `<input>`.
- `<Combobox.Trigger>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<Combobox.Value>` draws no element. The chosen value's label, or a placeholder while nothing is chosen, for a button that is the combobox (its input inside the popup). With several values, their labels with commas between. Its default slot is also given `value: Value | null`, `label: string`, `values: readonly Value[]`, `labels: readonly string[]`.
    - `placeholder?: string`: What it shows while nothing is chosen.
- `<Combobox.Clear>` draws a `<button>`.
    - `keepMounted?: boolean`: Keeps the button in the page while there is nothing to clear.
- `<Combobox.Chips>` draws a `<div>`. With several values: what holds the chips and the input, and what the list is placed against.
- `<Combobox.Chip>` draws a `<span>`.
    - `value: unknown`: Required. The chosen value it stands for: what its remove button takes away.
- `<Combobox.ChipRemove>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<Combobox.Portal>` draws no element. A portal takes nothing: where it is drawn is its `PortalProvider`'s to say.
- `<Combobox.Backdrop>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Combobox.Positioner>` draws a `<div>`. A positioner's own props: where its popup goes, and what it is placed against. Takes the positioner options ("Positioner options", above).
- `<Combobox.Popup>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Combobox.List>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Combobox.Collection>` draws no element. Draws the list from the root's `items`: its content once for each item left for what was typed, or for each group that has items left; given a group, for each of that group's items left. The root then filters, and no item hides itself. Its default slot is also given `entry: ComboboxEntry`.
    - `of?: ComboboxEntry`: A group the root's `items` gave: its items left are then what is drawn.
- `<Combobox.Group>` draws a `<div>`. Items that belong together, named by their label. Hidden while none is shown.
- `<Combobox.GroupLabel>` draws a `<div>`. The name of a group. Outside a group it is plain text, and names nothing.
- `<Combobox.Separator>` draws a `<div>`. A line between groups.
- `<Combobox.Item>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be chosen, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What is filtered and what the input shows; the item's text when left out.
    - `index?: number`: Its place among all the rows, in a virtualized list.
    - `value: unknown`: Required. What the combobox's value is while this item is the chosen one.
- `<Combobox.ItemIndicator>` draws a `<span>`. A mark an item shows while it is the chosen one.
    - `keepMounted?: boolean`: Keeps the mark in the page while its item is not chosen.
- `<Combobox.Empty>` draws a `<div>`. What is shown when no item is.
- `<Combobox.Status>` draws a `<div>`. Says how the list stands ("3 results", "Loading") to software that reads the page, as its text changes. It stays in the page while its text changes: inside the popup, or beside the input.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- input: The text input. What is typed filters the list, which is placed against it, or against the chips' box when it is in one. Inside the popup, it takes focus while the popup is open.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the list is open.
    - `data-pressed`: Present while its popup is open: it stays pressed, as a button held down.
    - `data-popup-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end | none"`: While the list is in the page: the side of the trigger it is on, after any flip; `none` when it lies over the trigger. Not said while it opens as a sheet.
    - `data-list-empty`: Present when no item is shown for what was typed, once the list is in the page.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
- trigger: A button that opens and closes the list. With the input inside the popup it is the combobox: a stop for Tab, and what the popup is placed against.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the list is open.
    - `data-pressed`: Present while its popup is open: it stays pressed, as a button held down.
    - `data-popup-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end | none"`: While the list is in the page: the side of the trigger it is on, after any flip; `none` when it lies over the trigger. Not said while it opens as a sheet.
    - `data-list-empty`: Present when no item is shown for what was typed, once the list is in the page.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
- backdrop: The layer over the page behind the list: a press on it closes the list.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-presentation="popup | sheet"`: How the list opened: placed against its trigger, or as a sheet from the bottom edge.
    - `data-swiping`: Present while the sheet is dragged.
    - `data-swipe-dismiss`: Present once a drag has closed it.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-x`: As a sheet: how far it has been dragged across, always 0px.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-y`: As a sheet: how far it has been dragged down.
    - `--drawer-swipe-progress`: As a sheet: how far it has been dragged, of its own height: 0 to 1.
- positioner: Places the list against the input: against the chips' box when the input is in one, the button when the input is inside the popup, or its own `anchor`. It carries the geometry. As a sheet it is not placed, and carries none.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-presentation="popup | sheet"`: How the list opened: placed against its trigger, or as a sheet from the bottom edge.
    - `data-anchor-hidden`: Present while the anchor is out of view: scrolled away, or clipped by a box around it.
    - `data-empty`: Present when no item is shown for what was typed.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
- popup: The list of items. With a `list` inside, what holds it: a dialog around an input and the list. As a sheet, a design moves it by what it says of the drag, and gives it `touch-action: none` where a finger drags it.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-presentation="popup | sheet"`: How the list opened: placed against its trigger, or as a sheet from the bottom edge.
    - `data-swiping`: Present while the sheet is dragged.
    - `data-swipe-dismiss`: Present once a drag has closed it.
    - `data-anchor-hidden`: Present while the anchor is out of view: scrolled away, or clipped by a box around it.
    - `data-empty`: Present when no item is shown for what was typed.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-x`: As a sheet: how far it has been dragged across, always 0px.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-y`: As a sheet: how far it has been dragged down.
    - `--drawer-swipe-progress`: As a sheet: how far it has been dragged, of its own height: 0 to 1.
    - `--drawer-swipe-strength`: As a sheet, once let go: 0.1 to 1, the share of the design's own time it should take to come to rest.
- list: The items' own box inside the popup, when the popup holds more than items (an input): it is then the listbox.
    - `data-empty`: Present when no item is shown for what was typed.
- item: One choice in the list.
    - `data-selected`: Present on the chosen item.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- clear: A button that empties the input and the value. It is in the page while there is something to clear (the text, for an autocomplete; else what is chosen), and through its exit; `keepMounted` keeps it there.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the list is open.
    - `data-visible`: Present while there is something to clear.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
- chip: One chosen value. The arrows reach it from the start of the input, and Backspace or Delete on it takes it away.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- chipRemove: A chip's button that takes its value away.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### Command

```
import { Command } from "@kirana-ui/vue/command"
```

Parts: `<Command.Root>`, `<Command.Input>`, `<Command.List>`, `<Command.Empty>`, `<Command.Group>`, `<Command.GroupHeading>`, `<Command.Item>`, `<Command.Separator>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Command.Root>
  <Command.Input>
  <Command.List>
    <Command.Empty>
    <Command.Group> (optional, repeated)
      <Command.GroupHeading>
      <Command.Item> (repeated)
    <Command.Separator> (repeated)
```

Props of its root:

- `inputValue?: string`: `v-model:inputValue`. What the input says.
- `defaultInputValue?: string`: The text the input starts with, when the caller does not hold `inputValue`. Read once. Default `""`.
- `filter?: ((label: string, query: string, keywords: readonly string[]) => boolean) | null`: Whether an item is shown for what was typed. Default: its label or one of its keywords holds the text, without regard to case. `null`: every item is shown, and the caller draws the ones it wants.
- `loop?: boolean`: Whether a step past an end of the list goes round to the other.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: nothing can be typed or chosen.
- `autoHighlight?: boolean`: Whether the first item shown is highlighted from the start and again whenever the text changes, so Enter does it with no arrow key first, as a command palette is used. Default: `true`. With `false`, nothing is highlighted until the input has focus or an arrow or the pointer moves to an item.
- `@input-value-change: (value: string, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as the input's text is about to change: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `@select: (value: string, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: An item was chosen: its value.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Command.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Its props are above.
- `<Command.Input>` draws a `<input>`.
- `<Command.List>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Command.Empty>` draws a `<div>`. What is shown when no item is.
- `<Command.Group>` draws a `<div>`. Items under a heading. Hidden while none of them is shown.
- `<Command.GroupHeading>` draws a `<div>`. A group's name.
- `<Command.Item>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be chosen, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What is filtered; the item's text when left out.
    - `keywords?: readonly string[]`: Other words the item answers to.
    - `value?: string`: What `@select` is told when this item is chosen; its `label`, or its text, when left out.
- `<Command.Separator>` draws a `<div>`. A line between groups. Hidden while something is typed.
    - `alwaysRender?: boolean`: Keeps the line while something is typed.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: A list of commands with the input that filters it.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- input: The text input. What is typed filters the list; focus stays in it.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- list: The commands.
    - `data-empty`: Present when no item is shown for what was typed.
- item: One command.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### ContextMenu

```
import { ContextMenu } from "@kirana-ui/vue/context-menu"
```

Parts: `<ContextMenu.Root>`, `<ContextMenu.Trigger>`, `<ContextMenu.Portal>`, `<ContextMenu.Positioner>`, `<ContextMenu.Popup>`, `<ContextMenu.Arrow>`, `<ContextMenu.Item>`, `<ContextMenu.LinkItem>`, `<ContextMenu.Group>`, `<ContextMenu.GroupLabel>`, `<ContextMenu.Separator>`, `<ContextMenu.CheckboxItem>`, `<ContextMenu.CheckboxItemIndicator>`, `<ContextMenu.RadioGroup>`, `<ContextMenu.RadioItem>`, `<ContextMenu.RadioItemIndicator>`, `<ContextMenu.SubmenuRoot>`, `<ContextMenu.SubmenuTrigger>`.

Anatomy:

```
<ContextMenu.Root>
  <ContextMenu.Trigger>
  <ContextMenu.Portal>
    <ContextMenu.Positioner>
      <ContextMenu.Popup>
        <ContextMenu.Arrow>
        <ContextMenu.Group> (optional, repeated)
          <ContextMenu.Item> (repeated)
          <ContextMenu.LinkItem> (repeated)
          <ContextMenu.GroupLabel>
          <ContextMenu.CheckboxItem> (repeated)
            <ContextMenu.CheckboxItemIndicator>
          <ContextMenu.RadioGroup> (repeated)
            <ContextMenu.RadioItem> (repeated)
              <ContextMenu.RadioItemIndicator>
          <ContextMenu.SubmenuRoot> (repeated)
            <ContextMenu.Portal> (as above)
            <ContextMenu.SubmenuTrigger>
        <ContextMenu.Separator> (repeated)
```

Props of its root:

- `open?: boolean`: `v-model:open`. Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether it starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `disabled?: boolean`: The trigger cannot be pressed; a submenu's is passed over.
- `loopFocus?: boolean`: Whether the arrows go round from the last item to the first. Default: they do.
- `loop?: boolean`: Whether the arrows wrap from the last item to the first.
- `modal?: boolean`: Holds the page while the menu is open: its scroll is locked, and a press outside closes the menu and reaches nothing. Default: it does not. Not for a submenu.
- `@open-change: (value: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as it is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<ContextMenu.Root>` draws no element. Holds the menu: whether it is open. Its props are above.
- `<ContextMenu.Trigger>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<ContextMenu.Portal>` draws no element. A portal takes nothing: where it is drawn is its `PortalProvider`'s to say.
- `<ContextMenu.Positioner>` draws a `<div>`. A positioner's own props: where its popup goes, and what it is placed against. Takes the positioner options ("Positioner options", above).
- `<ContextMenu.Popup>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<ContextMenu.Arrow>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<ContextMenu.Item>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be pressed, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What typing matches; the item's text when left out.
    - `closeOnSelect?: boolean`: Whether choosing the item closes the menu. Default: it does for an item, and does not for a checkbox or a radio item.
    - `closeOnClick?: boolean`: Whether choosing the item closes the menu.
- `<ContextMenu.LinkItem>` draws a `<a>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be pressed, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What typing matches; the item's text when left out.
    - `closeOnSelect?: boolean`: Whether choosing the item closes the menu. Default: it does for an item, and does not for a checkbox or a radio item.
    - `closeOnClick?: boolean`: Whether choosing the item closes the menu.
- `<ContextMenu.Group>` draws a `<div>`. Items that belong together, named by their label.
- `<ContextMenu.GroupLabel>` draws a `<div>`. The name of a group. Outside a group it is plain text, and names nothing.
- `<ContextMenu.Separator>` draws a `<div>`. A line between items.
- `<ContextMenu.CheckboxItem>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be pressed, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What typing matches; the item's text when left out.
    - `closeOnSelect?: boolean`: Whether choosing the item closes the menu. Default: it does for an item, and does not for a checkbox or a radio item.
    - `closeOnClick?: boolean`: Whether choosing the item closes the menu.
    - `checked?: boolean`: `v-model:checked`. Whether the item is checked, when the caller holds it.
    - `defaultChecked?: boolean`: Whether the item starts checked, when the caller does not hold `checked`. Read once.
    - `@checked-change: (value: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as the item is about to be checked or unchecked: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `<ContextMenu.CheckboxItemIndicator>` draws a `<span>`.
    - `keepMounted?: boolean`: Keeps the mark in the page while the item is unchecked.
- `<ContextMenu.RadioGroup>` draws a `<div>`. Generic: `<Value = unknown>`.
    - `value?: Value | null`: `v-model:value`. The chosen value; `null` is "none".
    - `defaultValue?: Value | null`: The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables every item of the group.
    - `@value-change: (value: Value, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Told an item's own value, never `null`: a press chooses, and nothing takes the choice back.
- `<ContextMenu.RadioItem>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be pressed, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What typing matches; the item's text when left out.
    - `closeOnSelect?: boolean`: Whether choosing the item closes the menu. Default: it does for an item, and does not for a checkbox or a radio item.
    - `closeOnClick?: boolean`: Whether choosing the item closes the menu.
    - `value: unknown`: Required. What the group's value is while this item is the chosen one.
- `<ContextMenu.RadioItemIndicator>` draws a `<span>`.
    - `keepMounted?: boolean`: Keeps the mark in the page while its item is not the chosen one.
- `<ContextMenu.SubmenuRoot>` draws no element. A submenu: it holds the item that opens it and a portal, positioner and popup of its own.
    - `open?: boolean`: `v-model:open`. Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
    - `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether it starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: The trigger cannot be pressed; a submenu's is passed over.
    - `loopFocus?: boolean`: Whether the arrows go round from the last item to the first. Default: they do.
    - `loop?: boolean`: Whether the arrows wrap from the last item to the first.
    - `modal?: boolean`: Holds the page while the menu is open: its scroll is locked, and a press outside closes the menu and reaches nothing. Default: it does not. Not for a submenu.
    - `@open-change: (value: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as it is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `<ContextMenu.SubmenuTrigger>` draws a `<div>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- trigger: The area a secondary press, or a long press on a touch screen, opens the menu in.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the menu is open.
    - `data-pressed`: Present while its popup is open: it stays pressed, as a button held down.
- positioner: Places the menu against its trigger. It carries the geometry.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-anchor-hidden`: Present while the anchor is out of view: scrolled away, or clipped by a box around it.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
    - `--positioner-width`: The popup's width, as its content lays it out: a design gives the positioner `width: var(--positioner-width)` to animate a change of size.
    - `--positioner-height`: The popup's height, as its content lays it out: a design gives the positioner `height: var(--positioner-height)` to animate a change of size.
- popup: The menu itself: the list of items.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-instant="click | dismiss | group"`: Present when it opened or closed in a way that should skip the motion: `click` when the keyboard pressed its trigger or an item, `dismiss` when Escape closed it, `group` when focus or the pointer went from one menu of a bar to another.
- arrow: An element that points at the trigger.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-uncentered`: Present when the arrow cannot sit at the trigger's centre.
- item: An action. Choosing it closes the menu.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- linkItem: An item that is a link. Choosing it follows the link and closes the menu.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- checkboxItem: An item that is checked or not. Choosing it leaves the menu open.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- checkboxItemIndicator: A mark a checkbox item shows while it is checked.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
- radioGroup: Radio items of which one is chosen.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- radioItem: One choice of a radio group. Choosing it leaves the menu open.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- radioItemIndicator: A mark a radio item shows while it is the chosen one.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
- submenuTrigger: An item that opens a menu beside it.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when its menu is open.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### DateField

```
import { DateField } from "@kirana-ui/vue/date-field"
```

Parts: `<DateField.Root>`, `<DateField.Segments>`, `<DateField.Segment>`, `<DateField.Input>`.

Anatomy:

```
<DateField.Root>
  <DateField.Segments>
    <DateField.Segment> (repeated)
  <DateField.Input>
```

Props of its root:

- `value?: IsoDate | null`: `v-model:value`. The day typed, once all of it is; `null` until then.
- `defaultValue?: IsoDate | null`: The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `locale?: string`: The language and region that order the day, the month and the year and put what stands between them (`"en-US"`: month/day/year). Give it: a server does not know the reader's. Default `"en-US"`.
- `min?: IsoDate`: The first and the last day it takes: outside them it says it is invalid.
- `max?: IsoDate`: The last day it takes.
- `calendarSystem?: CalendarSystem`: The calendar its parts are typed in, when it is not the Gregorian one: an instance from `@internationalized/date` (`new PersianCalendar()`), as a calendar takes it. Its days, months, years and eras are the parts' ranges; the value is still an ISO day. In a calendar with several eras (Japanese, Minguo, Ethiopic), the era is a part of its own.
- `placeholders?: Partial<Record<DateUnit, string>>`: What an empty part shows. Default: `dd`, `mm`, `yyyy`, `era`.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable.
- `required?: boolean`: Needed: in a `Field`, leaving it empty is then invalid.
- `name?: string`: The name it is submitted under, by its hidden input.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form it belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `@value-change: (value: string | null, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as the day is about to change, once all of it is typed or as it is cleared: `details.cancel()` keeps the value as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<DateField.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Its props are above.
- `<DateField.Segments>` draws no element. The date's segments, in the locale's order: each is given to draw. Its default slot is also given `segment: DateFieldSegment`.
- `<DateField.Segment>` draws a `<span>`.
    - `segment: DateFieldSegment`: Required. The piece it draws, as `DateField.Segments` gives it.
- `<DateField.Input>` draws a `<input>`. The hidden input it is submitted by.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The field: a group of the date's parts.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when its value cannot be changed.
    - `data-invalid`: Present when the date is outside what it takes, or is asked for and half typed.
- segment: One piece of the date: a part that is typed, or what stands between two.
    - `data-segment="era | day | month | year | literal"`: Which piece it is: the era only in a calendar of several eras.
    - `data-placeholder`: Present on a part that is empty.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-invalid`: Present when the date is outside what it takes, or is asked for and half typed.

### DatePicker

```
import { DatePicker } from "@kirana-ui/vue/date-picker"
```

Parts: `<DatePicker.Root>`, `<DatePicker.Field>`, `<DatePicker.Segments>`, `<DatePicker.Segment>`, `<DatePicker.Input>`, `<DatePicker.Trigger>`, `<DatePicker.Portal>`, `<DatePicker.Positioner>`, `<DatePicker.Popup>`, `<DatePicker.Calendar>`, `<DatePicker.Heading>`, `<DatePicker.Previous>`, `<DatePicker.Next>`, `<DatePicker.Months>`, `<DatePicker.Grid>`, `<DatePicker.Weekdays>`, `<DatePicker.HeadCell>`, `<DatePicker.Weeks>`, `<DatePicker.Cell>`, `<DatePicker.Day>`, `<DatePicker.Clear>`, `<DatePicker.Preset>`.

Anatomy:

```
<DatePicker.Root>
  <DatePicker.Field> (repeated)
    <DatePicker.Segments>
      <DatePicker.Segment> (repeated)
    <DatePicker.Input>
  <DatePicker.Trigger>
  <DatePicker.Portal>
    <DatePicker.Positioner>
      <DatePicker.Popup>
        <DatePicker.Calendar>
          <DatePicker.Months> (optional)
            <DatePicker.Heading>
            <DatePicker.Grid>
              <DatePicker.Weekdays>
                <DatePicker.HeadCell> (repeated)
              <DatePicker.Weeks>
                <DatePicker.Cell> (repeated)
                  <DatePicker.Day>
          <DatePicker.Previous>
          <DatePicker.Next>
  <DatePicker.Clear> (optional)
  <DatePicker.Preset> (optional, repeated)
```

Props of its root:

- `value?: DatePickerValueOf<Mode>`: `v-model:value`. The day, typed or picked; with `mode: "range"` a first and a last day, each typed in its own field or both picked in the one calendar. `null` for none.
- `defaultValue?: DatePickerValueOf<Mode>`: The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `mode?: Mode`: One day (the default), or a first and a last (`"range"`): two fields, `DatePicker.Field` with `range="start"` and `range="end"`, and the calendar in range mode, which stays open until the range is whole. Read once.
- `open?: boolean`: `v-model:open`. Whether the calendar is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether the calendar starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `locale?: string`: The language and region of the field and the calendar. Give it: a server does not know.
- `min?: IsoDate`: The first and the last day that can be typed or picked.
- `max?: IsoDate`: The last day that can be typed or picked.
- `isDateUnavailable?: (date: IsoDate) => boolean`: Days that cannot be picked in the calendar.
- `calendarSystem?: CalendarSystem`: The calendar its months are laid out in and its field typed in, when it is not the Gregorian one. The value is an ISO day whatever it is.
- `fixedWeeks?: boolean`: Always six rows of days.
- `months?: number`: How many months the calendar shows side by side (1 by default).
- `pagedNavigation?: boolean`: With several `months`: whether Previous and Next turn them all rather than one month.
- `month?: IsoDate`: `v-model:month`. The month the calendar shows (the first, with several), when the caller holds it.
- `defaultMonth?: IsoDate`: The month the calendar starts on, when the caller does not hold `month`. Read once.
- `placeholders?: Partial<Record<DateUnit, string>>`: What an empty part of the field shows.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable.
- `required?: boolean`: Needed: in a `Field`, leaving it empty is then invalid, and the day picked, pressed again in the calendar, stays picked. Without it, that press empties the field and closes the calendar.
- `name?: string`: The name it is submitted under.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form it belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `@value-change: (value: DatePickerValueOf<Mode>, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as the value is about to change, typed, picked, pressed or cleared: `details.cancel()` keeps the value as it was. A range is heard as each end comes, its other end `null` until it is there too.
- `@open-change: (value: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as the calendar is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `@month-change: (value: string, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as the calendar is about to show another month, a day typed or picked included: its first day. `details.cancel()` keeps the month as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<DatePicker.Root>` draws no element. Generic: `<Mode extends DatePickerMode = "single">`. `value` and its events are typed by `mode`: a day, or a range. Its props are above.
- `<DatePicker.Field>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `range?: "start" | "end"`: With `mode="range"`: which day of the range it is typed in, the first (`"start"`, the default) or the last (`"end"`).
- `<DatePicker.Segments>` draws no element. The date's segments, in the locale's order: each is given to draw. Its default slot is also given `segment: DateFieldSegment`.
- `<DatePicker.Segment>` draws a `<span>`.
    - `segment: DateFieldSegment`: Required. The piece it draws, as `DateField.Segments` gives it.
- `<DatePicker.Input>` draws a `<input>`. The hidden input it is submitted by.
- `<DatePicker.Trigger>` draws a `<button>`.
    - `openOnHover?: boolean`: Whether the pointer resting on the trigger opens the popover too. A press and the keyboard still open it, and a press on one the pointer opened keeps it open. Default `false`.
    - `delay?: number`: How long the pointer rests on the trigger before the popover opens, in milliseconds. Default 300.
    - `closeDelay?: number`: How long after the pointer leaves a popover it opened closes, in milliseconds. Default 0.
- `<DatePicker.Portal>` draws no element. A portal takes nothing: where it is drawn is its `PortalProvider`'s to say.
- `<DatePicker.Positioner>` draws a `<div>`. A positioner's own props: where its popup goes, and what it is placed against. Takes the positioner options ("Positioner options", above).
- `<DatePicker.Popup>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<DatePicker.Calendar>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<DatePicker.Heading>` draws a `<div>`. Names the month shown. Read out when it changes.
- `<DatePicker.Previous>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<DatePicker.Next>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<DatePicker.Months>` draws no element. The months shown, with several: each is given to draw its heading and its grid. It draws no element, and is left out for one month. Its default slot is also given `month: CalendarMonth`.
- `<DatePicker.Grid>` draws a `<table>`. The table of a month's days: a grid the arrows move in, from one month shown into the next.
