- `<DatePicker.Weekdays>` draws no element. The days of the week: each is given to draw its head cell. Its default slot is also given `weekday: CalendarWeekday`.
- `<DatePicker.HeadCell>` draws a `<th>`. A column's heading: a day of the week.
    - `weekday: CalendarWeekday`: Required. The day of the week it names, as `Calendar.Weekdays` gives it.
- `<DatePicker.Weeks>` draws no element. The weeks of the month shown: each is given to draw its row of days. Its default slot is also given `week: readonly CalendarDay[]`.
- `<DatePicker.Cell>` draws a `<td>`.
    - `date: string`: Required. The day it is for, as a week of `Calendar.Weeks` gives it.
- `<DatePicker.Day>` draws a `<button>`.
    - `date?: string`: The day it is the button of. Left out, the `Calendar.Cell`'s it is inside.
- `<DatePicker.Clear>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<DatePicker.Preset>` draws a `<button>`.
    - `value: string | DatePickerRange`: Required. The value its press gives: a day, or with `mode="range"` a range.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- field: The field a day is typed in: with `mode: "range"`, one for the first day (`range="start"`) and one for the last (`range="end"`).
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when its value cannot be changed.
    - `data-invalid`: Present when the date is outside what it takes, or is asked for and half typed.
- segment: One piece of the date: a part that is typed, or what stands between two.
    - `data-segment="era | day | month | year | literal"`: Which piece it is: the era only in a calendar of several eras.
    - `data-placeholder`: Present on a part that is empty.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-invalid`: Present when the date is outside what it takes, or is asked for and half typed.
- trigger: The button that opens the popover, and what it is placed against.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the popover is open.
    - `data-pressed`: Present while the popover a press on this trigger opened is open: it stays pressed, as a button held down.
- positioner: Places the popup against the trigger. It carries the geometry.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-anchor-hidden`: Present while the anchor is out of view: scrolled away, or clipped by a box around it.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
    - `--positioner-width`: The popup's width, as its content lays it out: a design gives the positioner `width: var(--positioner-width)` to animate a change of size.
    - `--positioner-height`: The popup's height, as its content lays it out: a design gives the positioner `height: var(--positioner-height)` to animate a change of size.
- popup: The popover itself.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-instant="click | dismiss"`: Present when it opened or closed in a way that should skip the motion: `click` when the keyboard pressed the trigger, `dismiss` when Escape closed it.
    - `--popup-width`: Its width: `auto`, and while its content changes size, the old width and then the new one, for a transition between them.
    - `--popup-height`: Its height: `auto`, and while its content changes size, the old height and then the new one, for a transition between them.
- calendar: The calendar.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when its value cannot be changed.
- previous: Shows the month before.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- next: Shows the month after.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- cell: A day's cell.
    - `data-selected`: Present on a chosen day, on every day of a chosen range, and on each day of a list. Also on a copy of one (a day of the month before or after, shown in its own month too), which is drawn as the day is but has no aria-selected.
    - `data-today`: Present on today.
    - `data-outside-month`: Present on the days of the month before and after that fill the first and last weeks.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-unavailable`: Present on a day that cannot be chosen.
    - `data-range-start`: Present on the first day of a range, and on a copy of it.
    - `data-range-end`: Present on the last day of a range, and on a copy of it.
- day: The button for a day.
    - `data-selected`: Present on a chosen day, on every day of a chosen range, and on each day of a list. Also on a copy of one (a day of the month before or after, shown in its own month too), which is drawn as the day is but has no aria-selected.
    - `data-today`: Present on today.
    - `data-outside-month`: Present on the days of the month before and after that fill the first and last weeks.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-unavailable`: Present on a day that cannot be chosen.
    - `data-range-start`: Present on the first day of a range, and on a copy of it.
    - `data-range-end`: Present on the last day of a range, and on a copy of it.
- clear: Empties the value, and gives focus to the field. Disabled while there is none.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- preset: Makes the value the day, or the range, it is given. Pressed while the value is that.
    - `data-pressed`: Present while the value is the one it gives.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### Dialog

```
import { Dialog } from "@kirana-ui/vue/dialog"
```

Parts: `<Dialog.Root>`, `<Dialog.Trigger>`, `<Dialog.Portal>`, `<Dialog.Backdrop>`, `<Dialog.Viewport>`, `<Dialog.Popup>`, `<Dialog.Title>`, `<Dialog.Description>`, `<Dialog.Close>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Dialog.Root>
  <Dialog.Trigger>
  <Dialog.Portal>
    <Dialog.Backdrop>
    <Dialog.Viewport> (optional)
      <Dialog.Popup>
        <Dialog.Title>
        <Dialog.Description>
        <Dialog.Close>
```

Props of its root:

- `open?: boolean`: `v-model:open`. Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether it starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `modal?: boolean`: Blocks the page behind it and traps focus. Default `true`.
- `disablePointerDismissal?: boolean`: Keeps it open when the pointer presses outside it. Default `false`. Escape always closes it: a caller who must keep it open cancels the change whose `details.reason` is `"escape-key"`.
- `closeOnOutsidePress?: boolean`: Whether a press outside closes it. Default `true`.
- `dismissible?: boolean`: Whether a press outside closes it. Default `true`.
- `@open-change: (value: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as it is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Dialog.Root>` draws no element. Holds the dialog: whether it is open. Its props are above.
- `<Dialog.Trigger>` draws a `<button>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: It cannot be pressed: the button is disabled, and says so (`data-disabled`).
- `<Dialog.Portal>` draws no element. A portal takes nothing: where it is drawn is its `PortalProvider`'s to say.
- `<Dialog.Backdrop>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Dialog.Viewport>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Dialog.Popup>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Dialog.Title>` draws a `<h2>`. The heading that names the dialog.
- `<Dialog.Description>` draws a `<p>`. The text that describes the dialog.
- `<Dialog.Close>` draws a `<button>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: It cannot be pressed: the button is disabled, and says so (`data-disabled`).

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- trigger: The button that opens the dialog.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the dialog is open.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- backdrop: The layer over the page behind the dialog.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
- viewport: What a long dialog scrolls in: it lies over the page, between the backdrop and the popup. A press on it beside the popup is a press outside the dialog; a press on its scrollbar is not.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-nested`: Present when the dialog opened over another dialog.
    - `data-nested-dialog-open`: Present when another dialog is open above this one.
- popup: The dialog itself.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-nested`: Present when the dialog opened over another dialog.
    - `data-nested-dialog-open`: Present when another dialog is open above this one.
    - `--nested-dialogs`: How many dialogs are open above this one.
- close: A button that closes the dialog.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### Drawer

```
import { Drawer } from "@kirana-ui/vue/drawer"
```

Parts: `<Drawer.Root>`, `<Drawer.Trigger>`, `<Drawer.Portal>`, `<Drawer.Backdrop>`, `<Drawer.Popup>`, `<Drawer.Title>`, `<Drawer.Description>`, `<Drawer.Close>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Drawer.Root>
  <Drawer.Trigger>
  <Drawer.Portal>
    <Drawer.Backdrop>
    <Drawer.Popup>
      <Drawer.Title>
      <Drawer.Description>
      <Drawer.Close>
```

Props of its root:

- `open?: boolean`: `v-model:open`. Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether it starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `modal?: boolean`: Blocks the page behind it and traps focus. Default `true`.
- `disablePointerDismissal?: boolean`: Keeps it open when the pointer presses outside it. Default `false`. Escape always closes it: a caller who must keep it open cancels the change whose `details.reason` is `"escape-key"`.
- `closeOnOutsidePress?: boolean`: Whether a press outside closes it. Default `true`.
- `dismissible?: boolean`: Whether a press outside closes it. Default `true`.
- `swipeDirection?: DrawerSide`: The way it is dragged to close it: the edge it came from. Default: `"down"`.
- `snapPoints?: readonly DrawerSnapPoint[]`: Places it rests at, each how much of itself shows: a share (`0.4`, or `"40%"`) or a length (`"148px"`, `"20rem"`). `[0.4, 1]` is a drawer that opens two fifths shown and is dragged up to the whole. Without any, it is whole.
- `snapPoint?: DrawerSnapPoint`: `v-model:snapPoint`. Which of them it rests at, as it was given.
- `defaultSnapPoint?: DrawerSnapPoint`: Where it opens. Default: the smallest.
- `@open-change: (value: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as it is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `@snap-point-change: (value: DrawerSnapPoint, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as it is about to rest at another snap point: `details.cancel()` keeps it where it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Drawer.Root>` draws no element. Holds the dialog: whether it is open. Its props are above.
- `<Drawer.Trigger>` draws a `<button>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: It cannot be pressed: the button is disabled, and says so (`data-disabled`).
- `<Drawer.Portal>` draws no element. A portal takes nothing: where it is drawn is its `PortalProvider`'s to say.
- `<Drawer.Backdrop>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Drawer.Popup>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Drawer.Title>` draws a `<h2>`. The heading that names the dialog.
- `<Drawer.Description>` draws a `<p>`. The text that describes the dialog.
- `<Drawer.Close>` draws a `<button>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: It cannot be pressed: the button is disabled, and says so (`data-disabled`).

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- trigger: The button that opens the dialog.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the dialog is open.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- backdrop: The layer over the page behind the dialog.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-swiping`: Present while the drawer is dragged.
    - `data-swipe-dismiss`: Present once a drag has closed the drawer.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-x`: How far it has been dragged across.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-y`: How far it has been dragged up or down.
    - `--drawer-swipe-progress`: How far it has been dragged, of its own size: 0 to 1.
    - `--drawer-snap-point-offset`: How far from whole it rests, towards the edge it closes at: 0px at its largest snap point.
    - `--drawer-swipe-strength`: Always 1: the backdrop takes the design's own time to leave, however the drawer was thrown.
    - `--drawer-height`: While the drawer is dragged: the height of the drawer in front.
- popup: The drawer. A design moves it by what it says of the drag, and gives it `touch-action: none` where a finger drags it.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-nested`: Present when the dialog opened over another dialog.
    - `data-nested-dialog-open`: Present when another dialog is open above this one.
    - `data-swiping`: Present while the drawer is dragged.
    - `data-swipe-direction="up | down | left | right"`: The way it is dragged to close it.
    - `data-swipe-dismiss`: Present once a drag has closed it.
    - `data-expanded`: Present while it rests whole, of several snap points.
    - `data-nested-drawer-open`: Present while another drawer is open over it.
    - `data-nested-drawer-swiping`: Present while a drawer over it is dragged.
    - `--nested-dialogs`: How many dialogs are open above this one.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-x`: How far it has been dragged across.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-y`: How far it has been dragged up or down.
    - `--drawer-swipe-progress`: How far it has been dragged, of its own size: 0 to 1.
    - `--drawer-snap-point-offset`: How far from whole it rests, towards the edge it closes at: 0px at its largest snap point.
    - `--drawer-height`: Its height.
    - `--nested-drawers`: How many drawers are open over it.
    - `--drawer-frontmost-height`: The height of the drawer in front of every other, while this one is open.
    - `--drawer-swipe-strength`: Once let go: 0.1 to 1, the share of the design's own time it should take to come to rest. A drawer thrown hard arrives sooner.
    - `--drawer-width`: Its width.
- close: A button that closes the dialog.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### Editable

```
import { Editable } from "@kirana-ui/vue/editable"
```

Parts: `<Editable.Root>`, `<Editable.Preview>`, `<Editable.Input>`, `<Editable.EditTrigger>`, `<Editable.SubmitTrigger>`, `<Editable.CancelTrigger>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Editable.Root>
  <Editable.Preview>
  <Editable.Input>
  <Editable.EditTrigger> (optional)
  <Editable.SubmitTrigger> (optional)
  <Editable.CancelTrigger> (optional)
```

Props of its root:

- `value?: string`: `v-model:value`. The text it holds: what the preview shows, and what editing starts from.
- `defaultValue?: string`: The text it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once. Default `""`.
- `editing?: boolean`: `v-model:editing`. Whether it is being edited, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultEditing?: boolean`: Read once.
- `placeholder?: string`: What the preview shows while the text is empty. Default `""`.
- `activation?: "focus" | "click" | "dblclick" | "none"`: What on the preview starts an edit: focus reaching it (the default), a press, two presses, or nothing, where only the edit trigger does.
- `submitOnBlur?: boolean`: Whether focus leaving the input keeps the edit (the default) or drops it.
- `selectOnFocus?: boolean`: Whether the text is selected as editing starts. Default `true`.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be edited.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is, not editable.
- `required?: boolean`: Needed: in a `Field`, leaving it empty is then invalid.
- `name?: string`: With a name, the text is submitted with the form around it; in a `Field`, the field's by default.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the input belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `@value-change: (value: string, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as an edit is about to be kept: `details.cancel()` keeps the text, and the edit open.
- `@editing-change: (value: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as editing is about to start or end: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Editable.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Its props are above.
- `<Editable.Preview>` draws a `<span>`.
- `<Editable.Input>` draws a `<input>`.
- `<Editable.EditTrigger>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<Editable.SubmitTrigger>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<Editable.CancelTrigger>` draws a `<button>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: A text edited in place.
    - `data-editing`: Present while it is being edited.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it is shown and cannot be edited.
    - `data-placeholder`: Present while it holds no text.
    - `data-touched`: In a field: present once focus has left it.
    - `data-dirty`: In a field: present while the text is not the one it began with.
    - `data-filled`: In a field: present while it holds text.
    - `data-focused`: In a field: present while it has focus.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the text was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the text is wrong.
- preview: The text as it reads, or the placeholder while there is none: hidden while editing.
    - `data-editing`: Present while it is being edited.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it is shown and cannot be edited.
    - `data-placeholder`: Present while it holds no text.
    - `data-touched`: In a field: present once focus has left it.
    - `data-dirty`: In a field: present while the text is not the one it began with.
    - `data-filled`: In a field: present while it holds text.
    - `data-focused`: In a field: present while it has focus.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the text was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the text is wrong.
- input: Where the text is typed, an `<input>` or a `<textarea>`: hidden unless editing.
    - `data-editing`: Present while it is being edited.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it is shown and cannot be edited.
    - `data-placeholder`: Present while it holds no text.
    - `data-touched`: In a field: present once focus has left it.
    - `data-dirty`: In a field: present while the text is not the one it began with.
    - `data-filled`: In a field: present while it holds text.
    - `data-focused`: In a field: present while it has focus.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the text was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the text is wrong.
- editTrigger: Starts an edit: hidden while editing.
    - `data-editing`: Present while it is being edited.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it is shown and cannot be edited.
    - `data-placeholder`: Present while it holds no text.
    - `data-touched`: In a field: present once focus has left it.
    - `data-dirty`: In a field: present while the text is not the one it began with.
    - `data-filled`: In a field: present while it holds text.
    - `data-focused`: In a field: present while it has focus.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the text was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the text is wrong.
- submitTrigger: Keeps what was typed: hidden unless editing.
    - `data-editing`: Present while it is being edited.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it is shown and cannot be edited.
    - `data-placeholder`: Present while it holds no text.
    - `data-touched`: In a field: present once focus has left it.
    - `data-dirty`: In a field: present while the text is not the one it began with.
    - `data-filled`: In a field: present while it holds text.
    - `data-focused`: In a field: present while it has focus.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the text was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the text is wrong.
- cancelTrigger: Drops what was typed: hidden unless editing.
    - `data-editing`: Present while it is being edited.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it is shown and cannot be edited.
    - `data-placeholder`: Present while it holds no text.
    - `data-touched`: In a field: present once focus has left it.
    - `data-dirty`: In a field: present while the text is not the one it began with.
    - `data-filled`: In a field: present while it holds text.
    - `data-focused`: In a field: present while it has focus.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the text was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the text is wrong.

### Field

```
import { Field } from "@kirana-ui/vue/field"
```

Parts: `<Field.Root>`, `<Field.Label>`, `<Field.Control>`, `<Field.Description>`, `<Field.Error>`, `<Field.Validity>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Field.Root>
  <Field.Label>
  <Field.Control>
  <Field.Description>
  <Field.Error> (repeated)
  <Field.Validity>
```

Props of its root:

- `name?: string`: The control's name in the form.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disables the field: its control cannot be changed, and its parts say so (`data-disabled`).
- `invalid?: boolean`: Invalid whatever the value: an error known from elsewhere.
- `validate?: ( value: string ) => string | readonly string[] | null | Promise<string | readonly string[] | null>`: The field's own check, after the browser's: a message or several when the value is wrong, `null` when it is right. It may answer later, with a promise.
- `validationMode?: ValidationMode`: When the value is checked; the form's by default, else `"onSubmit"`.
- `validationDebounceTime?: number`: With `"onChange"`, how long the value must rest before it is checked, in milliseconds. Default `0`.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Field.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Its props are above.
- `<Field.Label>` draws a `<label>`.
- `<Field.Control>` draws a `<input>`.
- `<Field.Description>` draws a `<p>`.
- `<Field.Error>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `match?: ValidityKey | boolean`: One of the browser's findings (`"valueMissing"`) to show for only that; `true` to show always.
- `<Field.Validity>` draws no element. Gives the control's validity to what it holds, to draw from. Its default slot is also given `validity: FieldValidity`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: A control with its label, its description and its errors.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Present while the value is wrong.
- label: The control's name: a press on it reaches the control.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Present while the value is wrong.
- control: The control: an input, a textarea or a select.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Present while the value is wrong.
- description: More about the control, said after its name.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Present while the value is wrong.
- error: What is wrong with the value. In the page while it applies. Several, each with its own `match`, can be shown at once: each has an id of its own, and the control names them all.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Present while the value is wrong.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.

### Fieldset

```
import { Fieldset } from "@kirana-ui/vue/fieldset"
```

Parts: `<Fieldset.Root>`, `<Fieldset.Legend>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Fieldset.Root>
  <Fieldset.Legend>
```

Props of its root:

- `disabled?: boolean`: Disables every field inside.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Fieldset.Root>` draws a `<fieldset>`. Its props are above.
- `<Fieldset.Legend>` draws a `<div>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The group of fields.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- legend: The group's name.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### FileUpload

```
import { FileUpload } from "@kirana-ui/vue/file-upload"
```

Parts: `<FileUpload.Root>`, `<FileUpload.Dropzone>`, `<FileUpload.Trigger>`, `<FileUpload.List>`, `<FileUpload.Items>`, `<FileUpload.Item>`, `<FileUpload.ItemName>`, `<FileUpload.ItemSize>`, `<FileUpload.ItemRemove>`, `<FileUpload.Clear>`.

Anatomy:

```
<FileUpload.Root>
  <FileUpload.Dropzone>
    <FileUpload.Trigger> (optional, as above)
  <FileUpload.Trigger> (optional)
  <FileUpload.List>
    <FileUpload.Items>
      <FileUpload.Item> (repeated)
        <FileUpload.ItemName>
        <FileUpload.ItemSize> (optional)
        <FileUpload.ItemRemove> (optional)
  <FileUpload.Clear> (optional)
```

Props of its root:

- `files?: readonly File[]`: `v-model:files`. The files it holds, in order.
- `defaultFiles?: readonly File[]`: The files it starts with, when the caller does not hold `files`. Read once.
- `accept?: string | readonly string[]`: What may be taken, as a file input's `accept`: extensions (`".png"`), types (`"image/png"`) and kinds (`"image/*"`), in a list or one text with commas. Without it, anything.
- `multiple?: boolean`: Whether several files are held. Default `false`: a file taken is the one held.
- `maxFiles?: number`: With `multiple`, how many files it holds at most.
- `maxSize?: number`: The largest a file may be, in bytes.
- `minSize?: number`: The smallest a file may be, in bytes.
- `validate?: (file: File) => boolean`: Whether a file may be taken, asked after the checks above.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: no file can be taken or removed.
- `required?: boolean`: Needed: in a `Field`, holding none is then invalid.
- `name?: string`: With a name, the files are submitted with the form around them.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `@files-change: (value: File[], details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as the files are about to change: `details.cancel()` keeps them as they were.
- `@files-reject: (rejections: FileRejection[]) => void`: The files that were not taken, each with its reasons.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<FileUpload.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Its props are above.
- `<FileUpload.Dropzone>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<FileUpload.Trigger>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<FileUpload.List>` draws a `<ul>`.
- `<FileUpload.Items>` draws no element. The files, in order: each entry is given to draw. Its default slot is also given `entry: FileUploadEntry`.
- `<FileUpload.Item>` draws a `<li>`.
    - `entry: FileUploadEntry`: Required. The file it is, as `Items` gave it.
- `<FileUpload.ItemName>` draws a `<span>`.
- `<FileUpload.ItemSize>` draws a `<span>`.
    - `locale?: string`: The language the number is written in. Default: the reader's.
- `<FileUpload.ItemRemove>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<FileUpload.Clear>` draws a `<button>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: Files chosen to be sent.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while files are dragged over the dropzone.
    - `data-required`: Present when a file is needed.
    - `data-empty`: Present while it holds no file.
- dropzone: Where files are dropped or pasted; pressed, it opens the file picker. It holds the hidden file input.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while files are dragged over the dropzone.
    - `data-required`: Present when a file is needed.
- trigger: A button that opens the file picker.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while files are dragged over the dropzone.
    - `data-required`: Present when a file is needed.
- list: What holds the files: a list.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while files are dragged over the dropzone.
    - `data-required`: Present when a file is needed.
- item: A file.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while files are dragged over the dropzone.
    - `data-required`: Present when a file is needed.
- itemName: A file's name.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while files are dragged over the dropzone.
    - `data-required`: Present when a file is needed.
- itemSize: A file's size, as people read one.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while files are dragged over the dropzone.
    - `data-required`: Present when a file is needed.
- itemRemove: A file's button that takes it away.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while files are dragged over the dropzone.
    - `data-required`: Present when a file is needed.
- clear: Takes every file away: hidden while there is none.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while files are dragged over the dropzone.
    - `data-required`: Present when a file is needed.

### Form

```
import { Form } from "@kirana-ui/vue/form"
```

Props:

- `errors?: FormErrors`: Errors from outside the page (a server's), by field name. A field shows its own until its value changes.
- `onClearErrors?: (errors: FormErrors) => void`: A field's value changed while it showed an error from `errors`: what is left of them.
- `onFormSubmit?: (values: FormValues, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Every field is valid. Given this, the page is not left: the values come as an object. Without it, the form submits as a form does.
- `validationMode?: ValidationMode`: When the form's fields check their values, unless a field says otherwise. Default `"onSubmit"`.

`<Form>` draws a `<form>`. `onFormSubmit` and `onClearErrors` are heard as `@form-submit` and `@clear-errors`.

### HoverCard

```
import { HoverCard } from "@kirana-ui/vue/hover-card"
```

Parts: `<HoverCard.Root>`, `<HoverCard.Trigger>`, `<HoverCard.Portal>`, `<HoverCard.Positioner>`, `<HoverCard.Popup>`, `<HoverCard.Arrow>`.

Anatomy:

```
<HoverCard.Root>
  <HoverCard.Trigger>
  <HoverCard.Portal>
    <HoverCard.Positioner>
      <HoverCard.Popup>
        <HoverCard.Arrow>
```

Props of its root:

- `open?: boolean`: `v-model:open`. Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether it starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `delay?: number`: How long the pointer rests on the trigger before the popup opens, in milliseconds. Default `600`.
- `closeDelay?: number`: How long after the pointer leaves the popup closes, in milliseconds. Default `300`.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: the pointer and focus do not open it.
- `@open-change: (value: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as it is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<HoverCard.Root>` draws no element. Holds the card: whether it is open. Its props are above.
- `<HoverCard.Trigger>` draws a `<a>`.
    - `delay?: number`: How long the pointer rests on this trigger before the popup opens: before the root's.
    - `closeDelay?: number`: How long after the pointer leaves the popup closes: before the root's.
- `<HoverCard.Portal>` draws no element. A portal takes nothing: where it is drawn is its `PortalProvider`'s to say.
- `<HoverCard.Positioner>` draws a `<div>`. A positioner's own props: where its popup goes, and what it is placed against. Takes the positioner options ("Positioner options", above).
- `<HoverCard.Popup>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<HoverCard.Arrow>` draws a `<div>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- trigger: The link the card previews.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the card is open.
- positioner: Places the popup against the trigger. It carries the geometry.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-anchor-hidden`: Present while the anchor is out of view: scrolled away, or clipped by a box around it.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
    - `--positioner-width`: The popup's width, as its content lays it out: a design gives the positioner `width: var(--positioner-width)` to animate a change of size.
    - `--positioner-height`: The popup's height, as its content lays it out: a design gives the positioner `height: var(--positioner-height)` to animate a change of size.
- popup: The card itself.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-instant="delay | focus | dismiss"`: Present when it opened or closed without its usual wait, for a design that skips the motion then.
- arrow: An element that points at the trigger, placed along the popup's edge.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-uncentered`: Present when the popup was pushed along its edge, so the arrow is not at the trigger's centre.

### Input

```
import { Input } from "@kirana-ui/vue/input"
```

Props:

- `modelValue?: string`: `v-model:modelValue`. The text: `v-model`.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: nothing can be typed in it.
- `@value-change: (value: string, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: What was typed, as text, each time it changes.

`<Input>` draws a `<input>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- input: A text input. Inside a field it is the field's control.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the input.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while the input has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the value was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the value is wrong.

### Label

```
import { Label } from "@kirana-ui/vue/label"
```

`<Label>` draws a `<label>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- label: A control's name. Inside a field it is the field's label, with its states.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Present while the value is wrong.

### Listbox

```
import { Listbox } from "@kirana-ui/vue/listbox"
```

Parts: `<Listbox.Root>`, `<Listbox.Item>`, `<Listbox.ItemIndicator>`, `<Listbox.Group>`, `<Listbox.GroupLabel>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Listbox.Root>
  <Listbox.Group> (optional, repeated)
    <Listbox.Item> (repeated)
      <Listbox.ItemIndicator>
    <Listbox.GroupLabel>
```

Props of its root:

- `value?: readonly Value[]`: `v-model:value`. The chosen values: none, one, or with `multiple` several.
- `defaultValue?: readonly Value[]`: The values it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `multiple?: boolean`: Whether more than one can be chosen: a press then adds or takes away.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: no item can be chosen.
- `loop?: boolean`: Whether the arrows go round from the last item to the first. Default: they do not.
- `name?: string`: With a name, the chosen values are submitted with the form around the list.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the list belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `virtualized?: ListCollection`: Every row, when only some are in the page (a virtualizer draws the ones in view): how many there are, their names, and how to bring one into the page. Each item is then given its `index`.
- `@value-change: (value: Value[], details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as an item is about to be chosen or taken away, with the values there would then be: `details.cancel()` keeps them as they were.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Listbox.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Generic: `<Value = unknown>`. Its props are above.
- `<Listbox.Item>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be chosen, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What typing matches; the item's text when left out.
    - `index?: number`: Its place among all the rows, in a virtualized list.
    - `value: unknown`: Required. What is in the listbox's value while this item is chosen.
- `<Listbox.ItemIndicator>` draws a `<span>`.
    - `keepMounted?: boolean`: Keeps the mark in the page while its item is not chosen.
- `<Listbox.Group>` draws a `<div>`. Items that belong together, named by their label.
- `<Listbox.GroupLabel>` draws a `<div>`. The name of a group.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The list. It is one stop for Tab.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- item: One choice in the list.
    - `data-selected`: Present on a chosen item.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- itemIndicator: A mark an item shows while it is chosen.
    - `data-selected`: Present on a chosen item.

### Menu

```
import { Menu } from "@kirana-ui/vue/menu"
```

Parts: `<Menu.Root>`, `<Menu.Trigger>`, `<Menu.Portal>`, `<Menu.Positioner>`, `<Menu.Popup>`, `<Menu.Arrow>`, `<Menu.Item>`, `<Menu.LinkItem>`, `<Menu.Group>`, `<Menu.GroupLabel>`, `<Menu.Separator>`, `<Menu.CheckboxItem>`, `<Menu.CheckboxItemIndicator>`, `<Menu.RadioGroup>`, `<Menu.RadioItem>`, `<Menu.RadioItemIndicator>`, `<Menu.SubmenuRoot>`, `<Menu.SubmenuTrigger>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Menu.Root>
  <Menu.Trigger>
  <Menu.Portal>
    <Menu.Positioner>
      <Menu.Popup>
        <Menu.Arrow>
        <Menu.Group> (optional, repeated)
          <Menu.Item> (repeated)
          <Menu.LinkItem> (repeated)
          <Menu.GroupLabel>
          <Menu.CheckboxItem> (repeated)
            <Menu.CheckboxItemIndicator>
          <Menu.RadioGroup> (repeated)
            <Menu.RadioItem> (repeated)
              <Menu.RadioItemIndicator>
          <Menu.SubmenuRoot> (repeated)
            <Menu.Portal> (as above)
            <Menu.SubmenuTrigger>
        <Menu.Separator> (repeated)
```

Props of its root:

- `open?: boolean`: `v-model:open`. Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether it starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `disabled?: boolean`: The trigger cannot be pressed; a submenu's is passed over.
- `loopFocus?: boolean`: Whether the arrows go round from the last item to the first. Default: they do.
- `loop?: boolean`: Whether the arrows wrap from the last item to the first.
- `modal?: boolean`: Holds the page while the menu is open: its scroll is locked, and a press outside closes the menu and reaches nothing. Default: it does not. Not for a submenu.
- `@open-change: (value: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as it is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Menu.Root>` draws no element. Holds the menu: whether it is open. Its props are above.
- `<Menu.Trigger>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<Menu.Portal>` draws no element. A portal takes nothing: where it is drawn is its `PortalProvider`'s to say.
- `<Menu.Positioner>` draws a `<div>`. A positioner's own props: where its popup goes, and what it is placed against. Takes the positioner options ("Positioner options", above).
- `<Menu.Popup>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Menu.Arrow>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Menu.Item>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be pressed, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What typing matches; the item's text when left out.
    - `closeOnSelect?: boolean`: Whether choosing the item closes the menu. Default: it does for an item, and does not for a checkbox or a radio item.
    - `closeOnClick?: boolean`: Whether choosing the item closes the menu.
- `<Menu.LinkItem>` draws a `<a>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be pressed, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What typing matches; the item's text when left out.
    - `closeOnSelect?: boolean`: Whether choosing the item closes the menu. Default: it does for an item, and does not for a checkbox or a radio item.
    - `closeOnClick?: boolean`: Whether choosing the item closes the menu.
- `<Menu.Group>` draws a `<div>`. Items that belong together, named by their label.
- `<Menu.GroupLabel>` draws a `<div>`. The name of a group. Outside a group it is plain text, and names nothing.
- `<Menu.Separator>` draws a `<div>`. A line between items.
- `<Menu.CheckboxItem>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be pressed, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What typing matches; the item's text when left out.
    - `closeOnSelect?: boolean`: Whether choosing the item closes the menu. Default: it does for an item, and does not for a checkbox or a radio item.
    - `closeOnClick?: boolean`: Whether choosing the item closes the menu.
    - `checked?: boolean`: `v-model:checked`. Whether the item is checked, when the caller holds it.
    - `defaultChecked?: boolean`: Whether the item starts checked, when the caller does not hold `checked`. Read once.
    - `@checked-change: (value: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as the item is about to be checked or unchecked: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `<Menu.CheckboxItemIndicator>` draws a `<span>`.
    - `keepMounted?: boolean`: Keeps the mark in the page while the item is unchecked.
- `<Menu.RadioGroup>` draws a `<div>`. Generic: `<Value = unknown>`.
    - `value?: Value | null`: `v-model:value`. The chosen value; `null` is "none".
    - `defaultValue?: Value | null`: The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables every item of the group.
    - `@value-change: (value: Value, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Told an item's own value, never `null`: a press chooses, and nothing takes the choice back.
- `<Menu.RadioItem>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be pressed, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What typing matches; the item's text when left out.
    - `closeOnSelect?: boolean`: Whether choosing the item closes the menu. Default: it does for an item, and does not for a checkbox or a radio item.
    - `closeOnClick?: boolean`: Whether choosing the item closes the menu.
    - `value: unknown`: Required. What the group's value is while this item is the chosen one.
- `<Menu.RadioItemIndicator>` draws a `<span>`.
    - `keepMounted?: boolean`: Keeps the mark in the page while its item is not the chosen one.
- `<Menu.SubmenuRoot>` draws no element. A submenu: it holds the item that opens it and a portal, positioner and popup of its own.
    - `open?: boolean`: `v-model:open`. Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
    - `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether it starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: The trigger cannot be pressed; a submenu's is passed over.
    - `loopFocus?: boolean`: Whether the arrows go round from the last item to the first. Default: they do.
    - `loop?: boolean`: Whether the arrows wrap from the last item to the first.
    - `modal?: boolean`: Holds the page while the menu is open: its scroll is locked, and a press outside closes the menu and reaches nothing. Default: it does not. Not for a submenu.
    - `@open-change: (value: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as it is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `<Menu.SubmenuTrigger>` draws a `<div>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- trigger: The button that opens the menu, and what it is placed against.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the menu is open.
    - `data-pressed`: Present while its popup is open: it stays pressed, as a button held down.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- positioner: Places the menu against its trigger. It carries the geometry.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-anchor-hidden`: Present while the anchor is out of view: scrolled away, or clipped by a box around it.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
    - `--positioner-width`: The popup's width, as its content lays it out: a design gives the positioner `width: var(--positioner-width)` to animate a change of size.
    - `--positioner-height`: The popup's height, as its content lays it out: a design gives the positioner `height: var(--positioner-height)` to animate a change of size.
- popup: The menu itself: the list of items.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-instant="click | dismiss | group"`: Present when it opened or closed in a way that should skip the motion: `click` when the keyboard pressed its trigger or an item, `dismiss` when Escape closed it, `group` when focus or the pointer went from one menu of a bar to another.
- arrow: An element that points at the trigger.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-uncentered`: Present when the arrow cannot sit at the trigger's centre.
- item: An action. Choosing it closes the menu.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- linkItem: An item that is a link. Choosing it follows the link and closes the menu.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- checkboxItem: An item that is checked or not. Choosing it leaves the menu open.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- checkboxItemIndicator: A mark a checkbox item shows while it is checked.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
- radioGroup: Radio items of which one is chosen.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- radioItem: One choice of a radio group. Choosing it leaves the menu open.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- radioItemIndicator: A mark a radio item shows while it is the chosen one.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
- submenuTrigger: An item that opens a menu beside it.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when its menu is open.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### Menubar

```
import { Menubar } from "@kirana-ui/vue/menubar"
```

Props:

- `loopFocus?: boolean`: Whether the arrows go round from the last menu to the first. Default: they do.
- `loop?: boolean`: Whether the arrows wrap from the last item to the first.
- `disabled?: boolean`: No menu of the bar opens.
- `orientation?: Orientation`: A row (the default) or a column of menus. In a column a menu opens beside its trigger.
- `modal?: boolean`: Holds the page while one of its menus is open, as a menu's own `modal` does: its scroll is locked, and a press outside closes the menu and reaches nothing. Default: it does not. Read as a menu opens.

`<Menubar>` draws a `<div>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The row of menus. A menu inside it is one of its items.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-modal`: Present when its menus hold the page while one is open.
    - `data-has-submenu-open`: Present while one of its menus is open.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether its menus are in a row or a column.

### MessageScroller

```
import { MessageScroller } from "@kirana-ui/vue/message-scroller"
```

Parts: `<MessageScroller.Root>`, `<MessageScroller.Viewport>`, `<MessageScroller.Content>`, `<MessageScroller.Button>`.

Anatomy:

```
<MessageScroller.Root>
  <MessageScroller.Viewport>
    <MessageScroller.Content>
  <MessageScroller.Button>
```

Props of its root:

- `initial?: "bottom" | "top"`: Where it begins: at the newest message (the default), or at the first.
- `threshold?: number`: How near the end counts as at it, in pixels. Default: 24.
- `@at-bottom-change: (atBottom: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: It came to the end, or left it.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<MessageScroller.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Its props are above.
- `<MessageScroller.Viewport>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<MessageScroller.Content>` draws a `<div>`. The messages: what grows as one is written.
- `<MessageScroller.Button>` draws a `<button>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: What holds the conversation and its button.
    - `data-at-bottom`: Present while the newest message is in view.
- viewport: What scrolls: a log, reached by the keyboard.
    - `data-at-bottom`: Present while the newest message is in view.
- button: Goes to the newest message. Inert while that is in view.
    - `data-at-bottom`: Present while the newest message is in view.

### Meter

```
import { Meter } from "@kirana-ui/vue/meter"
```

Parts: `<Meter.Root>`, `<Meter.Track>`, `<Meter.Indicator>`, `<Meter.Value>`, `<Meter.Label>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Meter.Root>
  <Meter.Track>
    <Meter.Indicator>
  <Meter.Value>
  <Meter.Label>
```

Props of its root:

- `min?: number`: Default 0.
- `max?: number`: Default 100.
- `format?: Intl.NumberFormatOptions`: How the value is written; a percentage of the range by default.
- `locale?: string`: The language the value is written in; the page's by default.
- `getAriaValueText?: (text: string | undefined, value: number | null) => string`: What assistive technology reads for the value, when the written value is not enough.
- `value: Value`: Required. The value; a progress bar's is `null` while how far it has come is not known.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Meter.Root>` draws a `<div>`. A meter always has a value. Its props are above.
- `<Meter.Track>` draws a `<div>`. The whole range.
- `<Meter.Indicator>` draws a `<div>`. The filled part: its width is the value's share of the range.
- `<Meter.Value>` draws a `<span>`. The value, written. Its default slot is also given `text: string`.
- `<Meter.Label>` draws a `<span>`. The meter's name.

### NavigationMenu

```
import { NavigationMenu } from "@kirana-ui/vue/navigation-menu"
```

Parts: `<NavigationMenu.Root>`, `<NavigationMenu.List>`, `<NavigationMenu.Item>`, `<NavigationMenu.Trigger>`, `<NavigationMenu.Icon>`, `<NavigationMenu.Content>`, `<NavigationMenu.Link>`, `<NavigationMenu.Portal>`, `<NavigationMenu.Positioner>`, `<NavigationMenu.Popup>`, `<NavigationMenu.Viewport>`, `<NavigationMenu.Arrow>`, `<NavigationMenu.Backdrop>`.

Anatomy:

```
<NavigationMenu.Root>
  <NavigationMenu.List>
    <NavigationMenu.Item> (repeated)
      <NavigationMenu.Trigger>
        <NavigationMenu.Icon>
      <NavigationMenu.Content>
        <NavigationMenu.Link> (repeated)
      <NavigationMenu.Link> (repeated, as above)
    <NavigationMenu.Link> (repeated, as above)
  <NavigationMenu.Portal>
    <NavigationMenu.Positioner>
      <NavigationMenu.Popup>
        <NavigationMenu.Viewport>
        <NavigationMenu.Arrow>
    <NavigationMenu.Backdrop>
```

Props of its root:

- `value?: Value | null`: `v-model:value`. The item whose content is shown; `null` is "none".
- `defaultValue?: Value | null`: The item whose content it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `delay?: number`: How long the pointer rests on a trigger before its content shows, in milliseconds. Default `50`.
- `closeDelay?: number`: How long after the pointer leaves the content goes, in milliseconds. Default `50`.
- `orientation?: Orientation`: Whether the triggers are laid out across (the default) or down: the arrows that move between them follow.
- `@value-change: (value: Value | null, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as another item's content is about to show, or none: `details.cancel()` keeps the value as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<NavigationMenu.Root>` draws a `<nav>`. Generic: `<Value = unknown>`. Its props are above.
- `<NavigationMenu.List>` draws a `<ul>`.
- `<NavigationMenu.Item>` draws a `<li>`. One item of the list: a link, or a trigger with its content. Its `value` tells it from the others; an item that is given none makes its own.
    - `value?: unknown`: What tells this item from the others: the menu's `value` while its content is shown. An item that is given none makes its own.
- `<NavigationMenu.Trigger>` draws a `<button>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: The trigger cannot be pressed, and the pointer resting on it shows nothing.
- `<NavigationMenu.Icon>` draws a `<span>`.
- `<NavigationMenu.Content>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<NavigationMenu.Link>` draws a `<a>`.
    - `active?: boolean`: The link is the page the reader is on.
    - `closeOnSelect?: boolean`: Whether following it closes the menu. Default: it does.
    - `closeOnClick?: boolean`: Whether following it closes the menu.
- `<NavigationMenu.Portal>` draws no element. A portal takes nothing: where it is drawn is its `PortalProvider`'s to say.
- `<NavigationMenu.Positioner>` draws a `<div>`. A positioner's own props: where its popup goes, and what it is placed against. Takes the positioner options ("Positioner options", above).
- `<NavigationMenu.Popup>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<NavigationMenu.Viewport>` draws a `<div>`. Where the contents are drawn, inside the popup.
- `<NavigationMenu.Arrow>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<NavigationMenu.Backdrop>` draws a `<div>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The navigation.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the list is a row or a column.
    - `data-open`: Present while an item's content is shown.
    - `data-nested`: Present on a navigation menu inside another's content: a submenu of it.
- list: The row of items.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the list is a row or a column.
    - `data-open`: Present while an item's content is shown.
- trigger: The button that shows an item's content.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present while the item's content is shown.
    - `data-pressed`: Present while its popup is open: it stays pressed, as a button held down.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- icon: A mark on a trigger that shows whether its content is open.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present while the item's content is shown.
- content: What an item shows. It is drawn in the viewport every item shares.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-activation-direction="left | right | up | down"`: Which way it came from: the item before it, or after; `up` and `down` when the list is a column.
- link: A link, in the list or in an item's content.
    - `data-active`: Present on the link of the page the reader is on.
- positioner: Places the popup against the open item's trigger. It carries the geometry.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-anchor-hidden`: Present while the anchor is out of view: scrolled away, or clipped by a box around it.
    - `data-instant`: Present while it should move at once: as it is first drawn, and while the window is resized.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
    - `--positioner-width`: The open content's width.
    - `--positioner-height`: The open content's height.
- popup: The panel every item's content is shown in.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-anchor-hidden`: Present while the anchor is out of view: scrolled away, or clipped by a box around it.
    - `--popup-width`: The open content's width.
    - `--popup-height`: The open content's height.
- arrow: An element that points at the open item's trigger.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-uncentered`: Present when the arrow cannot sit at the trigger's centre.
- backdrop: An element behind the popup, for a design that dims the page.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.

### NumberField

```
import { NumberField } from "@kirana-ui/vue/number-field"
```

Parts: `<NumberField.Root>`, `<NumberField.Group>`, `<NumberField.Input>`, `<NumberField.Increment>`, `<NumberField.Decrement>`, `<NumberField.ScrubArea>`, `<NumberField.ScrubAreaCursor>`.

Anatomy:

```
<NumberField.Root>
  <NumberField.Group>
    <NumberField.Input>
    <NumberField.Increment>
    <NumberField.Decrement>
  <NumberField.ScrubArea>
    <NumberField.ScrubAreaCursor>
```

Props of its root:

- `defaultValue?: number | null`: The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `min?: number`: The least the number may be.
- `max?: number`: The most the number may be.
- `step?: number`: What the buttons and the arrows move by. Default 1.
- `smallStep?: number`: With Alt held. Default 0.1.
- `largeStep?: number`: With Shift held. Default 10.
- `snapOnStep?: boolean`: A step lands on a multiple of the step, counted from `min`.
- `allowWheelScrub?: boolean`: The wheel steps it while the pointer is over the input and focus is in it.
- `format?: Intl.NumberFormatOptions`: How the number is written.
- `locale?: string`: The language it is written in; the page's by default.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable.
- `required?: boolean`: Needed: in a `Field`, leaving it empty is then invalid.
- `name?: string`: With a name, the number is submitted with the form around it.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `modelValue?: number | null`: `v-model:modelValue`. The number, `null` for none: `v-model`.
- `id?: string`: What its input's id is made from: the input is `<id>-input`, which a `<label for>` names. Inside a `Field`, the input takes the field's id instead.
- `@value-change: (value: number | null, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as the number is about to change, typed or stepped: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `@value-committed: (value: number | null, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard once a change is done: focus left the input, a key or a button stepped it.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<NumberField.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Its props are above.
- `<NumberField.Group>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<NumberField.Input>` draws a `<input>`.
- `<NumberField.Increment>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<NumberField.Decrement>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<NumberField.ScrubArea>` draws a `<span>`. What a scrub area takes of its own: which way it is dragged, and how fast.
    - `direction?: "horizontal" | "vertical"`: The way the pointer is dragged to change the number: `"horizontal"`, where right is more, or `"vertical"`, where up is more. Default `"horizontal"`.
    - `pixelSensitivity?: number`: How many pixels the pointer moves before the number changes: more is slower. Default 2.
    - `teleportDistance?: number`: How far past the scrub area's edges the drawn cursor goes before it comes back in at the other side, in pixels, half of it at each edge. Default: the edges of the window.
- `<NumberField.ScrubAreaCursor>` draws a `<span>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: Groups the number field's parts.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the number cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a number must be given.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the input.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the number is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while there is a number.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-scrubbing`: Present while the number is dragged from its scrub area.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the number was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the number is wrong.
- group: What holds the input and its buttons, as one control.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the number cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a number must be given.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the input.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the number is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while there is a number.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-scrubbing`: Present while the number is dragged from its scrub area.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the number was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the number is wrong.
- input: The text input: it takes what its locale writes a number with.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the number cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a number must be given.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the input.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the number is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while there is a number.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-scrubbing`: Present while the number is dragged from its scrub area.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the number was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the number is wrong.
- increment: A button that steps the number up. Held, it goes on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the number cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a number must be given.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the input.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the number is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while there is a number.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-scrubbing`: Present while the number is dragged from its scrub area.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the number was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the number is wrong.
- decrement: A button that steps the number down. Held, it goes on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the number cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a number must be given.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the input.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the number is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while there is a number.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-scrubbing`: Present while the number is dragged from its scrub area.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the number was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the number is wrong.
- scrubArea: An area that is pressed and dragged to change the number: the field's label, as a rule. It takes `direction`, `pixelSensitivity` and `teleportDistance`. A mouse's pointer is locked for the drag where the browser has that (not in Safari); a finger drags as it is.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the number cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a number must be given.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the input.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the number is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while there is a number.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-scrubbing`: Present while the number is dragged from its scrub area.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the number was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the number is wrong.
- scrubAreaCursor: What is drawn in place of the pointer while it is locked for a drag: in the page only then, at the end of `<body>`, placed by the component.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the number cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a number must be given.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the input.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the number is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while there is a number.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-scrubbing`: Present while the number is dragged from its scrub area.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the number was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the number is wrong.

### Otp

```
import { Otp } from "@kirana-ui/vue/otp"
```

Parts: `<Otp.Root>`, `<Otp.Input>`, `<Otp.Group>`, `<Otp.Slot>`, `<Otp.Separator>`, `<Otp.Caret>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Otp.Root>
  <Otp.Input>
  <Otp.Group> (repeated)
    <Otp.Slot> (repeated)
      <Otp.Caret>
  <Otp.Separator> (repeated)
```

Props of its root:

- `length?: number`: How many characters the code has. Default: 6.
- `value?: string`: `v-model:value`. The characters typed so far, when the caller holds them.
- `defaultValue?: string`: The characters it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once. Default `""`.
- `validationType?: OtpValidation`: What a character may be: a digit (`numeric`), a letter (`alpha`, `a` to `z` either case), either (`alphanumeric`), or anything but white space (`none`: no rule beyond that). It also says which keyboard a phone shows: the digits' for `numeric`, letters' otherwise. Default: `numeric`, on purpose: a one-time code is digits, and its keyboard is then the one to type them on. `alphabetic` and `text` are older spellings of `alpha` and `none`, still read.
- `mode?: OtpValidation`: What a character may be.
- `pattern?: string`: What else a character may be: a regular expression, as text, that one character must match whole (`"[A-F0-9]"`), in place of `validationType`'s rule. Text, as an attribute can only be, so it is given the same way on every framework and on a custom element. With a pattern, `validationType` only says the keyboard, and defaults to `none`.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable.
- `required?: boolean`: Needed: in a `Field`, an empty code is then invalid.
- `name?: string`: With a name, the code is submitted with the form around it.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the input belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `id?: string`: The id of its input, not of the root: a `<label for>` names it.
- `@value-change: (value: string, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as the characters are about to change: `details.cancel()` keeps them as they were.
- `@value-complete: (value: string, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: The finished code, once every cell is filled, with the details of the change that did it.
- `@complete: (value: string) => void`: The finished code.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Otp.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Its props are above.
- `<Otp.Input>` draws a `<input>`.
- `<Otp.Group>` draws a `<div>`. Cells that are drawn together.
- `<Otp.Slot>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `index: number`: Required. Which character of the code the cell shows, from 0.
- `<Otp.Separator>` draws a `<div>`. A mark between groups of cells.
- `<Otp.Caret>` draws a `<div>`. A caret drawn in the active cell while it is empty.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The code: the input and its cells.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present when the code has a character in it.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-complete`: Present when every character is in.
- input: The one input the code is typed in. A design lays it over the cells, unseen.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- slot: One cell of the code.
    - `data-index`: The cell's place, from 0.
    - `data-active`: Present on the cell the next character goes in, or that is selected.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present when the cell has its character.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-complete`: Present when every character is in.

### Pagination

```
import { Pagination } from "@kirana-ui/vue/pagination"
```

Parts: `<Pagination.Root>`, `<Pagination.Items>`, `<Pagination.Item>`, `<Pagination.Ellipsis>`, `<Pagination.Previous>`, `<Pagination.Next>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Pagination.Root>
  <Pagination.Items>
    <Pagination.Item> (repeated)
    <Pagination.Ellipsis> (repeated)
  <Pagination.Previous>
  <Pagination.Next>
```

Props of its root:

- `page?: number`: `v-model:page`. The page shown, from 1.
- `defaultPage?: number`: The page it starts at, when the caller does not hold `page`. Read once. Default `1`.
- `count: number`: Required. How many items there are in all.
- `pageSize?: number`: How many items a page holds. Default 10.
- `siblingCount?: number`: How many pages are listed each side of the one shown. Default 1.
- `boundaryCount?: number`: How many pages are always listed at each end. Default 1.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: no page can be gone to.
