- `@page-change: (value: number, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as another page is about to be shown: `details.cancel()` keeps the page as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Pagination.Root>` draws a `<nav>`. Its props are above.
- `<Pagination.Items>` draws no element. The row's entries, pages and the gaps between them: each is given to draw. Its default slot is also given `entry: PaginationEntry`.
- `<Pagination.Item>` draws a `<button>`.
    - `page: number`: Required. The page it goes to.
- `<Pagination.Ellipsis>` draws a `<span>`. The mark for pages that are left out of the row.
- `<Pagination.Previous>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<Pagination.Next>` draws a `<button>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The pages of a list, as a navigation.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- item: A page: pressed, it is the one shown.
    - `data-selected`: Present on the page that is shown.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- previous: Goes to the page before.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- next: Goes to the page after.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### PasswordInput

```
import { PasswordInput } from "@kirana-ui/vue/password-input"
```

Parts: `<PasswordInput.Root>`, `<PasswordInput.Input>`, `<PasswordInput.Toggle>`, `<PasswordInput.Indicator>`.

Anatomy:

```
<PasswordInput.Root>
  <PasswordInput.Input>
  <PasswordInput.Toggle>
    <PasswordInput.Indicator> (optional)
```

Props of its root:

- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: nothing can be typed in it.
- `visible?: boolean`: `v-model:visible`. Whether the password can be read, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultVisible?: boolean`: Read once. Default `false`.
- `@visible-change: (value: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as it is about to be shown or hidden: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `@value-change: (value: string, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: What was typed, as text, each time it changes.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<PasswordInput.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Its props are above.
- `<PasswordInput.Input>` draws a `<input>`.
- `<PasswordInput.Toggle>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<PasswordInput.Indicator>` draws a `<span>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: A password that can be shown while it is typed.
    - `data-visible`: Present while the password can be read.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- input: The `<input>`: a password, or text while it is shown. In a `Field` it is the field's control.
    - `data-visible`: Present while the password can be read.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left it.
    - `data-dirty`: Present once its text differs from what it began with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while it holds text.
    - `data-focused`: Present while it has focus.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the value was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the value is wrong.
- toggle: Shows the password, and hides it again. Focus and the caret stay in the input.
    - `data-visible`: Present while the password can be read.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- indicator: What draws which of the two it is: an eye, open or struck.
    - `data-visible`: Present while the password can be read.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### Popover

```
import { Popover } from "@kirana-ui/vue/popover"
```

Parts: `<Popover.Root>`, `<Popover.Trigger>`, `<Popover.Portal>`, `<Popover.Backdrop>`, `<Popover.Positioner>`, `<Popover.Popup>`, `<Popover.Arrow>`, `<Popover.Title>`, `<Popover.Description>`, `<Popover.Close>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Popover.Root>
  <Popover.Trigger>
  <Popover.Portal>
    <Popover.Backdrop>
    <Popover.Positioner>
      <Popover.Popup>
        <Popover.Title>
        <Popover.Description>
        <Popover.Close>
        <Popover.Arrow>
```

Props of its root:

- `open?: boolean`: `v-model:open`. Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether it starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `modal?: boolean | "trap-focus"`: What the page behind it may do while it is open. `false` (the default): everything. `true`: nothing, the page is inert and does not scroll, and Tab stays inside the popover. `"trap-focus"`: Tab stays inside the popover, and the page can still be pressed and scrolled. A popover the pointer opened holds nothing until it is pressed. Read as it opens.
- `@open-change: (value: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as it is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Popover.Root>` draws no element. Holds the popover: whether it is open. Its props are above.
- `<Popover.Trigger>` draws a `<button>`.
    - `openOnHover?: boolean`: Whether the pointer resting on the trigger opens the popover too. A press and the keyboard still open it, and a press on one the pointer opened keeps it open. Default `false`.
    - `delay?: number`: How long the pointer rests on the trigger before the popover opens, in milliseconds. Default 300.
    - `closeDelay?: number`: How long after the pointer leaves a popover it opened closes, in milliseconds. Default 0.
- `<Popover.Portal>` draws no element. A portal takes nothing: where it is drawn is its `PortalProvider`'s to say.
- `<Popover.Backdrop>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Popover.Positioner>` draws a `<div>`. A positioner's own props: where its popup goes, and what it is placed against. Takes the positioner options ("Positioner options", above).
- `<Popover.Popup>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Popover.Arrow>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Popover.Title>` draws a `<h2>`. The heading that names the popover.
- `<Popover.Description>` draws a `<p>`. The text that describes the popover.
- `<Popover.Close>` draws a `<button>`. A button that closes the popover.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- trigger: The button that opens the popover, and what it is placed against.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the popover is open.
    - `data-pressed`: Present while the popover a press on this trigger opened is open: it stays pressed, as a button held down.
- backdrop: A layer over the page behind the popover.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
- positioner: Places the popup against the trigger. It carries the geometry.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-anchor-hidden`: Present while the anchor is out of view: scrolled away, or clipped by a box around it.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
    - `--positioner-width`: The popup's width, as its content lays it out: a design gives the positioner `width: var(--positioner-width)` to animate a change of size.
    - `--positioner-height`: The popup's height, as its content lays it out: a design gives the positioner `height: var(--positioner-height)` to animate a change of size.
- popup: The popover itself.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-instant="click | dismiss"`: Present when it opened or closed in a way that should skip the motion: `click` when the keyboard pressed the trigger, `dismiss` when Escape closed it.
    - `--popup-width`: Its width: `auto`, and while its content changes size, the old width and then the new one, for a transition between them.
    - `--popup-height`: Its height: `auto`, and while its content changes size, the old height and then the new one, for a transition between them.
- arrow: An element that points at the trigger, placed along the popup's edge.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-uncentered`: Present when the popup was pushed along its edge, so the arrow is not at the trigger's centre.

### Progress

```
import { Progress } from "@kirana-ui/vue/progress"
```

Parts: `<Progress.Root>`, `<Progress.Track>`, `<Progress.Indicator>`, `<Progress.Value>`, `<Progress.Label>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Progress.Root>
  <Progress.Track>
    <Progress.Indicator>
  <Progress.Value>
  <Progress.Label>
```

Props of its root:

- `min?: number`: Default 0.
- `max?: number`: Default 100.
- `format?: Intl.NumberFormatOptions`: How the value is written; a percentage of the range by default.
- `locale?: string`: The language the value is written in; the page's by default.
- `getAriaValueText?: (text: string | undefined, value: number | null) => string`: What assistive technology reads for the value, when the written value is not enough.
- `value: Value`: Required. The value; a progress bar's is `null` while how far it has come is not known.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Progress.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Generic: `<Value extends number | null = number | null>`. Its props are above.
- `<Progress.Track>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Progress.Indicator>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Progress.Value>` draws a `<span>`. Its default slot is also given `text: string`.
- `<Progress.Label>` draws a `<span>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The progress bar: it says the value to assistive technology.
    - `data-progressing`: Present while the task is under way.
    - `data-complete`: Present once the value has reached the end of the range.
    - `data-indeterminate`: Present while how far the task has come is not known.
- track: The whole range.
    - `data-progressing`: Present while the task is under way.
    - `data-complete`: Present once the value has reached the end of the range.
    - `data-indeterminate`: Present while how far the task has come is not known.
- indicator: The filled part: its width is the value's share of the range.
    - `data-progressing`: Present while the task is under way.
    - `data-complete`: Present once the value has reached the end of the range.
    - `data-indeterminate`: Present while how far the task has come is not known.
- value: The value, written.
    - `data-progressing`: Present while the task is under way.
    - `data-complete`: Present once the value has reached the end of the range.
    - `data-indeterminate`: Present while how far the task has come is not known.
- label: The bar's name.
    - `data-progressing`: Present while the task is under way.
    - `data-complete`: Present once the value has reached the end of the range.
    - `data-indeterminate`: Present while how far the task has come is not known.

### QrCode

```
import { QrCode } from "@kirana-ui/vue/qr-code"
```

Parts: `<QrCode.Root>`, `<QrCode.Frame>`, `<QrCode.Pattern>`.

Anatomy:

```
<QrCode.Root>
  <QrCode.Frame>
    <QrCode.Pattern>
```

Props of its root:

- `value: string`: Required. What the code says: a link, a text. Written as UTF-8.
- `correction?: QrCorrection`: How much of it may be lost and still be read. Default: `"M"`.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<QrCode.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Its props are above.
- `<QrCode.Frame>` draws a `<svg>`. The drawing: an `<svg>` a module to the unit.
- `<QrCode.Pattern>` draws a `<path>`. The dark modules: one `<path>`, filled by the design.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: What holds the code.
    - `data-invalid`: Present when the value is longer than a code holds.

### RadioGroup

```
import { RadioGroup } from "@kirana-ui/vue/radio-group"
```

Parts: `<RadioGroup.Root>`, `<RadioGroup.Item>`, `<RadioGroup.Indicator>`.

Anatomy:

```
<RadioGroup.Root>
  <RadioGroup.Item> (repeated)
    <RadioGroup.Indicator>
```

Props of its root:

- `value?: Value | null`: `v-model:value`. The chosen value; `null` is "none".
- `defaultValue?: Value | null`: The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disables every item of the group.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable.
- `required?: boolean`: Needed: in a `Field`, choosing none is then invalid.
- `name?: string`: With a name, the chosen value is submitted with the form around the group.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `@value-change: (value: Value | null, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: `null` only when a form's reset takes the group back to "none".

Each part, and its own props:

- `<RadioGroup.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Generic: `<Value = unknown>`. Its props are above.
- `<RadioGroup.Item>` draws a `<span>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be chosen.
    - `id?: string`: The id of the item's native radio, unique in the page: a `<label for>` names it.
    - `value: unknown`: Required. What the group's value is while this item is the chosen one.
- `<RadioGroup.Indicator>` draws a `<span>`.
    - `keepMounted?: boolean`: Keeps the mark in the page while its item is not the chosen one.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: Groups the items: one of them is chosen at most.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
- item: One choice. It holds a hidden native radio, which a form and a label reach: the item's `id` (`kpId` on Angular, `kui-id` on a custom element) is the radio's, which a `<label for>` names.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
- indicator: The mark. In the page while its item is the chosen one.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.

### Rating

```
import { Rating } from "@kirana-ui/vue/rating"
```

Parts: `<Rating.Root>`, `<Rating.Items>`, `<Rating.Item>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Rating.Root>
  <Rating.Items>
    <Rating.Item> (repeated)
```

Props of its root:

- `value?: number`: `v-model:value`. How much is given, from 0 (none) to `count`; a half where `allowHalf` is set.
- `defaultValue?: number`: The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once. Default `0`.
- `count?: number`: How many items there are. Default 5.
- `allowHalf?: boolean`: Whether half an item can be given: by the half of it a pointer is over, and by the arrows.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable.
- `required?: boolean`: Needed: in a `Field`, giving none is then invalid.
- `name?: string`: With a name, the value is submitted with the form around it; none is submitted as empty.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `@value-change: (value: number, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as another value is about to be given: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `@hover-change: (value: number | null) => void`: The value the pointer is over, `null` once it leaves.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Rating.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Its props are above.
- `<Rating.Items>` draws no element. The items, from 1 to `count`: each place is given to draw. Its default slot is also given `place: number`.
- `<Rating.Item>` draws a `<span>`.
    - `place: number`: Required. Its place among the items, from 1.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The items, as one choice: a radio group. It holds the hidden input a form reads.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it is shown and cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a value is needed.
    - `data-hovering`: Present while a pointer is over an item.
- item: One item (a star): pressed, the value is its place, or half of it.
    - `data-checked`: Present on the item that holds the value.
    - `data-filled`: Present on every item up to the value drawn: the one a pointer is over, or the one held.
    - `data-half`: Present on the item the value drawn fills by half.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it is shown and cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a value is needed.

### Resizable

```
import { Resizable } from "@kirana-ui/vue/resizable"
```

Parts: `<Resizable.Group>`, `<Resizable.Panel>`, `<Resizable.Handle>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Resizable.Group>
  <Resizable.Panel> (repeated)
  <Resizable.Handle> (repeated)
```

Props of its root:

- `orientation?: Orientation`: Whether the panels are side by side (the default) or one over the other.
- `keyboardStep?: number`: How far an arrow key moves a handle, in hundredths of the group. Default: 10.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: the handles cannot be dragged or moved with the keyboard.
- `@sizes-change: (sizes: number[], details: ChangeDetails) => void`: The panels were resized: each one's share, in order.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Resizable.Group>` draws a `<div>`. Its props are above.
- `<Resizable.Panel>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `defaultSize?: number`: Its share to begin with, in hundredths of the group. Either every panel gives one or none does (they are then equal).
    - `minSize?: number`: The least it can be made. Default: 0.
    - `maxSize?: number`: The most it can be made. Default: 100.
- `<Resizable.Handle>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this handle: it cannot be dragged or moved with the keyboard.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- group: The panels and the bars between them. A design lays it out as a flex box: `display: flex`, and `flex-direction: column` when it is vertical. A group in a panel that is a flex box itself takes `min-width: 0` and `min-height: 0`, or what it holds widens the panel.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the panels are side by side or one over the other.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- panel: One panel. It carries its share of the group, written as its `flex` with `min-width: 0` and `min-height: 0`, so what it holds cannot keep it past its share. Its `overflow` is the design's.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the panels are side by side or one over the other.
    - `--panel-size`: The panel's share, in hundredths of the group.
- handle: The bar between two panels: dragged, or moved with the arrows. A design gives it its thickness and `flex-shrink: 0`, so the panels do not squeeze it.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the panels are side by side or one over the other.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while the bar is dragged.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### ScrollArea

```
import { ScrollArea } from "@kirana-ui/vue/scroll-area"
```

Parts: `<ScrollArea.Root>`, `<ScrollArea.Viewport>`, `<ScrollArea.Content>`, `<ScrollArea.Scrollbar>`, `<ScrollArea.Thumb>`, `<ScrollArea.Corner>`.

Anatomy:

```
<ScrollArea.Root>
  <ScrollArea.Viewport>
    <ScrollArea.Content> (optional)
    <ScrollArea.Scrollbar> (repeated, as above)
  <ScrollArea.Scrollbar> (repeated)
    <ScrollArea.Thumb>
  <ScrollArea.Corner>
```

Each part, and its own props:

- `<ScrollArea.Root>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<ScrollArea.Viewport>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<ScrollArea.Content>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<ScrollArea.Scrollbar>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `orientation?: Orientation`: Which way it scrolls; `vertical` when left out.
    - `keepMounted?: boolean`: Keeps the bar in the page while there is nothing to scroll that way.
- `<ScrollArea.Thumb>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<ScrollArea.Corner>` draws a `<div>`. The square where the two scrollbars meet, placed there.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The area. It holds the viewport and the scrollbars, which the library places against it: a design gives a scrollbar its thickness and draws it, and places nothing.
    - `data-has-overflow-x`: Present when there is more to see sideways.
    - `data-has-overflow-y`: Present when there is more to see up or down.
    - `data-overflow-x-start`: Present when there is more to scroll to towards the start of a line.
    - `data-overflow-x-end`: Present when there is more to scroll to towards the end of a line.
    - `data-overflow-y-start`: Present when there is more to scroll to above.
    - `data-overflow-y-end`: Present when there is more to scroll to below.
    - `data-scrolling`: Present while it is being scrolled, and a moment after.
    - `data-hovering`: Present while the pointer is over the area.
    - `--scroll-area-corner-width`: The width of the corner: the vertical scrollbar's, while both scrollbars and the corner are in the page.
    - `--scroll-area-corner-height`: The height of the corner: the horizontal scrollbar's, while both scrollbars and the corner are in the page.
- viewport: The element that scrolls.
    - `data-has-overflow-x`: Present when there is more to see sideways.
    - `data-has-overflow-y`: Present when there is more to see up or down.
    - `data-overflow-x-start`: Present when there is more to scroll to towards the start of a line.
    - `data-overflow-x-end`: Present when there is more to scroll to towards the end of a line.
    - `data-overflow-y-start`: Present when there is more to scroll to above.
    - `data-overflow-y-end`: Present when there is more to scroll to below.
    - `data-scrolling`: Present while it is being scrolled, and a moment after.
    - `--scroll-area-overflow-x-start`: How far the view is from the start of a line, to fade that edge by: `0px` at it.
    - `--scroll-area-overflow-x-end`: How far the view is from the end of a line: `0px` at it.
    - `--scroll-area-overflow-y-start`: How far the view is from the top: `0px` at it.
    - `--scroll-area-overflow-y-end`: How far the view is from the bottom: `0px` at it.
- content: A box around what is scrolled, as wide as what it holds. Not needed to measure: the viewport's children are watched as they are. For content whose own box does not grow with what is in it (a block holding a wider table, or bare text).
    - `data-has-overflow-x`: Present when there is more to see sideways.
    - `data-has-overflow-y`: Present when there is more to see up or down.
    - `data-overflow-x-start`: Present when there is more to scroll to towards the start of a line.
    - `data-overflow-x-end`: Present when there is more to scroll to towards the end of a line.
    - `data-overflow-y-start`: Present when there is more to scroll to above.
    - `data-overflow-y-end`: Present when there is more to scroll to below.
    - `data-scrolling`: Present while it is being scrolled, and a moment after.
- scrollbar: A scrollbar's track, placed along its edge of the area. In the page while there is something to scroll its way.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Which way the scrollbar scrolls.
    - `data-hovering`: Present while the pointer is over the area.
    - `data-scrolling`: Present while the area is scrolled its way.
    - `data-has-overflow-x`: Present when there is more to see sideways.
    - `data-has-overflow-y`: Present when there is more to see up or down.
    - `data-overflow-x-start`: Present when there is more to scroll to towards the start of a line.
    - `data-overflow-x-end`: Present when there is more to scroll to towards the end of a line.
    - `data-overflow-y-start`: Present when there is more to scroll to above.
    - `data-overflow-y-end`: Present when there is more to scroll to below.
    - `--scroll-area-thumb-height`: A vertical thumb's height.
    - `--scroll-area-thumb-width`: A horizontal thumb's width.
- thumb: The part of a scrollbar that shows where the view is, and can be dragged. As long as its scrollbar's variable says.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Which way the scrollbar scrolls.
    - `data-scrolling`: Present while the area is scrolled its way.

### Select

```
import { Select } from "@kirana-ui/vue/select"
```

Parts: `<Select.Root>`, `<Select.Trigger>`, `<Select.Value>`, `<Select.Portal>`, `<Select.Backdrop>`, `<Select.Positioner>`, `<Select.Popup>`, `<Select.List>`, `<Select.ScrollUpArrow>`, `<Select.ScrollDownArrow>`, `<Select.Group>`, `<Select.GroupLabel>`, `<Select.Separator>`, `<Select.Item>`, `<Select.ItemText>`, `<Select.ItemIndicator>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Select.Root>
  <Select.Trigger>
    <Select.Value>
  <Select.Portal>
    <Select.Backdrop> (optional)
    <Select.Positioner>
      <Select.Popup>
        <Select.ScrollUpArrow>
        <Select.List> (optional)
          <Select.Group> (optional, repeated)
            <Select.GroupLabel>
            <Select.Item> (repeated)
              <Select.ItemText>
              <Select.ItemIndicator>
          <Select.Separator> (repeated)
        <Select.ScrollDownArrow>
```

Props of its root:

- `presentation?: Presentation`: How the list opens. `"sheet"`: from the bottom edge, not placed against the trigger, modal with a backdrop, swiped down or pressed outside to close. `"auto"`: decided each time it opens, a sheet when the pointer is coarse and the viewport narrower than `sheetBelow`. Default `"popup"`.
- `sheetBelow?: number`: With `presentation: "auto"`: the viewport's width, in CSS pixels, under which a coarse pointer opens a sheet. Default 640.
- `value?: (Multiple extends true ? readonly Value[] : Value | null)`: `v-model:value`. The chosen value; `null` is "none". With `multiple`, the chosen values, in the order they were chosen.
- `defaultValue?: (Multiple extends true ? readonly Value[] : Value | null)`: The value it starts with (with `multiple`, the values), when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `open?: boolean`: `v-model:open`. Whether the list is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether the list starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable: the list still opens to be read, and no item can be chosen. Its value is still submitted with the form.
- `required?: boolean`: In a field, "none" is then wrong.
- `name?: string`: With a name, the value is submitted with the form around it.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `items?: readonly { value: Value; label: string }[] | Readonly<Record<string, string>>`: The labels of the values, for the trigger to show before the list has ever been opened: a list of values with their labels, or, for values that are text, the labels by value (`{ apple: "Apple" }`). Not needed for the list itself: its items are read from the markup.
- `itemToStringLabel?: (value: Value) => string`: For values that are objects: the text the trigger shows for one, and what typing matches an item by when it gives no `label`. Without it, an object's own `label` names it, then the label `items` gives it, then the item's text in the markup.
- `itemToStringValue?: (value: Value) => string`: For values that are objects: the text the form is sent for one. Without it, the `value` of an object shaped `{ value, label }` is sent, and any other object as JSON.
- `values?: readonly Value[]`: `v-model:values`. With `multiple`: the chosen values.
- `defaultValues?: readonly Value[]`: With `multiple`: the values it starts with.
- `virtualized?: ListCollection`: Every row, when only some are in the page (a virtualizer draws the ones in view). Each item is then given its `index`.
- `multiple?: Multiple`: Several values: `value` and `@value-change` then hold a list. Read once.
- `@value-change: (value: Multiple extends true ? Value[] : Value | null, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as a value is about to be chosen (with `multiple`, added or taken away, with the values there would then be): `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `@values-change: (value: Value[], details: ChangeDetails) => void`: With `multiple`: heard as a value is about to be added or taken away.
- `@open-change: (value: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as the list is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Select.Root>` draws no element. Generic: `<Value = unknown, Multiple extends boolean | undefined = false>`. `Multiple` is read from `multiple`: with it, `value` and `@value-change` hold a list. Its props are above.
- `<Select.Trigger>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<Select.Value>` draws a `<span>`. Its default slot is also given `value: Value | null`, `label: string`, `values: readonly Value[]`, `labels: readonly string[]`.
    - `placeholder?: string`: What it shows while nothing is chosen.
- `<Select.Portal>` draws no element. A portal takes nothing: where it is drawn is its `PortalProvider`'s to say.
- `<Select.Backdrop>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Select.Positioner>` draws a `<div>`. Takes the positioner options ("Positioner options", above).
    - `alignItemWithTrigger?: boolean`: Opens the list over its trigger, the chosen item's text on the trigger's own, where there is room and unless a finger opened it. While it lies there the page's scroll is held (its scrollbar's room kept), and a scroll of a box around the trigger closes the list (`"ancestor-scroll"`), as a change of the window's size does (`"window-resize"`).
- `<Select.Popup>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Select.List>` draws a `<div>`. The items' own box inside the popup, when the popup holds more than its items: the listbox, and what scrolls.
- `<Select.ScrollUpArrow>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Select.ScrollDownArrow>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Select.Group>` draws a `<div>`. Items that belong together, named by their label.
- `<Select.GroupLabel>` draws a `<div>`. The name of a group. Outside a group it is plain text, and names nothing.
- `<Select.Separator>` draws a `<div>`. A line between groups.
- `<Select.Item>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be chosen, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What typeahead matches and the trigger shows; the item's text when left out.
    - `index?: number`: Its place among all the rows, in a virtualized list.
    - `value: unknown`: Required. What the select's value is while this item is the chosen one.
- `<Select.ItemText>` draws a `<span>`. The item's name: what the trigger shows once it is chosen.
- `<Select.ItemIndicator>` draws a `<span>`. A mark an item shows while it is chosen.
    - `keepMounted?: boolean`: Keeps the mark in the page while its item is not chosen.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- trigger: The button that shows the value and opens the list.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the list is open.
    - `data-pressed`: Present while its popup is open: it stays pressed, as a button held down.
    - `data-popup-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end | none"`: While the list is in the page: the side of the trigger it is on, after any flip; `none` when it lies over the trigger. Not said while it opens as a sheet.
    - `data-placeholder`: Present while nothing is chosen.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
- value: The chosen value's label, or the placeholder. With several values, their labels with commas between.
    - `data-placeholder`: Present while nothing is chosen.
- backdrop: The layer over the page behind the list: a press on it closes the list.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-presentation="popup | sheet"`: How the list opened: placed against its trigger, or as a sheet from the bottom edge.
    - `data-swiping`: Present while the sheet is dragged.
    - `data-swipe-dismiss`: Present once a drag has closed it.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-x`: As a sheet: how far it has been dragged across, always 0px.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-y`: As a sheet: how far it has been dragged down.
    - `--drawer-swipe-progress`: As a sheet: how far it has been dragged, of its own height: 0 to 1.
- positioner: Places the list against the trigger. It carries the geometry. As a sheet it is not placed, and carries none.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end | none"`: The side of the trigger it is on, after any flip; `none` when it lies over the trigger.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-presentation="popup | sheet"`: How the list opened: placed against its trigger, or as a sheet from the bottom edge.
    - `data-anchor-hidden`: Present while the anchor is out of view: scrolled away, or clipped by a box around it.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
- scrollUpArrow: In the page while there is more of the list above: it scrolls the list while the pointer moves over it.
    - `data-direction="up | down"`: The way it scrolls the list.
    - `data-visible`: Present while there is more of the list its way.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end | none"`: The side of the trigger the list is on; `none` when it lies over the trigger.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
- scrollDownArrow: In the page while there is more of the list below: it scrolls the list while the pointer moves over it.
    - `data-direction="up | down"`: The way it scrolls the list.
    - `data-visible`: Present while there is more of the list its way.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end | none"`: The side of the trigger the list is on; `none` when it lies over the trigger.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
- popup: The list of items. As a sheet, a design moves it by what it says of the drag, and gives it `touch-action: none` where a finger drags it.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end | none"`: The side of the trigger it is on, after any flip; `none` when it lies over the trigger.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-presentation="popup | sheet"`: How the list opened: placed against its trigger, or as a sheet from the bottom edge.
    - `data-swiping`: Present while the sheet is dragged.
    - `data-swipe-dismiss`: Present once a drag has closed it.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-x`: As a sheet: how far it has been dragged across, always 0px.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-y`: As a sheet: how far it has been dragged down.
    - `--drawer-swipe-progress`: As a sheet: how far it has been dragged, of its own height: 0 to 1.
    - `--drawer-swipe-strength`: As a sheet, once let go: 0.1 to 1, the share of the design's own time it should take to come to rest.
- item: One choice in the list.
    - `data-selected`: Present on the chosen item, or on each of several.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### Separator

```
import { Separator } from "@kirana-ui/vue/separator"
```

Props:

- `orientation?: Orientation`: Whether the line lies across (the default) or stands upright: what a screen reader is told.

`<Separator>` draws a `<div>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The line.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the line runs.

### Slider

```
import { Slider } from "@kirana-ui/vue/slider"
```

Parts: `<Slider.Root>`, `<Slider.Value>`, `<Slider.Control>`, `<Slider.Track>`, `<Slider.Indicator>`, `<Slider.Thumb>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Slider.Root>
  <Slider.Value>
  <Slider.Control>
    <Slider.Track>
      <Slider.Indicator>
      <Slider.Thumb> (repeated)
```

Props of its root:

- `min?: number`: Default 0.
- `max?: number`: Default 100.
- `step?: number`: Default 1.
- `largeStep?: number`: What Page Up, Page Down and an arrow with Shift move by. Default 10.
- `minStepsBetweenValues?: number`: How many steps two thumbs of a range stay apart. Default 0.
- `orientation?: Orientation`: Whether the track lies across (the default) or stands upright: the arrows that move a thumb follow.
- `thumbAlignment?: "center" | "edge" | "edge-client-only"`: Where a thumb is at the ends of its range. `"center"` (the default): its centre on the control's edge, so half of it lies outside. `"edge"`: its edge on the control's edge, so it stays inside. `"edge-client-only"` is the same here: nothing waits for the browser.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable: no key and no pointer moves a thumb, and its value is still submitted with the form.
- `name?: string`: With a name, each thumb's value is submitted with the form around the slider.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `format?: Intl.NumberFormatOptions`: How a value is written.
- `locale?: string`: The language a value is written in; the page's by default.
- `getAriaValueText?: (text: string, value: number, index: number) => string`: What assistive technology reads for a thumb, when the written value is not enough.
- `value?: Value`: `v-model:value`. One number for a slider with one thumb, a list for a range.
- `defaultValue?: Value`: Read once. Default `min`.
- `@value-change: (value: SliderTold<Value>, details: SliderChangeDetails) => void`: Each step of a drag and each key.
- `@value-committed: (value: RootValue<Value>, details: SliderChangeDetails) => void`: The change is done: the pointer was let go, or a key moved a thumb.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Slider.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Generic: `<Value extends SliderValue = SliderValue>`. Its props are above.
- `<Slider.Value>` draws a `<output>`. Its default slot is also given `text: string`, `values: readonly number[]`.
- `<Slider.Control>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Slider.Track>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Slider.Indicator>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Slider.Thumb>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `index?: number`: Which value of a range the thumb is, from 0; its place among the thumbs when left out.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: Groups the slider's parts.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the track runs.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
- value: The value, written.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the track runs.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
- control: What a pointer presses and drags on. It holds the track and the thumbs.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the track runs.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
- track: The whole range.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the track runs.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
- indicator: The filled part: up to the thumb, or from the first thumb to the last. Its place and length are written on it.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the track runs.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
    - `--start-position`: With thumbs that stay inside the control: where the filled part starts, or with one thumb where it ends.
    - `--relative-size`: With thumbs that stay inside the control and a range: the filled part's length.
- thumb: What is dragged, and what the keyboard moves: a slider to assistive technology. Its place on the track is written on it. It holds a hidden input, which a form reads. A thumb that is given no `index` is the value at its place among the slider's thumbs, in the order they are written.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the track runs.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
    - `data-index`: Which thumb it is, from 0.
    - `--position`: With thumbs that stay inside the control: where the thumb's centre is.

### Steps

```
import { Steps } from "@kirana-ui/vue/steps"
```

Parts: `<Steps.Root>`, `<Steps.List>`, `<Steps.Item>`, `<Steps.Trigger>`, `<Steps.Indicator>`, `<Steps.Separator>`, `<Steps.Content>`, `<Steps.Completed>`, `<Steps.Previous>`, `<Steps.Next>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Steps.Root>
  <Steps.List>
    <Steps.Item> (repeated)
      <Steps.Trigger>
        <Steps.Indicator> (optional)
      <Steps.Separator> (optional)
  <Steps.Content> (repeated)
  <Steps.Completed> (optional)
  <Steps.Previous> (optional)
  <Steps.Next> (optional)
```

Props of its root:

- `step?: number`: `v-model:step`. The step shown, from 0. Equal to `count`, every step is done.
- `defaultStep?: number`: The step it starts at, when the caller does not hold `step`. Read once. Default `0`.
- `count?: number`: How many steps there are. Left out, the items in the page, counted once they are there: until then (and on a server) no step is the last, so none is all done. Give it where only some of the steps are drawn.
- `linear?: boolean`: In order only: a step that is not done yet cannot be gone to by its trigger.
- `orientation?: Orientation`: Whether the steps are laid out across (the default) or down: the arrows follow.
- `@step-change: (value: number, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as another step is about to be shown: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Steps.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Its props are above.
- `<Steps.List>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Steps.Item>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `index?: number`: Which step it is, from 0. Left out, its place among the items in the page, once it is there: give it on a page a server draws, which cannot count them.
- `<Steps.Trigger>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<Steps.Indicator>` draws a `<span>`.
- `<Steps.Separator>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Steps.Content>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `index: number`: Required. The step it is shown for, from 0.
- `<Steps.Completed>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Steps.Previous>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<Steps.Next>` draws a `<button>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: A task in steps, taken in order.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the steps are laid out across or down.
    - `data-complete`: Present once every step is done.
- list: The row of steps: the arrows move between their triggers.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the steps are laid out across or down.
- item: One step of the row, around its trigger and its separator.
    - `data-current`: Present on the step that is shown.
    - `data-complete`: Present on a step that is done: one before the step shown.
    - `data-incomplete`: Present on a step still to come.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the steps are laid out across or down.
- trigger: Names a step, and goes to it when pressed.
    - `data-current`: Present on the step that is shown.
    - `data-complete`: Present on a step that is done: one before the step shown.
    - `data-incomplete`: Present on a step still to come.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the steps are laid out across or down.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- indicator: A step's mark: its number, or a tick once it is done.
    - `data-current`: Present on the step that is shown.
    - `data-complete`: Present on a step that is done: one before the step shown.
    - `data-incomplete`: Present on a step still to come.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the steps are laid out across or down.
- separator: The line from a step to the next.
    - `data-current`: Present on the step that is shown.
    - `data-complete`: Present on a step that is done: one before the step shown.
    - `data-incomplete`: Present on a step still to come.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the steps are laid out across or down.
- content: What a step shows: hidden unless its step is the one shown.
    - `data-current`: Present on the step that is shown.
    - `data-complete`: Present on a step that is done: one before the step shown.
    - `data-incomplete`: Present on a step still to come.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the steps are laid out across or down.
- completed: What is shown once every step is done.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the steps are laid out across or down.
- previous: Goes to the step before.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- next: Goes to the step after; from the last, to all of them done.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### Switch

```
import { Switch } from "@kirana-ui/vue/switch"
```

Parts: `<Switch.Root>`, `<Switch.Thumb>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Switch.Root>
  <Switch.Thumb>
```

Props of its root:

- `checked?: boolean`: `v-model:checked`. Whether it is checked, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultChecked?: boolean`: Read once.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable.
- `required?: boolean`: Needed: in a `Field`, leaving it unchecked is then invalid.
- `name?: string`: With a name, the control is submitted with the form around it when it is checked.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `value?: string`: What is submitted. Default `"on"`, as a native checkbox's.
- `id?: string`: The id of the switch's hidden native checkbox, not of the switch: a `<label for>` names it. Inside a `Field`, that input takes the field's id instead.
- `@checked-change: (value: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as it is about to be checked or unchecked: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Switch.Root>` draws a `<span>`. Its props are above.
- `<Switch.Thumb>` draws a `<span>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The track. It holds a hidden native checkbox, which a form and a label reach.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.
- thumb: The knob that moves along the track.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-touched`: Inside a Field: present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Inside a Field: present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Inside a Field: present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Inside a Field: present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Inside a Field: present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Inside a Field: present while the value is wrong.

### Tabs

```
import { Tabs } from "@kirana-ui/vue/tabs"
```

Parts: `<Tabs.Root>`, `<Tabs.List>`, `<Tabs.Tab>`, `<Tabs.Indicator>`, `<Tabs.Panel>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Tabs.Root>
  <Tabs.List>
    <Tabs.Tab> (repeated)
    <Tabs.Indicator>
  <Tabs.Panel> (repeated)
```

Props of its root:

- `value?: Value | null`: `v-model:value`. The active tab's value; `null` is "none".
- `defaultValue?: Value | null`: Read once. Without one, the first tab that can be chosen is, once the page is there.
- `orientation?: Orientation`: Whether the tabs are laid out across (the default) or down: the arrows that move between them follow.
- `@value-change: (value: Value, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Told a tab's own value, never `null`: tabs do not go back to none.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Tabs.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Generic: `<Value = unknown>`. Its props are above.
- `<Tabs.List>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `activateOnFocus?: boolean`: Whether moving focus onto a tab with the arrows activates it. Default `false`.
    - `loopFocus?: boolean`: Whether the arrows wrap from the last tab to the first. Default `true`.
    - `loop?: boolean`: Whether the arrows wrap from the last item to the first.
- `<Tabs.Tab>` draws a `<button>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this tab: it cannot be chosen.
    - `value: unknown`: Required. What the tabs' value is while this tab is the active one.
- `<Tabs.Indicator>` draws a `<span>`.
- `<Tabs.Panel>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `value: unknown`: Required. The value of the tab this panel belongs to.
    - `keepMounted?: boolean`: Keeps the panel in the page, `hidden`, while its tab is not the active one.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: Groups the tabs and their panels.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the tabs are laid out.
    - `data-activation-direction="left | right | up | down | none"`: Where the newly active tab is from the one before, for a panel or a mark that slides.
- list: The row of tabs. The arrows move between them.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the tabs are laid out.
    - `data-activation-direction="left | right | up | down | none"`: Where the newly active tab is from the one before, for a panel or a mark that slides.
- tab: A button that shows its panel.
    - `data-active`: Present on the tab whose panel is shown.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the tabs are laid out.
    - `data-activation-direction="left | right | up | down | none"`: Where the newly active tab is from the one before, for a panel or a mark that slides.
- indicator: A mark for the active tab: it carries that tab's position and size.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the tabs are laid out.
    - `data-activation-direction="left | right | up | down | none"`: Where the newly active tab is from the one before, for a panel or a mark that slides.
    - `--active-tab-left`: The active tab's distance from the list's left edge.
    - `--active-tab-right`: The active tab's distance from the list's right edge.
    - `--active-tab-top`: The active tab's distance from the list's top edge.
    - `--active-tab-bottom`: The active tab's distance from the list's bottom edge.
    - `--active-tab-width`: The active tab's width.
    - `--active-tab-height`: The active tab's height.
- panel: A tab's content. In the page while its tab is active, and through its exit.
    - `data-hidden`: Present while its tab is not the active one.
    - `data-index`: The panel's place among the panels in the page, from 0, once it is in the page.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the tabs are laid out.
    - `data-activation-direction="left | right | up | down | none"`: Where the newly active tab is from the one before, for a panel or a mark that slides.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.

### TagsInput

```
import { TagsInput } from "@kirana-ui/vue/tags-input"
```

Parts: `<TagsInput.Root>`, `<TagsInput.List>`, `<TagsInput.Items>`, `<TagsInput.Item>`, `<TagsInput.ItemText>`, `<TagsInput.ItemInput>`, `<TagsInput.ItemRemove>`, `<TagsInput.Input>`, `<TagsInput.Clear>`.

Anatomy:

```
<TagsInput.Root>
  <TagsInput.List>
    <TagsInput.Items>
      <TagsInput.Item> (repeated)
        <TagsInput.ItemText>
        <TagsInput.ItemInput> (optional)
        <TagsInput.ItemRemove> (optional)
  <TagsInput.Input>
  <TagsInput.Clear> (optional)
```

Props of its root:

- `value?: readonly string[]`: `v-model:value`. The tags, in order.
- `defaultValue?: readonly string[]`: The tags it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `validate?: (text: string, value: readonly string[]) => boolean`: Whether a text may be a tag. Asked after the text is trimmed, and not for an empty one.
- `max?: number`: How many tags it holds at most.
- `allowDuplicates?: boolean`: Whether the same text may be a tag twice. Default `false`.
- `delimiter?: string | RegExp | null`: What ends a tag as it is typed or pasted, beside Enter. Default `","`. `null` for nothing.
- `addOnBlur?: boolean`: Whether what is typed becomes a tag as focus leaves the input. Default `false`.
- `addOnPaste?: boolean`: Whether a pasted text is cut into tags at its delimiters and line ends. Default `true`.
- `editable?: boolean`: Whether a tag can be edited in place, by two presses or Enter on it. Default `true`.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: nothing can be added or taken away.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as they are, focusable, not changeable.
- `required?: boolean`: Needed: in a `Field`, holding none is then invalid.
- `name?: string`: With a name, each tag is submitted under it with the form around them.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `@value-change: (value: string[], details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as the tags are about to change: `details.cancel()` keeps them as they were.
- `@value-invalid: (text: string, reason: "duplicate" | "max" | "invalid") => void`: A text that was not made a tag, and why.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<TagsInput.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Its props are above.
- `<TagsInput.List>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<TagsInput.Items>` draws no element. The tags, in order: each entry is given to draw. Its default slot is also given `entry: TagsInputEntry`.
- `<TagsInput.Item>` draws a `<span>`.
    - `entry: TagsInputEntry`: Required. The tag it is, as `Items` gave it.
- `<TagsInput.ItemText>` draws a `<span>`.
- `<TagsInput.ItemInput>` draws a `<input>`.
- `<TagsInput.ItemRemove>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<TagsInput.Input>` draws a `<input>`.
- `<TagsInput.Clear>` draws a `<button>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: Several short texts held as tags, and the input a new one is typed in. It holds the hidden inputs a form reads.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the tags are shown and cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a tag is needed.
    - `data-focused`: Present while focus is on a tag or in the input.
    - `data-empty`: Present while it holds no tag.
- list: What holds the tags: a list.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the tags are shown and cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a tag is needed.
- item: A tag: reached with the arrows, taken away with Backspace or Delete.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the tags are shown and cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a tag is needed.
    - `data-editing`: Present while the tag is edited.
- itemText: A tag's text: hidden while the tag is edited.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the tags are shown and cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a tag is needed.
- itemInput: Where a tag is edited in place: hidden unless it is being edited.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the tags are shown and cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a tag is needed.
- itemRemove: A tag's button that takes it away.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the tags are shown and cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a tag is needed.
- input: Where a new tag is typed. In a `Field` it is what the field's label names.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the tags are shown and cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a tag is needed.
- clear: Takes every tag away: hidden while there is none.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the tags are shown and cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a tag is needed.

### TimeField

```
import { TimeField } from "@kirana-ui/vue/time-field"
```

Parts: `<TimeField.Root>`, `<TimeField.Segments>`, `<TimeField.Segment>`, `<TimeField.Input>`.

Anatomy:

```
<TimeField.Root>
  <TimeField.Segments>
    <TimeField.Segment> (repeated)
  <TimeField.Input>
```

Props of its root:

- `value?: IsoTime | null`: `v-model:value`. The time typed, once all of it is; `null` until then.
- `defaultValue?: IsoTime | null`: The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `granularity?: TimeGranularity`: To the minute (`HH:MM`, the default) or to the second (`HH:MM:SS`).
- `locale?: string`: The language and region that order the parts, put what stands between them and say whether the clock has twelve hours or twenty-four (`"en-US"`: 12, with AM and PM). Give it: a server does not know the reader's. Default `"en-US"`.
- `hourCycle?: HourCycle`: A clock of 12 or 24 hours, whatever the locale's is.
- `min?: IsoTime`: The first time it takes: before it, it says it is invalid.
- `max?: IsoTime`: The last time it takes.
- `placeholders?: Partial<Record<TimeUnit, string>>`: What an empty part shows. Default: `hh`, `mm`, `ss`, and `--` for the day period.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable.
- `required?: boolean`: Needed: in a `Field`, leaving it empty is then invalid.
- `name?: string`: The name it is submitted under, by its hidden input; in a `Field`, the field's by default.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form it belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `@value-change: (value: string | null, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as the time is about to change, once all of it is typed or as it is cleared: `details.cancel()` keeps the value as it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<TimeField.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Its props are above.
- `<TimeField.Segments>` draws no element. The time's segments, in the locale's order: each is given to draw. Its default slot is also given `segment: TimeFieldSegment`.
- `<TimeField.Segment>` draws a `<span>`.
    - `segment: TimeFieldSegment`: Required. The piece it draws, as `TimeField.Segments` gives it.
- `<TimeField.Input>` draws a `<input>`. The hidden input it is submitted by.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The field: a group of the time's parts.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when its value cannot be changed.
    - `data-invalid`: Present when the time is outside what it takes, is asked for and half typed, or is wrong by its field.
    - `data-touched`: In a field: present once focus has left it.
    - `data-dirty`: In a field: present while the time is not the one it began with.
    - `data-filled`: In a field: present while it holds a time.
    - `data-focused`: In a field: present while one of its parts has focus.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the time was checked and found right.
- segment: One piece of the time: a part that is typed, or what stands between two.
    - `data-segment="hour | minute | second | dayPeriod | literal"`: Which piece it is: `dayPeriod` is AM or PM, on a clock of twelve hours.
    - `data-placeholder`: Present on a part that is empty.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-invalid`: Present when the time is outside what it takes, is asked for and half typed, or is wrong by its field.
    - `data-touched`: In a field: present once focus has left it.
    - `data-dirty`: In a field: present while the time is not the one it began with.
    - `data-filled`: In a field: present while it holds a time.
    - `data-focused`: In a field: present while one of its parts has focus.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the time was checked and found right.

### Toast

```
import { Toast } from "@kirana-ui/vue/toast"
```

Parts: `<Toast.Viewport>`, `<Toast.List>`, `<Toast.Root>`, `<Toast.Content>`, `<Toast.Title>`, `<Toast.Description>`, `<Toast.Close>`, `<Toast.Action>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Toast.Viewport>
  <Toast.List>
    <Toast.Root> (repeated)
      <Toast.Content> (optional)
        <Toast.Title>
        <Toast.Description>
      <Toast.Close>
      <Toast.Action>
```

Props of its root:

- `toast: ToastRecord`: Required. The toast it draws, as `Toast.List` gives it.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Toast.Viewport>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `toaster: Toaster<Content>`: Required. The toaster whose toasts are drawn: one made with `createToaster()`. Needed.
    - `label?: string`: What the region of toasts is called, for assistive technology. Default: `"Notifications"`.
    - `hotkey?: string`: The key that takes focus to the toasts. Default: `"F6"`.
    - `swipeDirection?: "left" | "right" | "up" | "down"`: The way a toast is dragged to close it. Default: `"right"`.
- `<Toast.List>` draws no element. The toasts in the page: each is given to draw its root. Its default slot is also given `toast: ToastRecord`.
- `<Toast.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Its props are above.
- `<Toast.Content>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Toast.Title>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Toast.Description>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Toast.Close>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<Toast.Action>` draws a `<button>`.

A page's toasts are a toaster's, made once in a module: `import { createToaster } from "@kirana-ui/vue"`, then `export const toaster = createToaster(options)` (`ToasterOptions`, under "Types"). The viewport is given it, and anything on the page adds to it: `toaster.add({ title, description, action, priority })`, `toaster.update(id, options)`, `toaster.dismiss(id)`, `toaster.promise(promise, { loading, success, error })`. What each takes and gives back is `Toaster`, `ToastOptions`, `ToastActionOptions` and `ToastRecord` under "Types".

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- viewport: Where the toasts are drawn: a region that is always in the page.
    - `data-expanded`: Present while the pointer or focus is on the stack: the toasts are spread out, and wait.
    - `--toast-frontmost-height`: The height of the newest toast.
- root: One toast.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-expanded`: Present while the pointer or focus is on the stack: the toasts are spread out, and wait.
    - `data-type`: The kind the toast was added as.
    - `data-limited`: Present on a toast behind as many as are shown at once.
    - `data-swiping`: Present while the toast is dragged.
    - `data-swipe-direction="left | right | up | down"`: The way the toast was dragged out, once it has been.
    - `--toast-index`: Its place in the stack: 0 for the newest.
    - `--toast-height`: Its height.
    - `--toast-offset-y`: The height of the toasts in front of it.
    - `--toast-swipe-movement-x`: How far it has been dragged across.
    - `--toast-swipe-movement-y`: How far it has been dragged up or down.
- content: What holds a toast's contents, when the design sizes the toast itself.
    - `data-behind`: Present on a toast that is behind the newest.
    - `data-expanded`: Present while the pointer or focus is on the stack: the toasts are spread out, and wait.
- title: What the toast is called: the title it was added with, when nothing else is written in it.
    - `data-type`: The kind the toast was added as.
- description: What the toast says: the description it was added with, when nothing else is written in it.
    - `data-type`: The kind the toast was added as.
- close: Closes the toast.
    - `data-type`: The kind the toast was added as.
- action: A button of the toast's own: the action it was added with, when nothing else is written in it. Pressing it closes the toast too, unless the action refuses.
    - `data-type`: The kind the toast was added as.

### Toggle

```
import { Toggle } from "@kirana-ui/vue/toggle"
```

Props:

- `pressed?: boolean`: `v-model:pressed`. Whether it is pressed, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultPressed?: boolean`: Read once.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: a press does nothing.
- `value?: unknown`: In a toggle group: what the group's value holds while this one is pressed.
- `@pressed-change: (value: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as it is about to be pressed or released: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.

`<Toggle>` draws a `<button>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The button. It stays pressed until it is pressed again.
    - `data-pressed`: Present while it is pressed.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### ToggleGroup

```
import { ToggleGroup } from "@kirana-ui/vue/toggle-group"
```

Props:

- `value?: readonly Value[]`: `v-model:value`. The values of the pressed toggles: none, one, or with `multiple` several.
- `defaultValue?: readonly Value[]`: The values pressed at the start, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `multiple?: boolean`: Whether more than one can be pressed at a time.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disables every toggle of the group.
- `orientation?: Orientation`: Whether the toggles are laid out across (the default) or down: the arrows that move between them follow.
- `loopFocus?: boolean`: Whether the arrows go round from the last toggle to the first. Default: they do.
- `loop?: boolean`: Whether the arrows wrap from the last item to the first.
- `@value-change: (value: Value[], details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as a toggle is about to be pressed or released, with the values that would then be pressed: `details.cancel()` keeps them as they were.

`<ToggleGroup>` draws a `<div>`. Generic: `<Value = unknown>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The group. A toggle inside it with a `value` is one of its toggles.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether its toggles are in a row or a column.
    - `data-multiple`: Present when several can be pressed at a time.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### Toolbar

```
import { Toolbar } from "@kirana-ui/vue/toolbar"
```

Parts: `<Toolbar.Root>`, `<Toolbar.Button>`, `<Toolbar.Link>`, `<Toolbar.Input>`, `<Toolbar.Group>`, `<Toolbar.Separator>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Toolbar.Root>
  <Toolbar.Group> (optional, repeated)
    <Toolbar.Button> (repeated)
    <Toolbar.Link> (repeated)
    <Toolbar.Input> (repeated)
  <Toolbar.Separator> (repeated)
```

Props of its root:

- `orientation?: Orientation`: Whether the controls are laid out across (the default) or down: the arrows that move between them follow.
- `loopFocus?: boolean`: Whether the arrows go round from the last item to the first. Default: they do.
- `loop?: boolean`: Whether the arrows wrap from the last item to the first.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disables every control of the toolbar.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Toolbar.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Its props are above.
- `<Toolbar.Button>` draws a `<button>`. `focusable-when-disabled` keeps it focusable while disabled, as Base UI's. Default `true`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this control.
    - `focusableWhenDisabled?: boolean`: Keeps this control focusable while disabled, as Base UI's: the arrows still reach it and it still says what it is, but a press, a click and the keys (Tab apart) do nothing. Default `true`. With `false`, a disabled control is the element's own `disabled`, and the arrows pass it.
- `<Toolbar.Link>` draws a `<a>`.
- `<Toolbar.Input>` draws a `<input>`. `focusable-when-disabled` keeps it focusable while disabled, as Base UI's. Default `true`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this control.
    - `focusableWhenDisabled?: boolean`: Keeps this control focusable while disabled, as Base UI's: the arrows still reach it and it still says what it is, but a press, a click and the keys (Tab apart) do nothing. Default `true`. With `false`, a disabled control is the element's own `disabled`, and the arrows pass it.
- `<Toolbar.Group>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this control.
- `<Toolbar.Separator>` draws a `<div>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The toolbar. It is one stop for Tab.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the toolbar is a row or a column.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- button: A button of the toolbar.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the toolbar is a row or a column.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-focusable`: Present when it stays focusable while disabled: the arrows still reach it.
- link: A link of the toolbar.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the toolbar is a row or a column.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- input: A text input of the toolbar. The arrows are its own until the caret is at an end.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the toolbar is a row or a column.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-focusable`: Present when it stays focusable while disabled: the arrows still reach it.
- group: Items that belong together.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the toolbar is a row or a column.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- separator: A line between items, across the toolbar.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the toolbar is a row or a column.

### Tooltip

```
import { Tooltip } from "@kirana-ui/vue/tooltip"
```

Parts: `<Tooltip.Root>`, `<Tooltip.Trigger>`, `<Tooltip.Portal>`, `<Tooltip.Positioner>`, `<Tooltip.Popup>`, `<Tooltip.Arrow>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Tooltip.Root>
  <Tooltip.Trigger>
  <Tooltip.Portal>
    <Tooltip.Positioner>
      <Tooltip.Popup>
        <Tooltip.Arrow>
```

Props of its root:

- `open?: boolean`: `v-model:open`. Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether it starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `delay?: number`: How long the pointer rests on the trigger before the popup opens, in milliseconds. Default `600`.
- `closeDelay?: number`: How long after the pointer leaves the popup closes, in milliseconds. Default `0`.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: the pointer and focus do not open it.
